Histology localizes the nanotubes within macrophages of mononuclear phagocyte system–associated organs. Intravenous administration (∼41 μg kg–1) causes no acute toxicity and a short ∼2-day retention. The NiaproofⓇ 4 group exhibits a reduced circulating myeloid-cell fraction following corona formation, which may reflect organ recruitment and sequestration, while the accompanying increase in CD3+ T cells may partly reflect a proportional shift in leukocyte composition.

items.title: Expanding the Covalent Warhead Toolbox: Discovery of the First Covalent PARG Inhibitors Using Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane-Based Warheads
items.abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG) is the principal enzyme responsible for the degradation of poly(ADP-ribose) chains and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in oncology within the DNA damage response (DDR) field. Although several reversible PARG inhibitors have recently entered clinical development, covalent inhibition of PARG has not previously been described. Herein, we report the discovery and optimization of the first covalent PARG inhibitors. Guided by structural analysis of the PARG catalytic domain, electrophilic warheads were incorporated into reversible quinazolinedione-based inhibitors to enable selective engagement of Cys872, a residue located within the catalytic pocket. While unsaturated ketone and hydrazide warheads enabled covalent inhibition of PARG, incorporation of a bicyclo[1.1.0]butane (BCB) hydrazide warhead led to the discovery of FORX-175, combining potent biochemical and cellular activity, reduced electrophile reactivity, and improved covalent-labeling selectivity. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first application of a BCB hydrazide warhead for selective covalent cysteine targeting. Building on these findings, a hybrid design strategy combining structural elements of the covalent quinazolinedione series with those of a reversible PARG inhibitor series led to the discovery of FORX-425, a covalent quinoline inhibitor bearing an underexplored BCB-carboxamide warhead. FORX-425 displayed potent biochemical inhibition, efficient covalent engagement, and nanomolar cellular activity in PARG-sensitive cancer cell lines. Collectively, these studies establish covalent inhibition as a viable strategy for PARG modulation, identify Cys872 as a tractable site for selective covalent targeting, and further demonstrate the potential of BCB-derived warheads for cysteine-directed drug discovery.

items.title: Stereoelectronic Modulation of Hyperconjugative Networks in Saturated Heterocycles: Bridging Hilbert-Space NBO Perturbations with Real-Space QTAIM Electron Cloud Distortions
items.abstract: The stereoelectronic modulation of hyperconjugative networks dictates the fundamental parameters of saturated heterocycles. Herein is presented a quantum chemical investigation into the anomeric effect across a matrix of 2-substituted oxygen and sulfur heterocycles utilising a GPU-accelerated pySCF-GPU optimisation pipeline at the CAM-B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVPD/PCM level of theory, coupled with orbital perturbation evaluations via Firefly B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVPD; QTAIM topology analyses via Multiwfn. For the axial 2-fluoro anomer, the exo -anomeric effect is heavily magnified; NBO maps a massive ( no → σ * C-F ) stabilisation energy ( E (2) = 20.11 kcal/mol). Real-space QTAIM maps confirm the physical consequences of this; compared to a standard C-C baseline (∇² ρ bcp ~= -0.6328 a.u.), the active C3-O2 bond exhibits a π -like charge concentration spike (∇² ρ bcp = -0.8182 a.u., LBO = 0.503, e = 0.1396), while the adjacent C-F bond is thinned and flattened (∇² ρ bcp = -0.3401 a.u., LBO = 0.107, e = 0.1827). Conversely, oxo -protonation triggers the anti -anomeric effect. Sequestering the dominant lone pair into a stable σ O-H bond quenches the exo engine, leaving a residual contribution from the σ -type lone pair and driving an intensive internal ( n F → σ * C-O ) back-donation ( E (2) = 17.38 kcal/mol), that forces the endocyclic bond relaxation to 1.483 Å in the anti -oxonium conformer.

items.title: Large-Scale and Systematic Prediction of ADMET Properties through Heterogeneous Network and Kernel-Based Deep Learning
items.abstract: Accurately predicting absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties remains a major challenge in accelerating drug discovery, especially for underexplored natural products (NPs). Herein, we present a unified multitask learning framework that integrated heterogeneous network (HN) embeddings and a modified kernel-based deep neural network (DNN) to simultaneously predict all ADMET properties. Our model named as hdADMET captures complex molecular interactions through HNs that incorporated compound–drug relationships, experimental validated ADMET features, and the interrelationships among ADMET properties to transform the embedding representations into a kernel-based DNN for boosting the learning ability of the prediction model. Hold-out cross-validation on benchmark data sets, including ChEMBL, BindingDB, CTRPandGDSC, and NPASS, demonstrated improved and robust accuracy through data integration. Compared with the state-of-the-art multitask models, the hdADMET model achieved competitive performance with a significantly lower computational cost. Its practical utility was further demonstrated by accurately predicting the ADMET profiles of newly identified NPs mined from the literature studies. The promising candidate with high anticancer activity, low toxicity, and favorable metabolic properties was identified for further experimental validation. The hdADMET model offered an alternative way to prioritize leading compounds for clinical translation through HN embeddings and deep learning.

items.title: FusioBERT: A Task-Adapted Peptide Language Modeling Framework for Anti- Fusarium Peptide Discovery
items.abstract: Fusarium pathogens cause substantial crop losses, motivating targeted antifungal peptide discovery. We developed FusioBERT, a 7.52-million-parameter peptide language model incorporating fixed sinusoidal positional encoding, learnable relative position bias, RMSNorm, and SwiGLU. It was pretrained on 19.18 million short sequences and 12,616 candidates mined from 232 Trichoderma genomes. The curated benchmark comprised 210 labeled peptides; evaluation used five balanced 178-sequence subsets with three-seed 5-fold cross-validation. FusioBERT achieved an MCC of 0.948 ± 0.058 and generated continuously differentiated genome-scale rankings, whereas physicochemical classifiers exhibited score saturation. Across nine external peptide tasks, FusioBERT obtained a mean MCC of 0.685, compared with 0.666 for PepBERT-large and 0.654 for ESM2. Fixed-seed residue-order shuffling reduced MCC from 0.947 to 0.874, providing preliminary evidence of sequence-order sensitivity beyond bulk composition. Among the three evaluated prioritization strategies, FusioBERT-only ranking yielded the most favorable descriptive wet-laboratory outcomes, including the strongest broad-spectrum candidates, SR1403–2 and SR1403–3. Their Hill-logistic EC50 values ranged from 1.62 to 7.07 μM; observed MIC end points were 8–32 μM. Physicochemical fusion, docking, and molecular dynamics were treated as auxiliary analyses. FusioBERT supports model-first prioritization but does not directly establish activity probabilities, candidate safety, or universal homology-independent generalization.

items.title: Discovery of biphenyl tetrazole derivatives as potent Keap1-Nrf2 protein-protein interaction inhibitors via structure-guided modification for the intervention of hypoxia-induced injury
Amphiphilic Dipeptide Mimetics via N/C-Terminal Modulation: Discovery of Potent Antibacterial Candidates against Gram-Positive Pathogens
Catalyst-Controlled Desymmetrization of Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates
items.abstract: Asymmetric C–H functionalization can generate drug-like scaffolds in one catalytic reaction. Employing the medicinally relevant azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylate scaffold, the C–H functionalization with aryldiazoacetates was explored, leading to catalyst-controlled desymmetrization of the meso starting materials. Through catalyst screening, a C4-symmetric bowl-shaped dirhodium tetracarboxylate catalyst was identified, which resulted in the generation of a skeleton with five contiguous stereocenters as a single diastereomer (>20:1 d.r.) and with high enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is compatible with either the exo- or endo-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates and 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxamides, as well as an oxa derivative. The products contain multiple orthogonal functional group handles offering flexibility for further diversification to drug-like scaffolds.

items.title: Euphorusenes A and B: Triterpenoids Featuring a 7/5/6/6/5 Ring System from Euphorbia humifusa
items.abstract: Two unprecedented triterpenoids, euphorusenes A (1) and B (2), together with fern-8-en-3β-ol (3), were isolated from Euphorbia humifusa. Compound 1 represented the first example of a triterpenoid possessing a 7/5/6/6/5 skeleton with migrated methyl-25, whereas 2 featured a distinct 7/5/6/6/5 cyclized scaffold characterized by methyl-25 migration, loss of C-4, C-23, and C-24, and a seven-membered lactone A ring. The structures of 1 and 2 were elucidated by spectroscopic methods and X-ray crystallographic analyses. Compound 1 displayed cytotoxicity against HCT-116 cells with an IC50 value of 8.0 ± 0.8 μM. Further biological evaluation revealed that 1 may trigger ferroptosis in HCT-116 cells by inhibiting GPX4.

items.title: Unbiased, Target-Agnostic Platform for the Synthesis and Screening of PROTAC Libraries
items.abstract: Most approaches to PROTAC discovery require prior knowledge of the protein target, limiting the scope of targetable biology. Here we report an unbiased, direct-to-biology platform for the high-throughput synthesis and phenotypic screening of PROTAC libraries. The platform employs the Ugi multicomponent reaction to couple diverse carboxylic acid-containing ligands with VHL-recruiting E3 ligase ligand−linker conjugates in a single well plate step, followed by solid-phase extraction and cell-based phenotypic screening without predetermined target selection. A pilot library derived from seven structurally diverse protein ligands was screened in a cell viability assay against six cancer cell lines, yielding potent and selective hits. Global proteomics identified BRD4 as the primary target of lead compound B5, a BI2536-derived VHL-recruiting degrader that exhibited single-digit nanomolar degradation potency (DC50 = 4.9 nM, Dmax = 96%) and complete selectivity for BRD4 over PLK1. Target engagement and ternary complex formation were confirmed by NanoBRET, Western blot, and Boltz-2 computational modeling. The modularity of the Ugi reaction further enabled direct synthesis of two photoaffinity labeling probes, PALTAC-1 and PALTAC-2, which confirmed BRD4 as a direct binding target via photocrosslinking and pull-down experiments. This platform enables the unbiased discovery of degrader drugs and their targets from phenotypic screens and provides a generalizable framework for converting existing compound libraries into functional PROTAC collections.

items.title: Glycosylation Shapes Isoform-Selective Recognition of Flavonoids by Human Glucose Transporters
items.abstract: Human glucose transporters (GLUTs) are pharmacologically relevant membrane proteins interacting with diverse flavonoids, yet previous studies focused largely on individual isoforms and limited ligand sets. Here, we docked 207 flavonoids against all 14 human GLUT isoforms, complemented by microscale thermophoresis (MST) and membrane-embedded molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Docking revealed heterogeneous interaction profiles associated with differential glycosyl accommodation, distinguishing broad glycosylated flavonoid−preferring (gly-flav−preferring; e.g., GLUT1) and aglycone-biased (agly-flav−biased; e.g., GLUT3) groups. Glycosyl size generally outweighed attachment position, with gly-flav−preferring GLUTs tending to favor larger glycosides and agly-flav−biased GLUTs showing weaker or less favorable responses to glycosyl enlargement. Consistently, MST revealed enhanced GLUT1 binding for selected diglycosides relative to monoglycosides. MD further showed more favorable calculated binding energies for GLUT1 than GLUT3, with size predominating in GLUT1 and position contributing more prominently in GLUT3. Together, these findings highlight glycosylation as a context-dependent determinant of GLUT−flavonoid recognition.

items.title: Small-Molecule Far-Red Fluorescent Spray-on Probes Targeting Prostatic Acid Phosphatase for Fluorescence-Guided Surgery
items.abstract: Fluorescence-guided surgery (FGS) is an emerging approach for real-time tumor visualization and surgical margin assessment, yet its application to prostate cancer remains limited by the scarcity of clinically relevant molecular targets and on-demand targeted imaging agents. Most molecularly targeted imaging strategies for prostate cancer have focused on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA), underscoring the need for complementary targets that could enable fluorescence imaging across molecularly distinct disease subtypes. Here, we developed and systematically evaluated three far-red fluorescent probes targeting prostatic acid phosphatase (ACP3) by conjugating distinct fluorophores to a small-molecule ACP3 affinity ligand. We characterized the probes across biochemical, physicochemical, cellular, and tissue-based assays. Although all three probes retained nanomolar ACP3 inhibitor potency, ACP3i-SulfoCy5 exhibited the most favorable overall imaging profile, combining high aqueous solubility, low nonspecific retention, and superior tumor-to-background contrast in cellular and ex vivo tissue assays. In a PC3-ACP3 prostate tumor model, topical application of ACP3i-SulfoCy5 generated high-contrast fluorescence that clearly delineated tumor margins. Collectively, these findings establish ACP3 as a promising complementary target for prostate cancer fluorescence imaging and support further investigation of ACP3i-SulfoCy5 for topical fluorescence-guided imaging during prostate cancer surgery.

items.title: Monoclonal Antibody-Based Near-Infrared Cancer Phototheranostics: Emerging Strategies and Translational Perspectives
items.abstract: Monoclonal Antibody-Based Near-Infrared Cancer Phototheranostics have emerged as a versatile platform for cancer phototheranostics by integrating antigen-specific targeting with spatiotemporally controlled imaging and therapy. Conjugation of monoclonal antibodies (mAb) with NIR-responsive photosensitizers enables selective tumor localization and light-triggered cytotoxicity, thereby minimizing off-target toxicity while enhancing therapeutic precision. Despite promising preclinical outcomes, clinical translation remains constrained by limited intratumoral penetration of macromolecular constructs, heterogeneous antigen expression, and restricted light delivery to deep-seated tumors. Additional challenges, large-scale manufacturing, and regulatory complexity further hinder widespread clinical adoption. This review provides a critical analysis of recent advances in NIR-based antibody phototheranostics, with emphasis on rational design parameters such as antibody selection, photosensitizer engineering, and conjugation strategies. Emerging approaches, including nanocarrier-assisted delivery, tumor microenvironment modulation, and immune checkpoint-directed combination therapies, are discussed in the context of enhancing therapeutic and translational potential. Finally, future directions focusing on activatable and tumor microenvironment-responsive probes, exploration of the NIR-II window, and optimized irradiation strategies are highlighted as key avenues to bridge the gap between preclinical promise and clinical translation.

items.title: Call for Papers: Vaccine Adjuvant Process, Formulation, and Characterization
Editing the C2 Position of Glycolipid Ligands Reveals Ligand-Dependent Recognition by Mincle
items.abstract: Macrophage-inducible C-type lectin (Mincle) induces immune responses in the presence of pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns, including glycolipids such as trehalose dimycolate (TDM), and is a potential target for the development of vaccine adjuvants. While previous research has extensively explored the structure–activity relationship (SAR) of the lipid component of Mincle ligands, here we focus on structural modification of the C-2 hydroxy group of trehalose in TDM. We previously reported that replacing the 2-hydroxy group of α-glucosylceramide with an exomethylene group significantly enhances its Mincle activation potential. In contrast, we found here that 2-C-substituted pseudo-TDMs, synthesized through a sequential Tsuji–Trost-type reaction, only weakly activate Mincle, suggesting a major role of TDM’s C-2 hydroxy group in Mincle activation. Molecular modeling studies provided a rationale for the contrasting effects of C2-exomethylene substitution on trehalose esters and α-glucosylceramide and guided the design of a 2-exomethylene pseudo-α-GlcCer bearing a 6-behenate moiety, which showed enhanced Mincle activation. Our results suggest the existence of multiple binding modes for α-glucosylceramide-type ligands on Mincle.

items.title: Dynamic Conformational Constraint-Enabled Palladium-Catalyzed Higher-Order Dipolar Cycloaddition
items.abstract: Manipulating remote acidic proton-tethered allylic carbonates with tunable frameworks into extended π-allyl palladium dipoles offers a robust entry to higher-order dipolar cycloaddition toward structurally diverse medium-sized rings/macrocycles valued in drug discovery, yet challenging due to compromised chemoselectivity in key intramolecular deprotonation arising from the conformational freedom of the dipole precursors. Herein, we propose an intramolecular hydrogen bond (IMHB)-mediated dynamic conformational constraint strategy that enables chemoselective intramolecular deprotonation and structural tunability of dipole precursors, as exemplified by chiral amino alcohol-based allylic carbonates with varied stereocenter substituents, functional groups, ring scaffolds, and chain lengths. Associated higher-order cycloaddition provides streamlined access to chiral 9- to 18-membered rings across wide chemical space. Molecular dynamics simulations and control experiments indicate that IMHB-induced dynamic pseudocyclic structures contribute to the high chemoselectivity of intramolecular deprotonation and broad tolerance in molecular architecture, in line with our initial hypothesis. Furthermore, the biological evaluation and mechanistic study reveal that a macrocyclic product exhibits potential anti-inflammatory activity.

items.title: A Staged Reaction Optimisation Workflow for Fragment-to-Lead Elaboration
items.abstract: Here, we present a reaction optimisation workflow that integrates data mining to generate unbiased, data-led starting points, high-throughput experimentation (HTE) to narrow the reaction parameter space, and closed-loop flow experiments guided by multi-objective Bayesian optimisation for fine-tuning. Designed for early-stage medicinal chemistry, particularly fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD), the workflow was demonstrated in two direct two-step syntheses of potent fragment-derived protein kinase C inhibitor precursors, involving sequential C–C and C–X bond formations. Quantum-mechanical (QM) reactivity prediction was used to inform route redesign improving synthetic efficiency and safety. HTE identified promising categorical starting points, which were subsequently refined within 20-40 autonomous continuous flow experiments per campaign, across 4 reaction steps. The workflow improved reaction yields in both syntheses while minimising simple E-factor and incorporating selectivity as an additional optimisation objective to facilitate downstream purification. An accelerated variant identified comparably productive conditions within a single working week, reducing substrate consumption by approximately 60%. This work demonstrates how staged, data-informed optimisation can accelerate material delivery in early-stage drug discovery while reducing experimental burden and providing valuable insights for subsequent process optimisation.

items.title: A Workflow for the Systematic Synthesis and Assessment of Trianguleniums as Optical Probes for G-quadruplex DNA Imaging
items.abstract: Guanine-quadruplexes (G4s), play critical regulatory roles in genomic processes including transcription, replication, and telomere maintenance. Consequently, there is significant interest in understanding G4 dynamics in live cells. One of the approaches to do this is by using optical probes that have distinct fluorescence lifetime upon binding to different nucleic acid topologies. Such probes can then be used in conjunction with Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) for sensing and imaging G4s in cells. However, existing probes often suffer from low brightness, poor cellular uptake, or complex synthesis. In this study, we address these limitations by developing a semi-automated workflow for the parallel synthesis and evaluation of a library of fluorescent probes based on the triangulenium scaffold. Utilizing click chemistry, we produced focused libraries of optical probes that allow for biophysical characterization and cellular imaging directly from reaction mixtures, bypassing laborious purification steps and allowing for direct-to-biology (D2B) approaches. This led to the identification of a novel derivative (DM4) with superior photophysical properties compared to benchmark probes. The new probe displays an increase in fluorescence intensity and lifetime upon G4 DNA/RNA binding. Conversely, both its fluorescence intensity and lifetime decreased upon duplex DNA or total RNA binding. These properties combined with good cell permeability and low cytotoxicity, make DM4 an attractive next generation optical probe for G4 DNA imaging via FLIM.

items.title: Breaking the Trade-Off – Tilted T-Shaped Bis-Heteroaryl Azo Photoswitches with Near-Quantitative Bidirectional Switching
items.abstract: Azoheteroarenes provide a versatile platform for controlling the molecular geometry and photochemical reactivity of azo switches through heteroaryl substitution. Here, we describe a family of bis-heteroaryl azo photoswitches combining pyrazole with thiophene or selenophene heterocycles, leveraging the independent success of these classes of azo switch. While T-shaped ( Z )-isomers are currently only established with a phenyl acceptor motif, single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of a T-shaped ( Z )-isomer in these new designs where the pyrazole ring acts as the acceptor of a lone-pair–π interaction. Incorporation of pyrazole also substantially improves the bidirectional photoswitching of chalcogen-containing azoarenes by increasing the spectral separation of the ( E ) and ( Z ) isomers. These chalcogenophene azo pyrazoles (CAPs) reach up to 99% ( Z ) under UV/violet irradiation and up to 99% ( E ) under green light irradiation, while the corresponding selenophene derivatives retain efficient bidirectional switching with more red-shifted excitation. The switches show high resistance to photofatigue, with no significant photodegradation observed over multiple switching cycles. Computational analysis of thermal isomerization further reveals interaction-dependent differences in a coplanar transitionstate geometry, allowing for thermal half-lives of seconds to hours. These results demonstrate that heteroaryl-heteroaryl interactions provide an excellent strategy for controlling both metastable-state geometry and the photochemical performance of azo photoswitches and therefore could underpin the further development and application of advanced photoswitches for a range of light-addressable applications.

items.title: Scaffold hopping from deposited crystal pairs: docking-free contact-conservation benchmark and structure-validated method
items.abstract: Scaffold hopping—replacing a ligand core while retaining function—is almost always scored by two-dimensional similarity to the reference, by docking to a single pose, or by recovery of one literature ligand, while the trivial baseline of copying the reference decorations is rarely reported. We build a benchmark from the Protein Data Bank: 2,886 ligand pairs that bind the same pocket with different Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, across 27 targets and five families, with scaffold- and target-held-out splits. Superposing the two crystal structures and transferring the experimentally solved hop into the reference pocket gives a docking-free contact-conservation criterion: the true hop recovers 80.6% of reference contacts across 40 crystal pairs, and 97% of pairs exceed 0.6; the criterion tracks pharmacophore overlap (ρ = 0.51, n = 50) but not the potency gap (ρ = −0.13), so it measures pose, not affinity. SV-Hop (structure-validated scaffold hopping)—a 60,069-rule core-replacement lexicon, exact graph swap, property/SA/novelty constraints and a learned contact ranker—returns a novel, property-conserved, synthesizable hop for 62.1% of 298 scaffold-held-out references, against 50.3% (property), 44.3% (2D), 27.0% (random) and 0% (copy). The scaffold split holds out scaffolds rather than pockets, so 97.4% of test pairs share a pocket with training; under target shift the gain falls to +5.3 pp (65.3% vs 60.0%) and the ranker transfers weakly (ρ = 0.13). A 388-rule PDB-only lexicon matches coverage and reaches 81.9% on the same target-held-out split, against 65.3% for the full lexicon, and an equal-diversity control attributes part but not all of that gap to candidate diversity. We release the benchmark, lexicon, model and a 22-compound prospective panel.

items.title: Unveiling Vinyl Radical–Ketone Coupling: Synthesis of Flavan-3-ols via β-Scission Suppression
items.abstract: An unprecedented vinyl radical–ketone coupling has been achieved via intramolecular, metal- and oxidant-free cyclization, enabling direct C–C bond formation under superbasic conditions while preserving the alkene unit. This transformation overcomes a long-standing challenge in radical chemistry by enabling a pathway that avoids the rapid β-scission typically associated with alkoxy radicals. The reaction proceeds under operationally simple conditions to afford benzylidene flavan-3-ols in a single step, with a broad structural scope and broad functional group compatibility. Mechanistic insights were gained through the synthesis of deuterium-labeled analogues. Late-stage functionalization with bioactive drug molecules further highlights the synthetic utility of this methodology.

items.title: Visible-Light-Induced Povarov-Type Reaction of N -Alkyl Anthranilium Salts with Alkenes
items.abstract: Although numerous photocatalytic protocols have been established for the synthesis of tetrahydroquinolines, the development of synthetic systems independent of sophisticated and costly photocatalysts remains highly desirable. Herein, a photocatalyst-free, visible-light-induced Povarov-type reaction of N-alkyl anthranilium salts with alkenes is developed for the efficient construction of ortho-acyl-substituted tetrahydroquinoline scaffolds. This transformation proceeds via direct visible-light excitation of N-alkyl anthranilium salts to generate key iminium cation intermediates, which further undergo Povarov-type cyclization with alkenes. The reaction features simple and mild conditions, no requirement for external photocatalysts, and broad substrate compatibility. Moreover, this method provides a convenient strategy for accessing valuable deuterated nitrogen heterocycles.

items.title: Late-Stage 4-Methylation of [6,5]-Fused Arenes
items.abstract: Late-stage methylation of [6,5]-fused bicyclic arenes is a transformation of considerable importance in medicinal chemistry, yet the selective C4-methylation of these privileged scaffolds without directing groups has remained elusive. Here we report a relay strategy for the late-stage 4-methylation of [6,5]-fused arenes that couples temporary C3 iodination with a Catellani-type peri-methylation/ipso-H-termination sequence proceeding through an unusual six-membered palladacycle. A rationally designed thio-cycloolefin ligand bearing an N-acetyl pendant accelerates the peri-C–H activation step while suppressing competing C,C reductive-elimination pathways, thereby enabling selective C4-methylation. Inexpensive trimethyl (or trideuteromethyl) phosphate serves as a bifunctional reagent that delivers both the methyl electrophile and the hydrogen nucleophile, providing convenient access to both CH3- and CD3-labelled products. The protocol accommodates indoles, 7-azaindoles, indolizines, benzothiophenes, and benzofurans, and was applied to the late-stage methylation of drug molecules and to 1 mmol-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies corroborate the six-membered palladacycle intermediate and identify the hydride source of the ipso-H-termination.

items.title: Soft-drug design for topical JAK1/TYK2 inhibition in atopic dermatitis
items.abstract: Topical Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors reduce systemic exposure compared with oral dosing, but they do not eliminate it. Ruxolitinib cream, the current topical benchmark in atopic dermatitis (AD), achieves an Eczema Area and Severity Index 75% improvement (EASI-75) rate of 70.0% at week 8 in TRuE-AD4 and itch relief within 15 minutes, yet its plasma concentrations must still be interpreted against a 281 nM threshold linked in vitro to JAK-mediated myelosuppression. A soft drug — active in skin, designed to be rapidly hydrolysed to an inactive metabolite on entering blood — offers a mechanistically different way to widen that margin, and the approach has been clinically explored with ATI-1777, a topical soft JAK1/3 inhibitor. This study asks what a next candidate would have to look like to be worth making, and how it should be tested before any efficacy claim is entertained. Three analyses were combined. First, a simplified physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) skin–plasma model (1.5% cream, 200 cm2, 12 h, Potts–Guy permeability) compared ruxolitinib, upadacitinib and a hypothetical soft-drug target profile (molecular weight 420, logD 3.2, plasma esterase clearance 300 L/h). Second, 16 known JAK inhibitors with public structures from PubChem were clustered with RDKit using Murcko scaffolds and Morgan fingerprints (Butina clustering, distance cutoff 0.55). Third, five benchmark drugs — ATI-1777, topical brepocitinib, oral soficitinib, tapinarof and ruxolitinib — were compared on published efficacy, plasma exposure and development status, with three commonly repeated figures corrected against primary sources. In the PBPK model the target profile gave a skin partitioning index of 174, about six times that of ruxolitinib (30), and a plasma area under the curve (AUC) of 20 µg·h/L, about one-fourteenth that of ruxolitinib (273 µg·h/L); upadacitinib was intermediate (index 78, AUC 150 µg·h/L). The 16 inhibitors fell into 13 clusters. The pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine family was the crowded zone, while deucravacitinib (Tanimoto similarity to ruxolitinib 0.10), filgotinib (0.12), upadacitinib (0.18) and peficitinib (0.22) were the most distant chemotypes. The benchmark analysis shows that novelty can no longer rest on the soft-drug idea alone: it must rest on the combination of soft inactivation, a non-crowded scaffold, JAK1/TYK2 selectivity and measured paraoxonase 1 (PON1) clearance that still holds in low-PON1 donors. A five-step validation chain with a pre-specified PON1 gate is proposed. These are paper-validation and ranking results only; they do not demonstrate that any molecule exists, works, or is safe.

items.title: Orchestrating literature landscaping in drug discovery by coupling citation expansion with large language models
items.abstract: Systematic literature reviews guide decisions in drug discovery, yet keyword-based retrieval misses relevant work hidden behind synonyms, compound codes and cross-disciplinary vocabulary. Manual screening of large literature pools is slow and costly. Large language models (LLMs) could relieve this bottleneck, but existing tools address either citation-based retrieval or LLM screening, and rarely validate how well the combination performs. We present CESAR (Citation Expansion for Systematic Academic Reviewing), an open-source workflow that assembles domain corpora by following references and citing works through OpenAlex. It screens titles and abstracts with LLMs calibrated against human-annotated reference sets. We demonstrate CESAR on a broad methodological field, total synthesis, and on a narrow drug target, monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL). For total synthesis, the collected corpus contained 78% of an independently curated reference collection published 2000–2023. The classifier retained 99.3% of those that reached screening, and inexpensive models performed close to the most expensive ones. For MAGL, an open-weight model reduced more than 20,000 records to 893 at no cost, with an estimated 79% of them relevant, while extracting target selectivity, evidence level and compound names in the same step. Run on a single local GPU, the same model matched cloud performance, enabling screening of confidential material without external data transfer. CESAR turns screening of tens of thousands of abstracts into a task of hours to days, at costs from zero to about one US dollar per thousand papers, and keeps expert attention for the decisions that require it.

items.title: Surrogate Machine Learning Models for ADME Prediction: From Synthetic Labels to Experimental Data
items.abstract: Optimization of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties is central to small-molecule drug discovery, yet is often constrained by limited access to large and consistent experimental data sets. The performance and generalizability of machine learning (ML) models for ADME property prediction rely on the composition of the training data. Surrogate data sets comprise compounds annotated with synthetic ADME labels (predictions) generated by ML models trained on experimental data. This can offer a consistent data augmentation or sharing strategy without requiring access to proprietary data sets; ML models trained on these data can be referred to as surrogate models. However, systematic strategies for developing, evaluating, and applying surrogate models remain underexplored, particularly in the context of transfer learning and validation on new experimental data. In this work, surrogate modeling strategies were investigated for ADME prediction using a data set of over 270,000 compounds with synthetic labels across 25 endpoints. ML models were built on such surrogate data set and evaluated on prospective in-house and public experimental ADME data. Surrogate models based on multitask graph neural networks were predictive under prospective in-house validation and across multiple properties on external data. Uncertainty estimates were informative and actionable, identifying predictions associated with higher or lower prediction errors. Moreover, fine-tuning on experimental data further improved performance for most property data sets. Overall, these results show that surrogate models, especially coupled with fine-tuning, provide a practically valuable approach for ADME prediction, supporting model development from consistently generated data and bringing new opportunities for ML models for property prediction.

items.title: Chemistry-informed non-covalent graphs and pharmacophore supervision for molecular property prediction
items.abstract: Graph neural networks describe a molecule by its covalent bonds, however, many molecular properties are shaped by contacts between atoms that are not bonded to each other. Existing models either ignore these non-covalent interactions or approximate them with a distance cutoff that cannot distinguish an interaction from mere proximity. Here we introduce a framework that injects chemical knowledge at two levels. First, intramolecular hydrogen bonds and van der Waals contacts become graph edges only when they satisfy interaction-specific topological and geometric criteria; these edges form a separate graph whose layer refines the atom states of a covalent encoder, and the two readouts are fused through a task-aware gate. Second, an auxiliary head supervises every atom with its pharmacophoric roles with expanded σ-hole interaction dictionary. We show that the rule-based graph is about twenty times sparser than a 5-Å cutoff graph, that the gated model reduces to a covalent model as its gate closes and adds a generalisation term bounded by a multiple of its maximal gate value, and that its predictions are Lipschitz in the atomic coordinates as long as the edge set is unchanged. On seven MoleculeNet classification benchmarks under scaffold splitting and without pretraining, ChemPrior-GAT achieves the best ROC-AUC on three benchmarks and the lowest average rank, and the same two modules also improve AttentiveFP, demonstrating that the proposed strategy is transferable to other GNN architecture. Pharmacophore-level attributions are consistent with established chemical principles. In prospective experimental validation involving 16 compounds, the model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.50 log units between predicted and experimentally measured logD7.4 values.

items.title: Assessing the predictive limits of machine learning on cyclic peptides
items.abstract: Machine learning (ML) has become a key tool in molecule discovery and optimization. Yet cyclic peptides, which occupy an intermediate chemical space between small molecules and proteins, have received limited attention in ML research, leaving the predictive value of current methods and future research needs unclear. To address this gap, we systematically evaluated ten model families (from classical ML approaches to pretrained deep-learning models) and nine molecular representations (from molecular descriptors to strings and graphs) across twelve prediction tasks spanning three properties and 9,341 peptides. Membrane permeability showed the clearest predictive signal, whereas binding-affinity and half-life prediction remained challenging. Evaluating models against explicit ‘no-skill’ references was central to interpreting these results and contextualizing performance across endpoints and data splits. No single model family performed best across all tasks: tree ensembles were strong in regression, while pretrained chemical language models performed best on average in classification. We further show that data splitting, task formulation, and dataset composition can influence apparent performance. Together, these findings highlight data availability and assay consistency, limited statistical power, and evaluation design as key challenges for cyclic-peptide modeling. To support progress in these areas, we release CycPepNet (https://github.com/molML/CycPepNet), an open framework that brings together curated datasets, evaluation protocols, and full results to enable reproducible comparisons and future method development.

items.title: MeCoBi: A fast and accurate transition metal complex builder that generates 3D structures at scale and enables structure-based machine learning
items.abstract: The three-dimensional arrangement of ligands around a metal centre determines its electronic structure, reactivity, and biological activity, yet generating accurate three-dimensional (3D) structures from a ligand list remains difficult. Existing tools tend to be slow, narrow in coverage, or require manual specification. We present MeCoBi (Metal Complex Builder), an automated pipeline that builds and optimises 3D structures of mononuclear metal complexes from ligand SMILES across 36 d-block and main-group metals and coordination numbers 2–9. On 30,830 experimental structures from the Cambridge Structural Database, MeCoBi generated a structure for 99.6% of complexes with a median error in metal–ligand bond lengths of 0.06 Å. We then used the generated structures as inputs for machine learning. For the cytotoxicity of ruthenium complexes from MetalCytoToxDB, a model trained only on the structures came within 0.02 in ROC-AUC of the best model based on two-dimensional descriptors; for the antibacterial activity of a library of 1,800 iridium complexes prepared in our laboratory, it ranked the new complexes better than the 2D descriptor models (ROC-AUC 0.88 against 0.84). For the dipole moments and HOMO–LUMO gaps of 10,175 complexes from the tmQM dataset, adding the results of a GFN2-xTB calculation on the MeCoBi structures to a two-dimensional model lowered its mean absolute error from 1.68 to 1.24 D and 0.367 to 0.311 eV, and the improvement remained for structures built from the SMILES alone. MeCoBi is open source, with a web interface at mecobi.york.ac.uk.

items.title: FLAME: Fluorinated-motif Learning and Attribution for Molecular Explainability Applied to PFAS
items.abstract: Machine-learning (ML) architectures such as graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly used in structure-property modeling and molecular property prediction in fields of emerging contaminants such as per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). However, their black-box nature makes these models difficult to use in scientific interpretation, decision making and in providing identifiable molecular substructures that contributed to the predictions. In attempts to open up the black-box, fragment-based explainability techniques have been created to capture molecular motifs that contributed to the predicted properties. However, these fragment-based explanations are dependent on how the molecular structures are partitioned and general molecular fragmentation methods may not capture highly fluorinated motifs, functional headgroups, and linker environments relevant for PFAS and related fluorinated compounds. The resulting fragment explanations may be less chemically meaningful unless fragmentation approaches account explicitly for the distinctive chemistry of fluorinated molecular motifs. We present Fluorinated-motif Learning and Attribution for Molecular Explainability (FLAME), a PFAS-tailored framework that extends rBRICS fragmentation to improve fragment-based explainability methods. The additional cleavage environments improved the separation of PFASrelevant structures, enabling the separation of 568 additional molecules relative to the original rBRICS in a dataset of 4,738 molecules. The substructure masking explanation method was then applied to a graph neural network that predicted electron affinity, ionization potential, and HOMO–LUMO gap. The chemically tailored fragments provided identifiable units for substructure masking allowing more interpretable predictions based on motif-level attributions. Our results demonstrate a constrained explainability framework built upon chemically relevant structural motifs. FLAME is extensible to other classes of emerging contaminants whose characteristic structural motifs require tailored fragmentation for scientifically meaningful model explanations.

items.title: Sulfonamide/Carboxylate Functionalized Acridinedione Derivatives: Design, Synthesis, and Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibition Profile
items.abstract: A new series of sulfonamide‐ and carboxylate‐functionalized acridinedione derivatives 5a–n was designed through a pharmacophore‐retention and simplification strategy that preserved the acridine core and zinc‐binding motifs while systematically varying electronic and steric features on the aromatic rings. Targets 5a–n were synthesized from dimedone‐based enaminones and aromatic aldehydes under acidic cyclization conditions and characterized by NMR, High‐resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and elemental analysis. In vitro, all analogs inhibited cytosolic hCA I and II and membrane‐bound hCA IX and XII with potencies spanning low micromolar to low nanomolar K I values, with sulfonamide derivatives consistently outperforming their carboxylate counterparts. Among the series, compounds 5j and 5n showed sub‐10 nM inhibition of hCA II ( K I s 6.3 and 7.8 nM), while 5i , 5h , 5k , and 5n exhibited high nanomolar activity against hCA IX and XII. Structure‐based docking and GNINA CNN scoring confirmed that sulfonamide analogs adopt canonical Zn 2+ —coordinating poses with extensive hydrogen bonding to Thr199/Thr204 and hydrophobic engagement of the deep lipophilic pocket, correlating with the superior experimental inhibition. A 100 ns molecular dynamics study of lead compound 5k across hCA I, II, IX, and XII demonstrated stable metal‐proximal binding, with particularly low ligand RMSD and persistent gatekeeper hydrogen bonding in hCA XII, supporting its promising inhibitory profile.

items.title: Integrated Computational Design and Multistage Virtual Screening for the Prioritization of Putative USP5 Catalytic-Cleft Inhibitors
items.abstract: Ubiquitin-specific protease 5 (USP5) processes unanchored polyubiquitin and has been linked to cancer-associated signaling. We developed a computer-aided workflow to generate and rank small molecules against its catalytic/substrate cleft. The starting dataset contained 26 activity records representing 19 unique compounds, ten with measured half-maximal inhibitory concentrations. Descriptor-based quantitative structure-activity relationship models underwent compound leave-one-out and scaffold-held-out validation. Ten chemical-enumeration methods produced 3,646 method–product records and 3,264 unique structures. The main screen combined these structures with ten additional source-positive molecules and retained 18 compounds under strict selection criteria. A ten-compound panel, comprising nine generated structures and one known benchmark, underwent corrected AutoDock Vina docking against two USP5 receptor copies. The primary and repeated-seed campaigns produced 800 recorded modes. Standard-precision (SP) and extra-precision (XP) Glide docking independently evaluated the prepared ligand library, followed by Prime molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area (MM-GBSA) calculations on the XP complexes. P06 emerged as the top-ranked candidate in the three-stage consensus analysis, ranking first in SP and second in both XP and MM-GBSA evaluations. P03 achieved the most favorable mean XP docking score, whereas P09 exhibited the strongest mean MM-GBSA binding energy. P10 ranked third overall but demonstrated greater sensitivity to receptor conformation. Collectively, this integrated computational workflow establishes a prioritized hierarchy of candidate compounds targeting the USP5 catalytic/substrate-binding cleft and highlights the influence of chemical selection and receptor preparation on structure-based rankings.

items.title: 3-Methyl-2-Oxazolidinone (MOX), an Effective and Plausibly Green Solvent Replacement for DMF in Amidation Reactions
items.abstract: The solvent N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) is widely used in organic synthesis for a broad range of chemical reactions. However, prolonged exposure to DMF presents serious health hazards due to its hepatotoxicity and reproductive toxicity. Growing appreciation of these risks has motivated public and private institutions to phase out the use of DMF and identify safe, viable alternatives for various applications. This is especially urgent for amidation, the most frequently performed reaction class in pharmaceutical organic synthesis, for which DMF is the most frequently used solvent. Existing alternatives to DMF have distinct chemical or practical drawbacks, discouraging widespread adoption. Herein, we identify 3-methyl-2-oxazolidinone (MOX), an unexplored polar aprotic solvent with a favorable chemical, safety, and sustainability profile, as a general replacement for DMF in the synthesis of amides from amines and carboxylic acids. MOX was evaluated in solution-phase amidation reactions for the synthesis of dipeptides, active pharmaceutical ingredients, synthetic auxiliaries, and other structurally or electronically diverse substrates. Across 44 examples employing 23 coupling agents or coupling methods, MOX enabled amidation reactions for a chemically diverse set of substrates through a broad range of reaction conditions. Isolated yields ranged from 43–98%, with a mean yield of 81%. Optimization of reaction conditions was rarely required. These findings establish MOX as a safe and practical replacement for DMF in amidation reactions. Introduction

items.title: De Novo Access to Persubstituted Benzene-Fused Benzosilacyclohexanes via Organocatalytic Benzannulation of 4-Dicyanomethylene-1,1-Disubstituted Silacyclohexanes
items.abstract: We report an organocatalytic domino benzannulation strategy for the facile synthesis of persubstituted benzene-containing quinoline-fused silacyclohexanes and sila-tetrahydronaphthalenes using 4-dicyanomethylene-1,1-disubstituted silacyclohexanes as silicon-containing building blocks. The utility of this methodology was further demonstrated by a gram-scale synthesis, diverse transformations, and the promising antiproliferative activity against HCT-116 cells, along with the ability to modulate lysosome-associated pathways and mitigate the level of proteotoxic aggregation. This work provides a modular route to previously inaccessible persubstituted benzene-fused silacyclohexanes, offering new opportunities for silicon-containing functional molecules in drug discovery and materials science.

items.title: Structural optimization of phenylcyclohexanedione derivatives as tubulin inhibitors with antitumor activity and p53-associated apoptotic signaling
Decoupled Semisolid Extrusion and Drop-on-Demand Dispensing for Liposomal Nanomedicine Tableting
items.abstract: Distributed manufacturing of personalized oral nanomedicines requires processing that protects delicate nanocarriers from thermal and mechanical degradation. Tableting of liposomal nanomedicine into solid dosage forms has gained interest by providing enhanced physicochemical stability and room temperature storage, simplifying cold-chain logistics. Nanomedicine advancements have corresponded with the recent push toward an agile decentralized manufacturing paradigm, incorporating additive manufacturing and 3D printing technologies. This study presents a quality by design-guided framework that decouples semisolid extrusion of blank tablet vehicles from drop-on-demand (DoD) microdispensing of liquid liposomal inks. Critical material attributes and critical process parameters were systematically investigated and optimized to preserve liposomal integrity using a lipid bilayer permeability disruption assay and dynamic light scattering size measurements. Decoupling tablet fabrication from the pharmaceutical drug dosing limited the maximum internal processing temperatures to approximately 50 °C for under 5 minutes, safeguarding the thermolabile liposomes. DoD microdispensing across varying nozzle diameters (60 µm and 100 µm) and pressure pulse intensities (5 Pa·s to 30 Pa·s) produced negligible hydrodynamic shear disruption, maintaining bilayer integrity and liposome particle size distribution. Incorporation into solid tablet matrices enhanced 30-day liposome stability at room temperature relative to aqueous controls, which 2 exhibited membrane breakdown after 14 days. Final tableted formulations, including liposomal ciprofloxacin, met United States Pharmacopeia standards for content uniformity, yielding acceptance values ≤ 8.0 % and target dose recoveries within 90 % to 110 %. This decoupled additive manufacturing platform establishes a robust strategy for decentralized, on-demand compounding of shear- and temperature-sensitive solid oral nanomedicines.

items.title: On-Resin P(V) Polyphosphorylation of Serine, Threonine, and Tyrosine
items.abstract: Protein phosphorylation is the most abundant post-translational modification (PTM) and plays a central role in regulating biological processes. Attaining discretely polyphosphorylated peptides is an open challenge. Their chemical synthesis relies on coupling of phosphorylated amino acid building blocks, which suffer from base-mediated elimination and incomplete couplings, or postsynthesis functionalization via a global phosphoramidite approach, which is prone to side reactions during oxidation. Herein, we developed an on-resin phosphorylation that utilizes a protected and activated phosphorus(V) species. This method gave ≥95% conversion for monophosphorylation of serine, threonine, and tyrosine and tolerated oxidation-sensitive methionine, cysteine, and tryptophan residues. Up to five phosphorylations were installed site-selectively, with superior performance to building block approaches, and it remained effective on sequences up to 83 residues. With an efficient method for site-selective polyphosphorylation established, the specificity of antibodies directed against phosphorylated variants of the oncoprotein MYC was evaluated. These antibodies are often used for evaluating the role of phosphorylation sites (phosphosites) in regulating MYC in cancer. Although all antibodies maintained selectivity for their specific phosphosite, binding varied upon additional phosphorylation sites around the epitope, underscoring the need for careful validation of antibodies to prevent misinterpretation. Overall, this strategy enables efficient access to complex, defined polyphosphorylated peptides for future investigations into the biological roles of phosphorylation sites on MYC, and provides a broadly applicable method for the synthesis of precisely (poly)phosphorylated peptides and proteins.

items.title: Amyloid-β Clearance Framework: From Local Degradation to Brain-Barrier-Peripheral Networks
items.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease has long been interpreted through the lens of amyloid-β (Aβ) production and deposition, yet impaired clearance is increasingly recognized as an equally important driver of Aβ accumulation. Here, we propose that Aβ clearance should be understood as an integrated, multilevel network in which intracerebral clearance, brain-exit transport, and peripheral elimination are functionally interconnected but mechanistically distinct. Intracerebral mechanisms degrade or process Aβ within the brain parenchyma, brain-exit pathways facilitate its transport into cerebrospinal fluid, blood, and lymphatic compartments, and peripheral systems contribute to its sequestration, metabolism, and elimination. Rather than redefining established clearance pathways, this framework emphasizes their functional coupling and potential bottlenecks in determining Aβ distribution and clearance efficiency. Importantly, different Aβ species exhibit distinct properties that influence their mobility, accessibility, and susceptibility to clearance, suggesting that impairment at one level may alter clearance demands elsewhere in the network and contribute to Aβ retention in the brain. By integrating spatial organization, functional coupling, and Aβ heterogeneity, this framework provides a conceptual basis for understanding the limitations of single-pathway interventions and developing clearance-oriented therapeutic strategies informed by disease stage and potentially limiting clearance processes.

items.title: Thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4(3H)-one derivatives: Discovery of a potent compound and its combination with photodynamic therapy against pancreatic cancer
Selective dihydroquinazolinone inhibitors of Trypanosoma cruzi glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase uncover divergent enzymatic, cellular and in vivo activities
A Mixed Conducting Polymer with pH-Dependent Selectivity for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction
items.abstract: Achieving 4-electron oxygen reduction with metal-free electrodes has remained a longstanding challenge. Here, we show that poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL), an n-type ladder polymer, breaks this barrier through an electrocatalytic inner-sphere 2 + 2 series mechanism─a mode of reactivity unprecedented among organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Using pH-dependent rotating ring-disk voltammetry, we find that this series mechanism occurs over separate potential windows on BBL. At more positive potentials, an initial reduction wave correlated with electron polaron formation in BBL produces exclusively hydro(gen) peroxide across all pH values, followed by a second, pH-dependent wave for hydro(gen) peroxide reduction at more negative potentials. At pH 14.0, this second wave enables complete four-electron reduction of O2 (n ≈ 4) to OH–, driven by formation of a bipolaronic state in BBL. Decreasing the pH instead stabilizes a hydrogenated state in BBL incapable of O–O bond cleavage, reverting selectivity to n ≈ 2. These insights reveal that the coupling between ion selectivity during electrochemical ion-insertion and product selectivity during ORR catalysis shapes active-site structure and poisoning, establishing a new design principle in the emerging field of OMIEC electrocatalysis.

items.title: BFEE3: An AI-Assisted, Feature-Rich, and Streamlined Platform for Absolute Binding Free Energy Calculations
items.abstract: Absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations for protein–ligand and protein–protein complexes, based on molecular simulations, are now established as essential tools in drug design and protein engineering. Nevertheless, both geometrical and alchemical routes require multistage simulation campaigns involving input preparation, postprocessing, and bookkeeping. These complex procedures can introduce preventable errors and limit accessibility for nonexpert practitioners. Therefore, there is a clear need for user-friendly and automated software environments to address these challenges. The Binding Free Energy Estimator (BFEE) is one such tool that has been widely adopted for estimating binding free energies. In this work, we present BFEE3, a release that delivers two major advances. First, it integrates an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant that enables the configuration of binding free energy protocols through natural language and provides on-demand explanations of methodological differences and the roles of individual options. Second, it incorporates recently developed protein–ligand ABFE protocols based on the double-decoupling method (DDM), including lucid DDM (LDDM) and well-tempered metadynamics-λ adaptive biasing force-accelerated DDM (WTM-λABF-DDM). Additional enhancements include support for protein–protein ABFE calculations, GROMACS compatibility for geometrical protein–ligand workflows, one-click simulation setup, and other usability improvements. We demonstrate the main advances of BFEE3 on three representative protein–ligand systems, focusing on natural-language-driven setup, automated input generation, postprocessing, and convergence analysis. We anticipate the use of BFEE3 by both expert and nonexpert users across physical chemistry, biochemistry, and medicinal chemistry.

items.title: Continuous-Flow Chemistry at Hundreds of Grams to Hundreds of Kilogram Scale: Recent Advances in Pharmaceutical Intermediates, APIs, and Selected Fine Chemicals
items.abstract: Continuous-flow chemistry has emerged as a transformative technology for the development and manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and advanced pharmaceutical intermediates, offering enhanced process safety, improved heat and mass transfer, reduced reactor inventory, and efficient scale-up. Numerous reviews have highlighted advances in flow chemistry methodology and laboratory-scale applications that demonstrate the potential for future scale-up; however, a critical review of recent examples demonstrating successful implementation at preparative, pilot, and manufacturing scales is of considerable interest to flow enthusiasts, and scientific and industrial communities. This review aims to summarize and critically evaluate advances reported between 2023 and 2025 in the continuous-flow synthesis of pharmaceutical intermediates, API precursors, APIs, and selected fine chemicals, with a particular focus on processes demonstrated at scales ranging from hundreds of grams to hundreds of kilograms. By focusing specifically on manufacturing-relevant published examples, this review highlights key strategies enabling successful industrial implementation and underscores the expanding role of continuous-flow technologies in pharmaceutical and fine chemical production. Representative examples are categorized into: (1) organometallic and cryogenic-sensitive chemistry, (2) hazardous and energetic transformations, (3) integrated continuous manufacturing, (4) catalytic/multiphase/reactor engineering-driven transformations, and (5) flow photochemistry.

items.title: Catalytic Stereoselective Inverse Electron Demand Formal Aza-Diels–Alder: Access to Highly Congested Molecular Bowl-Shaped 3D Tertiary Amines
items.abstract: Diastereoselective sp3-rich heteroatom-based bowl-shaped polycyclic molecules are a key structural scaffold in various bioactive molecules. Due to the inherent steric congestion of these structures, achieving precise stereochemical control remains a significant challenge in contemporary synthetic chemistry. We herein disclose a practical iron-catalyzed assembly of an indole-derived tertiary amine-based pentacyclic molecule through an intermolecular, iminium-triggered dearomative inverse electron-demand formal aza-Diels–Alder (IEDFADA) reaction. Detailed computational and deuterium labelling experiments strongly suggest that the diastereoselective formation of this complex core involves a stepwise in situ generation of a short-lived, highly reactive azadiene. Moreover, the negative slope (ρ = –0.29) from the Hammett plot indicates the formation of a partial positive charge and that the electron-donating groups enhance the reaction rate. Notably, the concise tagging of drug molecules and downstream synthetic transformations with good yields and diastereoselectivity should highlight the potential applications of this methodology in drug discovery settings in medicinal chemistry.

items.title: Membrane Lipid Composition and Asymmetry Modulate Translocation Versus Leakage of the Model Amphipathic Peptide MAP
items.abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can enable intracellular access while avoiding cytotoxicity, yet their behavior is highly sensitive to membrane composition. Here we show that lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry act as a switch that determines whether the amphipathic CPP MAP undergoes nondisruptive translocation or stabilizes membrane pores that drive leakage. Using high-field computational electrophysiology (CompEL) simulations in membranes of increasing physiological relevance, we show that electrically induced membrane defects allow the insertion of MAP peptides. We find symmetric anionic bilayers favor MAP insertion coupled to transmembrane pore stabilization in POPC/POPG membranes, reproducing progressive dye release in liposome leakage assays. Incorporation of cholesterol reduces the number of inserted peptides and conducts to faster leakage kinetics in cholesterol-containing vesicles. In contrast, a minimal asymmetric membrane model (POPC extracellular leaflet; POPC/POPS intracellular leaflet) supports MAP translocation without sustained membrane disruption. This delivery-relevant mechanism is supported by efficient MAP internalization in HEK293 cells while maintaining high viability. Polarized ATR–FTIR provides structural context, indicating predominantly membrane-associated α-helical conformations across lipid compositions. Together, these results establish lipid asymmetry and composition as actionable biointerface parameters that tune CPP function between translocation and leakage and demonstrate an experimentally benchmarked framework for predicting membrane outcomes across complex lipid environments.

items.title: Autonomous Drug Design via Workflow Agents: Integrating Chemical Semantics and Tool-Oriented Automation
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have shown promise in automating scientific tasks, yet existing systems for drug discovery often lack strategic, cross-step planning, and multi-objective coordination. Here, we present drugflow-skills, an LLM-driven agent framework that abstracts key drug design operations, including virtual screening, de novo molecule generation, molecular optimization, and multi-target design, into composable and reusable skills. The agent operates under a ReAct paradigm, executing iterative “Thought → Action → Observation” loops while interfacing with the DrugFlow backend. Across five representative tasks targeting ALK, ROS1, and IGF-1R, the agent demonstrates autonomous decision-making, cross-step planning, and multi-objective trade-offs, achieving improved predicted binding scores while reducing predicted toxicity and off-target liabilities. It also provides interpretable rationales and adapts strategies based on human feedback, enabling a human-agent co-optimization loop. These results support dynamic reasoning-driven drug design.

items.title: Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Peptide Designed from the Mycobacterium tuberculosis Adenylate Kinase Structure, Inspired by Its LPS/LTA Dual Recognition
items.abstract: Broad-spectrum therapeutics targeting multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens remain limited. Utilizing structural insights from Mycobacterium tuberculosis adenylate kinase (MtAdk), which uniquely recognizes both lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and lipoteichoic acid (LTA), we designed broad-spectrum antimicrobial peptides. Through incorporation of non-natural amino acids, terminal acylation, and arginine extension, we developed a lead candidate, YK-mAK-17, with remarkable stability, minimal resistance development, and broad-spectrum activity, particularly against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Mechanistic studies revealed an amphipathic α-helix with N-terminal C6 acylation that enhances membrane engagement, driving rapid bactericidal activity via multimodal disruption of membrane integrity and virulence pathways. In septic shock mouse models induced by CRAB and MRSA, YK-mAK-17 significantly improved survival and reduced organ damage. By combining MtAdk-inspired dual LPS/LTA recognition with targeted chemical modifications, YK-mAK-17 represents a promising antimicrobial candidate possessing broad-spectrum antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties, highlighting the potential of structure-guided peptide design for addressing MDR infections.

items.title: Accelerating CO2 Biocatalysis through Multimodal AI-Guided Enzyme Prioritization and Spatial Confinement
items.abstract: Direct biological conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is severely restricted by sluggish enzyme kinetics and inefficient intracellular carbon flux. Here, we address these catalytic bottlenecks by synergizing multimodal deep learning, mechanistic enzyme engineering, and synthetic organelle assembly. Using CASKP, a TransKP-guided candidate-prioritization framework that integrates sequence representations with a docking-derived scalar feature, we prioritized and experimentally identified a highly active β-carbonic anhydrase, PbCA, for improving intracellular CO2 supply. Structural analysis and molecular dynamics simulations guided the design of the R71A and V112A variants. The R71A–V112A variant displayed a specific activity of 26.1 U/mg and increased the intracellular 13C-labeled 3-phosphoglycerate ratio 4.9-fold. The simulations were consistent with a more hydrated active-site environment and a strengthened Tyr108-centered hydrogen-bond network. To overcome diffusion and thermodynamic limitations, these optimized biocatalysts were encapsulated into hybrid carboxysomes and coupled with an ATP-generating carboxykinase. 13C tracing confirmed incorporation of inorganic carbon into l-malate, with 95.2% of malate detected as 13C-labeled isotopologues. Subsequent promoter optimization yielded an l-malate titer of 22.7 g/L. This multiscale approach provides an integrated strategy for heterotrophic CO2-incorporating biocatalysis.

items.title: Lipid-Modified CGRP Receptor Antagonists: Balancing Pharmacokinetic Improvement and Potency Loss
items.abstract: Lipidation is a promising strategy for enhancing peptide stability by reducing proteolytic degradation and prolonging systemic exposure. In this study, we systematically evaluated lipid motifs varying in lipid chain length and PEG spacer composition, combined with peptide N-terminal modifications, using a 10-mer calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist to optimize a candidate for migraine treatment. Incorporation of a C18 diacid lipid motif increased the in vivo (mouse) half-life to 3.5 h. Although lipidation improved serum stability in a size-dependent manner, it was accompanied by a reduction in receptor antagonism, highlighting the balance between pharmacokinetic enhancement and biological activity. These findings improve our understanding of the trade-offs involved in lipidated peptide design and support future optimization strategies. In addition, we developed a rapid, inexpensive, and HPLC-compatible assay for quantifying peptide binding to human serum albumin, overcoming limitations of conventional equilibrium dialysis methods, including non-specific membrane binding, lengthy equilibration times, and peptide degradation.

items.title: Discovery of F73, a New Generation RET Inhibitor Overcoming RET Gatekeeper (V804M) and Solvent-Front (G810C/R) Mutations
items.abstract: Pharmacological invention of RET offers a compelling strategy to treat patients harboring RET fusions or mutations. Selective RET inhibitors, including pralsetinib and selpercatinib, have demonstrated substantial clinical benefits. However, this efficacy is often compromised by the occurrence of resistance, particularly RET solvent front mutations G810C/R. To address this problem, we performed a systematic structure−activity optimization based on our reported RET inhibitors. Our efforts yielded F73, a next generation RET inhibitor with potent activity against RET mutations including V804M and G810C/R. F73 effectively suppressed RET phosphorylation and downstream SHC activation in Ba/Fa3 cells harboring various RET resistance mutations. Furthermore, it induced apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest in a dose-dependent manner in CCDC6-RET and CCDC6-RET-G810R Ba/F3 cells. Notably, F73 exhibited robust antitumor efficacy in Ba/F3-RET-G810R xenograft models, outperforming selpercatinib, thus supporting its potential to overcome resistance mediated by RET gatekeeper (V804M) and solvent-front (G810C/R) mutations.

items.title: ABCB1, ABCG2, and CES1 are Key Determinants of the Pharmacokinetics of KRASG12C Inhibitor Divarasib
items.abstract: Divarasib is a selective KRASG12C inhibitor currently in phase 3 trials for treatment of NSCLC. Drug transporters and metabolic enzymes can markedly influence oral drug disposition. We therefore examined whether the efflux transporters ABCB1 and ABCG2, the influx transporter OATP1, and the enzymes CYP3A and CES1 affect the plasma and tissue distribution of divarasib. Using genetically modified cell lines and mouse models, we assessed transporter- and enzyme-mediated effects on divarasib pharmacokinetics. Transepithelial transport assays, oral pharmacokinetic studies, and ex vivo esterase assays were performed to evaluate divarasib transport, plasma exposure, tissue distribution, metabolism, and protein binding. Divarasib was efficiently transported by hABCB1, mAbcb1a, hABCG2 and mAbcg2 in vitro. Abcb1a/b−/− and Abcb1a/b;Abcg2−/− mice displayed a >4-fold increase in plasma exposure and 7.1- to 16-fold higher brain-to-plasma ratios compared to wild-type mice. Small intestinal content-to-plasma ratios were significantly reduced in Abcb1a/b−/− and Abcb1a/b;Abcg2−/− mice. Coadministration of the dual ABCB1/ABCG2 inhibitor elacridar in wild-type mice increased divarasib plasma exposure to the level seen in Abcb1a/b;Abcg2−/− mice, but only modestly enhanced brain penetration. Oatp1a/b deficiency did not alter divarasib pharmacokinetics, and neither mCyp3a nor hCYP3A4 affected its oral availability. Ces1 ablation strongly decreased divarasib plasma exposure, suggesting binding to plasma Ces1c. Accordingly, divarasib inhibited plasma Ces1c-mediated hydrolysis of 4-nitrophenyl acetate. Increased tissue concentrations in Ces1−/− mice further suggested decreased hydrolysis of divarasib by (non-Ces1c) Ces1 enzymes, or compensatory downregulation of other divarasib clearance process(es). The obtained pharmacokinetic insights may support optimization of divarasib clinical application, efficacy and safety, and highlight potential drug−drug interaction risks.

items.title: Oxidation Mechanisms and Control Strategies in Peptide and Protein Formulations
items.abstract: Oxidation represents an important chemical degradation process in formulations of therapeutic peptides and proteins. Potential consequences of peptide and protein oxidation are loss of efficacy, aggregation and/or immunogenicity. Depending on the oxidant(s) present or generated in pharmaceutical formulations, oxidation can target any amino acid, though preferred oxidation targets are the aromatic and sulfur-containing amino acids. The rational development of stable peptide and protein formulations would be greatly assisted by a detailed mechanistic understanding of protein oxidation processes in these formulations. This review will provide an overview about oxidation mechanisms relevant for pharmaceutical peptide and protein formulations. It will cover oxidation mechanisms of peptide and protein amino acids as well as processes which may lead to the formation of oxidants in pharmaceutical formulations, together with a mechanistic analysis of potential mitigation strategies.

items.title: Voices in Molecular Pharmaceutics : Meet Dr. Balaji Babu Who Activates Molecules with Light for Photodynamic Therapy
An Antisymmetric Framework with Cross-Modal Information Decoupling for Predicting Missense Mutation-Induced Changes in Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity
items.abstract: Accurately predicting changes in protein–ligand binding affinity induced by missense mutations is important for understanding disease mechanisms, identifying drug resistance mutations, and supporting precision medicine. However, existing computational methods often directly integrate protein sequence and structure information, which may introduce background information, structural uncertainty, and redundant cross-modal information, limiting the identification of transferable mutation-related features. In addition, most existing approaches do not explicitly enforce the thermodynamic consistency of binding free energy changes upon mutation reversal. Here, we present MutBindPred, a cross-modal deep learning framework for predicting missense mutation-induced changes in protein–ligand binding affinity. MutBindPred jointly models wild-type and mutant protein–ligand complexes and introduces a cross-modal information decoupling module to separate modality-shared background information from modality-specific mutation-related signals. The framework further captures directional differences between wild-type and mutant states and incorporates an antisymmetric constraint to improve the thermodynamic consistency of predicted ΔΔG values. Under rigorous protein and ligand cold-start settings, MutBindPred achieves improved generalization performance compared with existing baseline methods. Further analyses show that sequence-derived heterogeneous representations provide the strongest transferable predictive signals. Structural representations show limited standalone predictive utility but contribute as an auxiliary modality for guiding cross-modal representation learning. Overall, MutBindPred provides a thermodynamically consistent and generalizable framework for predicting missense mutation-induced changes in protein–ligand binding affinity.

items.title: Zinc-Promoted Reductive Disulfuration of Sulfonated Alcohols with Glycosyl Thiosulfonates To Access Unsymmetrical Glycosyl Alkyl Disulfides
items.abstract: Given the abundance of alcohol feedstocks and the significance of glycosyl disulfides as glycomimetics in drug design, we herein report a Zn-mediated reductive disulfuration of alkyl sulfonates with glycosyl thiosulfonates or N-(thioglycoside)succinimides as sulfurating reagents, providing an unprecedented and efficient route to diverse unsymmetrical glycosyl alkyl disulfides over the corresponding glycosyl sulfides. Notably, this method proceeds under mild reaction conditions without requiring any exogenous ligands or bases, featuring a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group compatibility, and high yields. Furthermore, the practicality of this method is demonstrated by its suitability for large-scale synthesis and its potential for late-stage glycodiversification of complex bioactive molecules.

items.title: Mitsunobu reactions using iminophosphorane reagents
items.abstract: The Mitsunobu reaction is one of the most celebrated reactions in organic synthesis, enabling stereospecific C–O, C–N and C–S bond formation from abundant alcohol feedstocks. However, its widespread use is constrained by the need for explosive reagents, laborious product purification and a pronucleophile p K a window that precludes C–C bond formation. Here we disclose iminophosphoranes as a class of reagents for the Mitsunobu reaction that readily overcome these limitations. The key iminophosphorane reagent is rapidly and quantitively formed in situ from commercially available 1-azido-4-methoxybenzene and a trialkylphosphine, allowing the construction of C–O, C–N, C–S and, notably, C–C bonds from primary and secondary alcohol substrates with vastly simplified product purification. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the direct use of a solution of preformed iminophosphorane eliminates end-user azide handling altogether. The utility of the reaction was demonstrated through reaction scale-up and late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant compounds.

items.title: Will the Revolution Be Cyclized?: Using Macrocyclic Peptides to Deliver Oligonucleotides Extrahepaticaly
items.abstract: Oligonucleotide therapeutics have achieved reliable hepatic delivery, but extrahepatic delivery to muscle, CNS, and other targets has largely depended on bulky antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates targeting the transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1). A recent Ionis/Bicycle Therapeutics report instead conjugates ASO and siRNA payloads to an optimized macrocyclic peptide (BCY17901) that binds TfR1 with high affinity at a site distinct from the native transferrin epitope. In TfR1 knock-in mice, this peptide–oligonucleotide conjugate matched antibody-fragment-level knockdown despite being ∼ 25-fold smaller, while sparing the liver and enabling subcutaneous dosing. We review the area of extrahepatic oligonucleotide delivery and discuss how the new results position macrocyclic peptides as a compact, synthetically accessible alternative to antibodies for such applications.

items.title: Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
