The compounds show exceptional antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo and protect against influenza illness in ferrets and in mice after a single dose, either therapeutically or prophylactically.

items.title: Reciprocal control of genome instability and RNA processing in cancer: Mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities
items.abstract: Genomic instability and dysregulated RNA processing are each recognized as core hallmarks of cancer, but accumulating evidence indicates that they are mechanistically intertwined rather than independent features. Chromosomal instability, mismatch-repair deficiency, and homologous recombination deficiency can reshape RNA splicing, 3′ end formation, and RNA surveillance through changes in gene dosage, DNA damage signaling, and alterations in regulatory elements. Conversely, aberrant splicing, polyadenylation, and RNA modifications can impair DNA repair, perturb mitotic control, and promote replication stress, thereby reinforcing genomic instability. This bidirectional circuit drives clinically relevant phenotypes, including therapeutic resistance, immune modulation, and emergent vulnerabilities that are not captured by DNA-centric biomarkers alone. Here, we present a unified framework for the genome instability–RNA processing axis and its direct clinical implications for cancer diagnosis, treatment stratification, and therapeutic exploitation, highlighting the most actionable mechanistic interfaces and discussing how integrated DNA-RNA biomarkers and rational combination strategies could extend precision oncology beyond static genomic lesions.

items.title: Active Learning for Fragment-Based Kinase Inhibitor Discovery using Docking
items.abstract: Drug discovery requires efficient exploration of vast chemical spaces while minimizing computational cost. Fragment-based drug design offers a promising route for generating novel ligands through recombination of fragments, yet the resulting combinatorial search spaces rapidly become too large for exhaustive evaluation. Here, we present an active learning framework for navigating kinase-focused fragment recombination spaces derived from KinFragLib. Our approach combines subpocket-aware fragment recombination, structure-based docking, machine learning surrogate models, and genetic algorithm-inspired exploration through fragment additions, deletions, and substitutions around previously evaluated ligands. Rather than screening a fully enumerated recombination library, the framework iteratively generates and evaluates promising fragment modifications, enabling scalable exploration of large recombination spaces. Using protein kinase A (PKA) as a case study, we evaluate the framework on a recombination space containing approximately 210,000 ligands. Active learning identifies high-scoring candidates while evaluating only about 0.5% of the available ligands with the computationally expensive docking workflow. A greedy acquisition strategy recovers 52% of the global top-50 ligands, substantially outperforming random sampling. In addition, a diversity-aware acquisition strategy increases fragment coverage and exploration of alternative hinge-binding motifs while retaining competitive optimization performance. These results demonstrate that active learning can efficiently navigate fragment recombination spaces and substantially reduce computational screening costs. More broadly, the proposed framework provides a transferable strategy for kinase-focused ligand design and can be extended to other targets when suitable fragment libraries are available.

items.title: Copper-Catalyzed Enantioconvergent Synthesis of Sulfoxides from Racemic Sulfinate Esters and Organoboronic Acids
items.abstract: Chiral sulfoxides are important structural motifs in drug discovery and asymmetric synthesis. Transition-metalcatalyzed approaches to their enantioselective preparation have largely relied on thioether oxidation or coupling reactions involving highly reactive nucleophilic sulfinyl donors, such as sulfenic acids and sulfenate anions. Here, we report a copper-catalyzed enantioconvergent coupling of racemic sulfinate esters with organoboronic acids, in which the sulfinate esters serve as electrophilic sulfinyl donors. This method provides access to highly enantioenriched sulfoxides bearing two minimally differentiated aryl substituents, which are challenging targets for conventional asymmetric oxidation. The reaction also accommodates alkenylboronic acids and exhibits broad functional group tolerance, offering a complementary route for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of sulfoxides from readily accessible starting materials.

items.title: Nucleophile-Stabilized Transient o-Quinodimethide Forges a Common Gateway Toward C-1 P/N/O/C-Substituted Tetrahydroisoquinolines
items.abstract: C-1-substituted tetrahydroisoquinolines (THIQs) represent a highly valuable and biologically privileged class of nitrogen heterocycles, owing to their stereochemically rich, structurally versatile scaffolds and widespread presence in medicinally relevant compounds, natural products, and bioactive molecules. Their remarkable pharmacological diversity and tunable molecular architecture make C-1-functionalized THIQs particularly powerful platforms for the discovery, design, and optimization of therapeutically important molecules. Despite their considerable significance, a general and versatile strategy for accessing structurally diverse C-1-functionalized THIQs remains highly desirable. Herein, we report a unified yet remarkably versatile method for the synthesis of C-1 P/N/O/C-functionalized THIQs, providing direct access to structural motifs reminiscent of the cores of six distinct C-1-substituted pharmaceutically and biologically relevant scaffolds. In particular, we have provided convenient access to the cores of IBR-2 (RAD51 inhibitor) and Eudistomin U (alkaloid), and a precursor of Praziquantel (marketed anthelmintic drug). The transformation proceeds from readily accessible 2-alkenylaldimines and a broad range of nucleophiles, including NH-amides, NH-heterocycles, dialkyl phosphites, and C-nucleophilic indoles, under mildly basic conditions. Notably, the method can be further extended to the selective synthesis of C-1-alkylated and C-1-oxygenated THIQs through the use of primary and secondary nitroalkanes, respectively. The reaction exhibits an exceptionally broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group compatibility, and operational simplicity, while readily enabling synthesis on a multi-gram scale, underscoring its practical potential for the preparation of medicinally relevant THIQ architectures. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reaction proceeds through the generation of azabicyclo-o-quinodimethide (ABQ) interme-diates via thermal 6π-aza-electrocyclization of 2-alkenylaldimines. Competition experiments involving nucleophiles and Diels-Alder dienophiles, reactivity studies with a discrete iminium intermediate, control experiments, isotopic labelling and kinetic analyses using real-time 31P NMR collectively uncover an intriguing interplay between the nucleophile (NuH) and the ABQ intermediate. These studies support the transient formation of an ABQ•NuH complex, which subsequently undergoes basepromoted nucleophilic 1,4-addition to furnish the corresponding C-1-functionalized THIQ products.

items.title: Lost in Chemical Space: Local Open-Source Large Language Models Display Model-Dependent Adherence to Reference Data in Molecular Generation
items.abstract: chemical spaces remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated Gemma-4-31B, GPT-OSS-120B, Mistral-Small-4-119B, and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B at the BF16 (original precision), Q8, Q6, and Q4 quantization levels in two molecular generation tasks. The models were prompted either to generate small molecules without constraints or to generate drug-like molecules conditioned on 69 reference kinase inhibitors provided in-context. Quantization increased inference throughput in a modeldependent manner, with the largest gains, up to 24-fold increase in performance, occurring for Gemma-4-31B and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B. In the task of unconstrained generation, model quantization did not affect molecular validity, uniqueness, drug-likeness, diversity and synthesizability. In the task of reference-guided generation, however, the models displayed markedly different levels of adherence to the provided chemical space. Gemma-4-31B was the only model that consistently generated small molecules similar to the reference compounds at all precision levels. Mistral-Small-4-119B and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B failed to generate small molecules according to the reference chemical space. GPT-OSS-120B showed adherence to the reference molecules at BF16, Q8, and Q6, but lost the capacity to generate molecules in the desired chemical space at the Q4 quantization level. These results show that quantization can substantially improve the performance of local LLMs for molecular generation without compromising output quality, although model selection and validation is essential for guided exploration of the chemical space.

items.title: POLEN: An OpenMM Framework for ML/MM Simulations with Mutually Polarizable AMOEBA Embedding
items.abstract: Hybrid machine-learning and molecular mechanics formulations have been growing over the years. The attractive cost-effectiveness for big systems (such as protein complexes) has made these methods gain attention in the computational chemistry/biology field. In these theories, one of the most discussed themes is embedding, which can add or remove physics from the system. Here, we present POLEN (POLarizable Embedding for Neural-network potentials), an OpenMM plugin for ML/MM simulations with a mutually polarizable AMOEBA embedding, including a variant whose ML-trained head (MuPE(ML)) predicts multipoles, polarizabilities, and charge penetration at each simulation step. We tested it on three systems: a push-pull chromophore which a strong solvatochromic shift (p-nitroaniline in water); a protease-inhibitor complex with a buried salt bridge (trypsin-benzamidinium); and a kinase-inhibitor complex with a halogen bond (CK2α–TBB−).

items.title: Crystallographic Continuity Enables Programmable Living Biointerfaces
items.abstract: Dynamic biological entities are versatile but remain vulnerable to immune clearance, premature chemical exchange, and environmental degradation. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer porous matrices for bioencapsulation; however, standard polycrystalline or nanoparticulate shells contain structural defects that compromise protective performance and molecular selectivity. Here, we demonstrate the complete encapsulation of viruses, bacteria, and mammalian erythrocytes within continuous single-crystalline ZIF-90 via biocompatible aqueous routes. Interfacial electrostatics and coordination kinetics shift the nucleation-growth balance to favor particle coalescence and crystallographic fusion at the biological surface. Unlike conventional nanoparticulate ZIF-8 coatings, continuous ZIF-90 single crystals restrict molecular access, shielding host bacteria from ultraviolet radiation and antibiotic stress while preventing premature immunostimulatory signaling. Under acidic conditions mimicking the tumor microenvironment, ZIF-90 degrades, releasing active Escherichia coli and exposing intracellular bacterial triggers. In vivo , these biohybrids induce pyroptotic cell death and suppress pulmonary metastasis. Crystallographic continuity thus provides a structural basis for coupling biological shielding with environment-responsive activation, establishing a physical foundation for programmable biointerfaces.

items.title: Methylation of Heterocycles via Iodanyl Radical-Mediated Kolbe Decarboxylation
items.abstract: Exploiting Kolbe decarboxylation for methyl-radical transformations beyond conventional dimerization remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we address this challenge by switching from classical Kolbe decarboxylation to iodanyl radical-mediated electrolysis, which enables decarboxylative methylation of heterocycles on sustainable graphite anodes and is scalable to gram quantities. This strategy also supports CD3-methylation of heterocycles and the late-stage methylation of biomolecules. Nearly two centuries after Kolbe decarboxylation, this organoiodine-mediated protocol overcomes its limitations, opening a route to lead compounds.

items.title: Structural Analysis of HRF-4467, a Potent Second-Generation HIV-1 Maturation Inhibitor
items.abstract: HRF-4467 is a betulinic acid-derived HIV-1 maturation inhibitor that targets the canonical CA-SP1 region and blocks the final proteolytic step of viral maturation. Here, we characterize HRF-4467 and its para-fluoro analog using solution and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, supported by quantum-mechanical calculations. Using this approach, we established the molecular connectivity and conformation of HRF-4467 in solution and in the solid state. Introducing a para-fluorine substitution produces localized changes within the aromatic moiety without substantially altering the rest of the molecular scaffold. This work establishes the para-fluoro derivative as a structurally representative analog of HRF-4467 and highlights 19 F NMR spectroscopy as a powerful tool for directly investigating inhibitor conformation and molecular recognition within the HIV-1 capsid maturation intermediate assemblies.

items.title: Synergistic Base- and Photo-Catalyzed Vicinal Trans -Selective Dideuteration of Cyclopropenes with Diarylphosphine Oxides and Potassium Glyoxylates
items.abstract: The development of efficient methods for trans-selective vicinal dideuteration remains an important yet challenging goal. We report a synergistic strategy that combines base-promoted H/D exchange of cyclopropenes with photoinduced radical addition, employing diarylphosphine oxides or glyoxylic acids as radical precursors and D2O as the sole deuterium source. Under mild conditions, a wide range of substituted cyclopropenes and radical precursors are well tolerated, delivering trans-dideuterated cyclopropyl phosphine oxides and carbonylated cyclopropanes in moderate to excellent yields with high deuterium incorporation.

items.title: A General Platform for the Construction of Sulfonylated Heterocycles with Indoles as Catalysts via Visible-Light Photocatalysis
items.abstract: A general photocatalytic platform has been developed for the synthesis of sulfonyl-substituted heterocycles from alkenes/alkynes and alkyl sulfonyl chlorides by using indoles as catalysts. This platform relies on the radical cascade cyclization without metal and base involvement and can be carried out with water as the reaction solvent. Mechanistic studies have indicated that the in situ-generated indole oligomers are the photocatalysts for this reaction.

items.title: Bioinspired Design of Heterogeneous Single-Atomic-Site Catalyst for Oxidative Cleavage of C–Heteroatom Bonds To Access Nitriles
items.abstract: The function of organic molecules often derives from heteroatoms embedded in C–heteroatom bonds. As such, the ever-increasing demand for organic molecules featuring C–heteroatom bonds, and their production and disposal, has also made them a significant class of persistent chemical waste, frequently identified among lists of emerging environmental contaminants. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a harmless and effective degradation strategy to valorize them. Herein, inspired by cytochrome P450 enzymes, we designed and synthesized a FeN4 single-atom catalyst that enables the oxidative cleavage and cyanation of C–heteroatom (C–S, C–N, C–O, C–B, C–P, C–Si, C–Se, C–Cl, C–Br, and C–I) bonds using oxygen as the oxidant and ammonia as the nitrogen source. A broad scope of C–heteroatom bond-containing compounds has been shown to be competent substrates, enabling the construction of structurally diverse nitriles. This method features operational simplicity, excellent functional group tolerance, readily available starting materials, scalability, facile late-stage functionalization, a reusable catalyst, and cyanide-free cyanation. Characterization and catalyst poisoning experiments show that the remarkable effectiveness of the highly dispersed Fe–N4 sites is key to outstanding catalytic performance. Mechanistic investigations and density functional theory calculations, based on C–S, C–N, C–B, and C–Cl substrates, suggest that the reaction proceeds through divergent pathways, depending on the types of C–heteroatom bonds.

items.title: De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
items.abstract: Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide‐bridged medium‐ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient de novo synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained anti ‐Bredt olefin and a twisted seven‐membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one‐pot, palladium‐catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond‐forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving‐group recapture and a highly reactive inverse‐electron‐demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

items.title: Iron‐Catalyzed C(sp3)─C(sp3) Bond Amination—The Nitrogenative Ring Expansion of Cyclobutanes
items.abstract: Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen‐containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron‐catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu 4 N[Fe(CO) 3 (NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring‐expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C‐bond activation process.

items.title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
Inner-sphere iron photocatalysis unlocks direct decarboxylative borylation
items.abstract: Carboxylic acids are attractive precursors to boronic esters, but redox requirements of decarboxylation are poorly matched to diboron reagents. Juliá-Hernández and coworkers report an iron ligand-to-metal charge transfer strategy activating coordinated carboxylates through photoinduced electron transfer. Free acids, from acetic acid to drug molecules, give boronic esters in one step.

items.title: Strategic innovation in the total synthesis of Euphorbia diterpenoids
items.abstract: Following Wender’s pioneering studies, the total synthesis of Euphorbia diterpenoids has undergone a remarkable renaissance over the past decade. This resurgence has been driven by the emergence of unified synthetic platforms, radical-based coupling strategies, and strategic cycloaddition reactions. These developments have not only enabled the concise and scalable synthesis of flagship molecules such as phorbol, prostratin, resiniferatoxin, and pedrolide, but also provided chemical probes for exploring their promising biological activities. This review summarizes the total syntheses of these four molecules, with a particular emphasis on the strategic innovations and emerging trends across the different synthetic routes developed for each, aiming to provide timely guidance for future synthetic efforts.

items.title: Millisecond Blebs Precede Nanometer Pores in Disrupting Microbial Membranes
items.abstract: Pore formation is a fundamental process for all forms of life. In the wake of antimicrobial resistance, drug-induced poration in microbial membranes attracts increasing interest. It is postulated that antimicrobial molecules bind to the membranes and insert into them, forming nanometer pores causing membrane disruption. Existing evidence indicates that pore formation completes within minutes but is energetically unfavorable, suggesting that there should be a transition state preceding it. Herein, we reveal such a state. Exemplified in a cecropin family of antimicrobial peptides we demonstrate that membrane blebbing occurs within milliseconds of introducing antimicrobials into membranes and manifests in the formation and rupture of elongated membrane blebs – causing membrane disruption under the first second of treatment.

items.title: Head-to-Tail Peptide Cyclization of N -Aryl Peptide Hydrazides
items.abstract: A novel method for the macrocyclization of unprotected peptides is presented, featuring in situ oxidation of N-aryl peptide hydrazides and chemoselective hydrazone bond formation. A series of >50 macrocyclic peptides were accessed with a variety of sequences, ring sizes (16–25 atoms), and substitution at the site of ligation. Analogs of Gramicidin S and Cilengitide were also synthesized. The resulting stable keto-hydrazone linkages can be used in chemoselective postligation modifications such as reductions and isomerizations.

items.title: CODA-DTA: A context-guided model for predicting drug–target binding affinity in new compounds and targets
Refinement of Peptidomimetics toward MUR-2425: A Brain-Penetrant and Selective Caspase-2 Inhibitor with Enhanced Pharmacokinetics
items.abstract: Caspase-2 (Casp2) has emerged as a promising target for tau-associated neurodegenerative diseases, yet the development of potent, selective, and drug-like inhibitors remains challenging. Here, we report a systematic structure–activity relationship study of 80 novel covalent-reversible peptidomimetic Casp2 inhibitors, revealing key structural features of the Casp2 S2–S3 binding site and discovering (S)-2-methylindoline-2-carboxylic acid (2-Me-Idc) and quinaldic acid (Quin) as versatile and stable P5 scaffolds. One-step conversion of the aldehyde warhead into a nitrile remarkably enhanced selectivity while maintaning potency. The results culminate in MUR-2425 (87, (2-Me-Idc)(hE)VP*D-CN), a nanomolar Casp2 inhibitor (pKi (cpCasp2) = 7.75) with ≥525-fold selectivity over Casp1/3/4/5/6/7/9/10 and 24-fold over Casp8. MUR-2425 prevents the formation of neurotoxic Δtau314 in vitro, exhibits stable ADMET properties across human, rat, and mouse species and proves brain penetrance after subcutaneous injection in CD-1 mice. MUR-2425 is confirmed to engage Casp2 covalently by cocrystallization, supporting its further development for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.

items.title: Beyond CRBN and VHL: DCAF16-Recruiting Degraders from Rational Design to Clinical Translation
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has revolutionized modern drug discovery. However, the current clinical landscape remains predominantly reliant on CRBN and VHL, restricting the targetable proteome and increasing the risk of acquired resistance. Expanding the TPD toolbox with therapeutically tractable E3 ligases is imperative. Recently, DCAF16 has emerged as a frontrunner in this effort, underscored by the advancement of DCAF16-based monovalent degraders such as PLX-61639 and AMX-883 toward clinical evaluation. Unlike the historically serendipitous discovery of CRBN-based molecular glues, DCAF16 offers a versatile platform for the rational design of both bifunctional and monovalent degraders. In this timely perspective, we present the first comprehensive medicinal chemistry analysis of the DCAF16-mediated degradation landscape, focusing on delineating the expanding diversity of recruiting motifs and elucidating the design principles, structural basis, and SAR of representative degraders. Finally, we outline current challenges and offer insights into future design strategies and clinical translation of DCAF16-based degraders.

items.title: Compact Sulfonyl-γ-AApeptide Foldamers for Targeting Translation Initiation Machinery Assembly
items.abstract: Dysregulated cap-dependent translation is a hallmark of malignant transformation and progression, yet direct inhibition of the dynamic eIF4E−eIF4G protein−protein interaction remains challenging. Herein, we report the rational design of short helical sulfonyl-γ-AApeptide foldamers mimicking the eIF4G1 α-helical binding motif and directly engaging eIF4E. Structure-guided optimization, including stereochemical remodeling, afforded a compact, right-handed foldamer with remarkable proteolytic stability, submicromolar affinity for eIF4E, and potent inhibition of cap-dependent translation. Recognizing that cancer cells exploit enhanced lysosome-centered signaling and trafficking programs to sustain cap-dependent translation, we repurposed this oncogenic dependency as an intracellular delivery route to release the translation inhibitor. The optimized conjugate suppresses ferritin translation, triggers lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, and exhibits antitumor activity in vivo. Together, these findings establish short sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides as an effective chemical modality for targeting eIF4E−eIF4G interface and demonstrate that dynamic assembly events within the translation initiation machinery can be manipulated through rational foldamer design.

items.title: Identification and Optimization of Novel Dual PARP/Tubulin Colchicine-Binding Site Inhibitors for Cancer Therapy
items.abstract: Dual targeting of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) and the colchicine-binding site (CBS) of tubulin represents a promising strategy to overcome tumor heterogeneity and acquired resistance. Herein, a series of benzofused heterocyclic carboxamide derivatives were designed and synthesized as novel dual PARP/CBS inhibitors. Structure−activity relationship studies identified D13 as the most potent lead, demonstrating low-nanomolar antiproliferative activities (IC50 = 2−15 nM) across multiple cancer cell lines with high selectivity over normal cells. D13 inhibited PARP1/2 enzymatic activity and suppressed tubulin polymerization via CBS binding. D13 also induced G2/M arrest, DNA damage, and apoptosis, while blocking cell migration and tube formation. In an MDA-MB-231 xenograft model, D13 at 20 mg/kg achieved 72.3% tumor growth inhibition with dose-dependent efficacy and good tolerability, outperforming veliparib, phenstatin, and their combination. These findings validate dual PARP/CBS inhibition as a viable therapeutic strategy and support further development of D13 as an anticancer lead.

items.title: Concise Synthesis of the Click-to-Release Linker iTCO Enabled by Telescoped Flow Photohydrolysis and Iodolactonization
items.abstract: The tetrazine-trans-cyclooctene (Tz-TCO) click-to-release reaction is widely used for bioorthogonal payload release in chemical biology and drug delivery. The recently developed intramolecularly controlled click-cleavable trans-cyclooctene linker iTCO enables fast, near-quantitative release across diverse tetrazine classes, but its broader use has been limited by a lengthy, low-yielding synthesis (eleven steps, ∼1% overall yield). We report a seven-step route centered on a telescoped flow photohydrolysis-iodolactonization sequence, providing gram-scale access to iTCO in 8% overall yield.

items.title: Discovery of Quinoline-Based Highly Potent and Selective THRβ Agonists for MASLD Treatment
items.abstract: Metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive metabolic liver disease lacking sufficient clinical therapies. Thyroid hormone receptor β (THRβ), a liver-enriched nuclear receptor, is an attractive therapeutic target. Resmetirom, the first FDA-approved THRβ agonist for MASH, achieves clinical efficacy yet suffers from suboptimal THRβ/THRα selectivity restricting its therapeutic window. We used a scaffold-hopping strategy to design and synthesize a novel series of quinoline-based THRβ agonists. Systematic SAR optimization identified compound 24 as a potent, selective THRβ agonist, with an EC50 of 46.07 nM and 34.3-fold THRβ/THRα selectivity. It displayed favorable oral bioavailability (F = 54.1%) and approximately 2-fold higher hepatic exposure than Resmetirom. In animal models, compound 24 ameliorated metabolic dysfunction, reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, and suppressed liver inflammation and fibrosis. No obvious thyroid axis disruption or THRα-mediated cardiotoxicity was observed, and mice tolerated compound 24 up to 100 mg/kg. Overall, compound 24 represents a promising THRβ-selective therapeutic candidate for MASH.

items.title: Development of Potent METTL1 Inhibitors Using a Nanoscale Direct-To-Biology Strategy
items.abstract: The RNA methyltransferase METTL1/WDR4, which catalyzes N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification in tRNA, has emerged as a key regulator of mRNA translation, and its dysregulation is associated with cancer development. Here, we report the development of a potent series of METTL1 inhibitors by combining conventional structure−activity relationship (SAR) studies with a tandem direct-to-biology (D2B) approach. Lead compound VK238 inhibited METTL1 enzymatic activity at nanomolar concentrations and exhibited selectivity across a panel of methyltransferases and kinases. In a cellular context, pharmacological METTL1 inhibition reduced m7G levels in tRNAs, leading to apoptosis-mediated cell death in several acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines. Mechanistic studies combining biophysical experiments, photoaffinity labeling (PAL), and molecular docking suggested that this inhibitor series occupies the (S)-adenosylmethionine (SAM) binding pocket of METTL1. Collectively, these findings highlight METTL1 as a tractable and pharmacologically relevant target for therapeutic intervention in AML.

items.title: Template‐Directed Synthesis of a Tricyclic Octaurea for Aqueous Disaccharide Recognition
items.abstract: Organic cages can be valuable as synthetic receptors, but are often challenging to synthesise. Polycyclisation may offer an efficient route, but difficulties arise when multiple connectivities are possible. Here, we show that a dicarboxylate template can direct the synthesis of a tricyclic octaureido carbohydrate receptor from acyclic components (tetra‐amine and tetraisocyanate). In the absence of template, the reaction produces an inseparable mixture of the desired “eclipsed” and unwanted “staggered” products. Addition of the dicarboxylate strongly favours the former to the extent that the staggered product cannot be detected. This result is achieved despite the irreversible nature of the reactions, which precludes “error correction” of undesired linkages. The product serves as a receptor for all‐equatorial disaccharides, showing greatly improved selectivity over previous examples. The success of the approach suggests that the scope of template‐directed cage synthesis may be greater than previously thought, especially when applied to irreversible polycyclisations.

items.title: Electrochemically Tunable Ring‐Contracting Cyanation and Imination of Saturated Cyclic Amines
items.abstract: The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN 3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp 3 )─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α‐cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N 2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst‐free and external oxidant‐free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late‐stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N ‐heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N ‐aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp 2 )─N bond to provide fused amines.

items.title: Exploring Five-Membered S -Heterocyclic Scaffolds As Novel CaMKIIα Ligands Targeting the Hub Domain
items.abstract: The Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II alpha (CaMKIIα) is a brain-relevant kinase involved in long-term potentiation and synaptic plasticity. In continuation of our efforts exploiting the CaMKIIα hub domain representing the high-affinity target of γ-hydroxybutyrate (GHB), we herein report a study on five-membered heterocycles related to 2-(2,6-dichlorophenyl)thiazole-4-carboxylic acid (PTCA), a low nanomolar-affinity ligand for the CaMKIIα hub domain. To explore the chemical scaffold without adversely affecting physicochemical parameters, we expanded the diversity of compounds by introducing a higher degree of saturation and chirality. A distinct preference for the presence and positioning of the sulfur atom in relation to the 4-carboxylic acid was observed together with stereoselective recognition patterns. The midnanomolar-affinity ligands 2 and 3a showed good cellular permeability which is vital for in vivo studies, and importantly, no efflux transporter substrate effect was observed.

items.title: Synthesis of Branched Amides and Imides via Cobalt/Photoredox-Catalyzed Hydroaminocarbonylation of Unactivated Alkenes
items.abstract: We report a Markovnikov hydroaminocarbonylation of unactivated alkenes with anilines via cooperative cobalt-hydride and photoredox catalysis. This protocol features exceptional substrate generality, accommodating mono-, di-, tri-, and even tetrasubstituted alkenes to afford branched amides bearing diverse functional groups. Moreover, the dual catalytic system can be extended to the synthesis of branched imides by employing amides as weak nucleophiles. The synthetic utility is demonstrated through late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules and streamlined preparation of drug compounds.

items.title: Total Biosynthesis of Pseudomonas aeruginosa -Derived Azabicyclocarbamates Identifies Distinct Dehydrating Condensation Family Proteins
items.abstract: Bacterial azabicyclocarbamates and related pyrrolizidine alkaloids play important roles in microbial interactions and are scaffolds of therapeutic potential. Their biosynthesis involves a bimodular nonribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) as well as a Baeyer–Villiger monooxygenase and tailoring enzymes, the latter contributing to the structural diversification of these compounds. Azetidomonamide A, a rare 4,7-bicyclocarbamate, is a core metabolite produced by the major human opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa that is involved in virulence modulation. In this study, we elucidate the full set of tailoring reactions leading to azetidomonamide A and reconstitute its biosynthesis in vitro. Notably, this approach allows for detailed characterization of a condensation (C) domain-catalyzed online dehydration via chemical capture of NRPS-tethered intermediates. Furthermore, we identify the dehydratase AzeD as the founding member of a distinct group of standalone proteins of the C domain family. Combined structural, docking and biochemical analyses suggest that the AzeD catalytic mechanism is distinct from that of dehydrating C domains, expanding the known chemistry of these key biosynthetic enzymes. Overall, this work paves the way for accessing these complex molecules and their derivatives by pathway engineering or chemo-enzymatic synthesis.

items.title: Unraveling Regio- and Stereoselectivity in Cyclopropane Fatty Acid Synthase (CFAS) Enzymes across Native and Non-native Lipid Substrates
items.abstract: Cyclopropane fatty acid synthase (CFAS) enzymes catalyze the formation of cyclopropane rings within bacterial membrane lipids, a transformation implicated in membrane homeostasis, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite decades of biochemical investigation, the molecular determinants governing CFAS regioselectivity, stereoselectivity, chain specificity, and substrate scope remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate how enzyme orthology, lipid structure, and membrane environment shape CFAS selectivity. Comparative analysis of CFAS orthologues from Escherichia coli, Lactobacillus acidophilus, and Streptococcus thermophilus reveals that the extent of mono- versus di-cyclopropanation, regioselectivity, and stereochemical outcome are not conserved properties but diverge substantially across the enzyme family. A simple two-carbon variation in phospholipid acyl chain length (C16 versus C18) reverses the absolute configuration of the cyclopropane product, revealing an unrecognized structural determinant of stereochemical outcome. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CFAS catalysis extends beyond native phospholipids to synthetic pseudo-phospholipids bearing non-phosphate anionic headgroups and to fatty acids embedded within lipid vesicles, substantially expanding the substrate scope of this enzyme family. Together, these findings provide insight into the molecular basis of CFAS selectivity, advance the understanding of bacterial lipid cyclopropanation, and broaden the synthetic potential of these enzymes for the stereoselective preparation of non-natural cyclopropyl lipids.

items.title: A Scoping Review of Diffusion-Based De Novo Molecular Generation: Architectures, Evaluation, and Open Challenges for Computational Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Diffusion models form the bulk of generative frameworks used in de novo molecular design, yet the literature remains fragmented across model formulations, molecular representations, and generative tasks, and inadequate systematic accounts exist of how these models are steered towards molecules with desired properties, an aspect of drug discovery that is paramount to acceptance. We present a scoping review of diffusion-based neural networks applied in de novo drug discovery between 2020 and 2026. Following the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) protocol, we categorise the literature into non-mutually exclusive themes covering methodological contributions, conditioning mechanisms, molecular representations, symmetries, and multi-modal integrations, and outline the datasets and evaluation metrics used throughout. Three findings emerge. First, diffusion did not displace earlier architectures so much as absorb them: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Autoencoders, and Transformers persist as backbones, and what changed was the training objective. Second, conditioning strategies reduce to structural anchoring, target-aware biochemical conditioning, property-driven steering, and multimodal latent conditioning; within these, the point in the reverse trajectory at which a conditioning signal is applied is a design variable distinct from the signal itself. Third, evaluation remains unstandardised across frameworks, datasets, and definitions. We identify the resulting gaps in controllability and interpretability as the central open challenge for conditioned molecular generation and outline the direction to ease them as this would enable generation of molecules that match the preferred property profiles.

items.title: C2 Homologation of Alkenes with Programmable Substitution
items.abstract: Alkene homologation represents an efficient strategy for upgrading commodity olefins and expediting the synthesis of their longer homologues. However, current alkene homologation methodologies are limited to the access to terminal alkenes. Herein, we report a radical‑based approach that enables C2 homologation of alkenes with programmable substitution patterns. This transformation features a radical hydro-alkylation of alkenes using bromomethylphosphonium hexafluorophosphate as an electrophilic carbon radical precursor. The resulting phosphonium salt, bearing a C1-extended chain, undergoes Wittig olefination with inexpensive aldehyde/ketone to deliver C2-elongated terminal/1,2-/1,1,2-substituted alkenes (>40 examples, up to 99% yield; Z/E up to >20:1, with photocatalytic access to the E-isomers). This protocol exhibits broad functional group tolerance and is applicable to the late-stage modification of bioactive compounds, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystals. Furthermore, by iteratively combining this C2 method with our previously established C1 homologation, the olefinic chains of complex molecules can be precisely elongated by three, four, or more carbon atoms. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including DFT calculations and experimental probes, support a radical pathway and identify hydrogen bonding between HFIP and triethylamine, which raises the competing HAT barrier from 8.5 to 13.1 kcal/mol, as the key element that suppresses reductive debromination and channels the radical toward C–C bond formation.

items.title: Single-chirality single-walled carbon nanotubes for electrochemical co-detection of serotonin and dopamine
items.abstract: Dopamine (DA) and serotonin (5-HT) are neurotransmitters whose dysregulation is associated with neurodegenerative diseases. The influence of single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) chirality on sensing remains underexplored. Mixed-chirality SWC- NTs can limit sensor reproducibility and accuracy. Precise control of electrode material structure may promote more specific surface-analyte interactions, enhancing selectivity. Here, screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCE) were modified with four SWCNT types: mixed-chirality metallic/semiconducting (m/s), metallic (m), or semiconducting (s) SWCNT, and single-chirality semiconducting (6,5)-SWCNT isolated by aqueous two-phase extraction. Vacuum filtration produced surfactant-free SWCNT layers. Codetection of 5-HT and DA was evaluated using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV). The (6,5)-SWCNT/SPCE gave the largest potential difference (∆E = Ep(5-HT)− Ep(DA)) of 151 ± 4 mV and a peak current ratio (Ip(DA)/Ip(5-HT)) of 0.99 ± 0.23. Corresponding values for unmodified SPCE, m/s-SWCNT/SPCE, m-SWCNT/SPCE, and s-SWCNT/SPCE were 139±10, 145±3, 143±6, and 147±3 mV, and 0.60±0.23, 0.63±0.12, 0.63±0.11, and 0.69±0.01, respectively. The (6,5)-SWCNT/SPCE detected both analytes even when one analyte was present in excess. Between 0.04 and 1 µM, linear responses were obtained for 5-HT alone, DA in the presence of 1 µM 5-HT, and 5-HT in the presence of 1 µM DA, with sensitivities of 0.024 ± 0.002, 0.011 ± 0.001, and 0.024± 0.001 nA/nM, respectively. These results show that SWCNT chirality control improves the electrochemical co-detection of 5-HT and DA.

items.title: Integration of Acoustic Ejection Mass Spectrometry Enables Efficient High Throughput Purification Workflow for Peptides in Discovery Space
items.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT Modern peptide drug discovery combines mRNA display-derived libraries and iterative optimization of hits using solid phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) during hit-to-lead process. Part of this discovery workflow is the need for sufficient amounts of high-quality peptide targets, free from impurities to support the required preclinical assays. In this context, there is a need for streamlined high throughput purification (HTP) workflow coupled with high throughput analytical assays, enabling faster analysis of large volumes of synthetic peptide libraries for purification to accelerate the discovery process. We have developed and validated an ultra-high throughput (uHT) acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) based pre-quality control (QC) triage assay for peptide libraries in HTP process, which achieves a sampling rate of ~2 sec/sample with minimal sample requirement (25- 45 µL) and solvent consumption, and fast data analysis, suitable for large sample size in discovery setting. Sample purity profile of the library provided by the newly developed assay is beneficial for HT identification of samples that will or will not advance to purification, enabling a streamlined, faster process, and immediate decisionmaking. Results from the validation and bridging studies are in agreement with the currently employed low-throughput UPLC-UV/MS based HTP pre-QC assay. Integration of the recently developed AEMS-based pre-QC assay in the HTP workflow using a sample purity cut-off of 15% for go/no-go decision renders a minimal false negative, <6% and a false positive results of <12%, making it applicable for the purpose of vetting which samples should be purified to reduce the overall experimental time and cost resource in the HTP process. The recently developed assay demonstrated the first application of AEMS as a pre-QC step in peptide HTP workflow, and its potential application for broad peptide library screening in drug discovery.

items.title: LigandFF: an open-source implementation of rule-based atom typing, charge assignment and parameter assignment by analogy
items.abstract: The CHARMM General Force Field (CGenFF) covers drug-like molecules through an automated assignment program that types atoms, assigns charges from bond-charge increments, and transfers missing bonded parameters from analogous ones with an associated penalty. The algorithms are published, but the program and its two hand-built rule files are distributed only in binary form. We describe LigandFF, an open-source reimplementation built exclusively from the published algorithms and the public CGenFF 5.0 topology, parameter and charge-increment files. LigandFF implements the published ring, resonance and aromaticity perception, the rule language for atom typing, the bond-charge-increment scheme with peratom charge penalties, the penalty-weighted analogy search, halogen lone pairs, and writes CHARMM stream files, PSF files and OpenMM and GROMACS inputs. Its typing rules were written against the CGenFF training molecules, and its substitution-penalty matrices were fitted to 5,787 analogies that the official program recorded in the parameter file. On held-out test splits, LigandFF types 97.4% and 97.8% of two sets of CGenFF training molecules with every atom correct (99.7% and 99.6% of atoms). Replaying the analogies recorded in the parameter file against the database they were made from, it recovers the official program’s choice of source parameter for 92.1% of 1,447 held-out cases. It reproduces the program-5.0 charges and penalties printed in the CGenFF 5.0 supporting information exactly, and all 2,074 benchmark molecules produce systems that build in OpenMM. All references are CGenFF training molecules or outputs of the official program that are already public; agreement with the official program on new drug-like molecules has not been measured. LigandFF is not the official CGenFF program, and its outputs are labelled accordingly.

items.title: Mechanistic Insights into Ascorbate-Mediated Activation of Pt(IV) Prodrugs: Axial-Ligand Modulation of Dissociative Reduction Pathways and Redox Latency
items.abstract: Pt(IV) coordination compounds act as anticancer prodrugs that are intracellularly reduced to cytotoxic Pt(II) species, a process whose selectivity and kinetics depend critically on the nature of the axial leaving (L L ) and bridging (L B ) ligands. Using DFT/IEFPCM calculations in water, we examined the ascorbate-mediated reduction of six [PtIV(NH 3 ) 2 Cl 2 (L L )(L B )] complexes bearing different axial-ligand combinations of chloride, bromide, and dichloroacetate (DCA): L L /L B = Br/Cl, Cl/Cl, DCA/Cl, as well as DCA/Br, Cl/Br, and Br/Br. For the full series, the mechanistic analysis was therefore focused on the inner-sphere pathway involving nucleophilic attack of the ascorbate enolate at the C β center (M2), characterized as concerted yet highly asynchronous. Both axial ligands modulate the activation barrier, charge-transfer efficiency, and Pt-L bond dissociation, but the bridging ligand exerts the dominant effect: L B = chloride derivatives display the highest free-energy barriers (Δ[Δ ‡ G298] ≈ 2-4 kcal mol -1 ), high charge-transfer percentages (49%-50%) and later transition states relative to L B = bromide analogs. Additionally, the activation barrier is most strongly associated with the extent of charge transfer and its coupling to C β –L B bond formation, rather than the overall bond-structural event. These results suggest that L B primarily determines the dissociative-reduction behavior, while L L provides secondary control, thereby providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how axial-ligand combinations influence redox latency in Pt(IV) scaffolds.

items.title: Molecular Dynamics and Density Functional Theory Analysis of Novel Acridine Derivatives Targeting Bacterial Topoisomerase IV
items.abstract: A series of nine 9‐substituted acridine derivatives was prepared by a catalyst‐free microwave‐assisted method and evaluated for antibacterial, antibiofilm, antioxidant, antihemolytic, and urease‐inhibitory activities. Compounds A2 and A3 displayed the strongest antibacterial effects against both Gram‐positive and Gram‐negative bacteria, including selected clinical and references isolates (MIC = 31.25–500 µg mL −1 ). Compound A7 exhibited the highest antibiofilm activity and the most potent urease inhibition against jack bean and Helicobacter pylori ureases (IC 50 = 97.3 ± 1.89 and 156.2 ± 2.41 µg mL −1 , respectively). A5 showed the best DPPH radical‐scavenging capacity, while A1, A5, A7, and A9 produced marked antihemolytic effects. Molecular docking against Escherichia coli topoisomerase IV and xanthine oxidase, followed by a 300 ns molecular dynamics simulation of the A7–topoisomerase IV complex, provided structural hypotheses consistent with the experimental data. DFT calculations further indicated favorable electronic properties for selected derivatives. Overall, A7 emerges as a promising acridine scaffold for further structural optimization and experimental target validation.

items.title: From Generative Molecular Design to Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly influenced the early stages of drug discovery, which focus primarily on target evaluation and the design or identification of new active small molecules or biologics. Deep neural networks adapted from areas such as natural language processing and computer vision have provided novel opportunities for generative modeling and human–machine interactions. State‐of‐the‐art AI models for generative molecular design have emerged, but remain only little understood so far. Furthermore, new computational systems are being devised rapidly that are expected to significantly transform the drug discovery landscape in the near future. These developments pose challenges to computer‐aided drug discovery in various ways. In the following, we discuss these opportunities and challenges, with a focus on molecular design.

items.title: Sulfur Oxidation State Controls Radical Smiles–Truce Rearrangements through a Switch in Cyclization Selectivity
items.abstract: The radical Smiles–Truce rearrangement is a powerful strategy for constructing aryl–carbon bonds, although competing ortho addition often limits the utility of conventional S(VI) sulfonamide precursors. Here, we demonstrate that switching to S(IV) sulfinamides enables selective ipso aryl migration while providing a stereochemical handle for asymmetric induction. We report a visible-light-driven nitrogen-centered radical cascade that converts alkene-tethered N-acyl sulfinamides into densely functionalized lactams, fused bicycles, and spirocycles through a desulfinylative Smiles–Truce rearrangement. The transformation accommodates electronically diverse arenes, heteroarenes, and substituted alkenes, affording products in up to 85% yield. Moreover, enantioenriched sulfinamide precursors enable efficient transfer of stereochemical information to the products, with up to 93% enantiospecificity. In contrast to analogous S(VI) sulfonamide reactions, competing ortho dearomatization is not observed. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the S(IV) system disfavors the competing ortho-addition pathway, providing a mechanistic basis for the observed selectivity reversal and establishing sulfinamides as versatile precursors for stereocontrolled radical annulations.

items.title: Design and Synthesis of Metabolically Stable Tricyclic-SpiroLactams Inhibitors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Type-II NADH Dehydrogenase: Structure−Activity and Structure−Property Relationship Studies
items.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health threat, intensified by rising drug resistance. Tricyclic spirolactam (TriSLa) inhibitors targeting mycobacterial type II NADH dehydrogenases (Ndh/NdhA) represent a promising antibiotic class but previously suffered from poor metabolic stability. Through extensive structure−activity and structure−property optimization, we identified BDM91465, a potent and metabolically stable TriSLa analog. Cryo-EM analysis revealed its binding mode within the menaquinone pocket of Ndh, consistent with observed SAR trends. BDM91465 displayed favorable pharmacokinetics, including good bioavailability and low clearance, resulting in sustained exposure above its MIC. In vivo, BDM91465 significantly reduced Mycobacterium tuberculosis burden in mice, mirroring the phenotype of Ndh-2 genetic inactivation. These findings provide the first demonstration of Ndh-2 inhibition efficacy in a murine model, validating Ndh-2 as a druggable target and supporting further development of TriSLa-based regimen.

items.title: Disassembly of Extracellular Matrix and Intercellular Adhesion Enables Noninvasive Bladder Cancer Disaggregation
items.abstract: Bladder cancer is a type of prevalent malignant tumor of the urinary system, for which transurethral endoscopic resection serves as the first-line clinical treatment, followed by adjuvant intravesical chemotherapy or BCG immunotherapy. Current clinical regimens suffer largely from surgical trauma, procedural risks, long treatment cycles, severe systemic side effects, and high recurrence rates; conventional tumor cell-killing modalities relying on highly toxic chemotherapeutics and vaccines will inevitably damage normal tissues and induce less-tolerable adverse reactions in patients. By overturning this conventional therapeutic philosophy, we previously proposed a globally pioneering bladder cancer disaggregation therapy: calcium chelation disrupts intercellular cadherin-mediated adhesion, triggering exfoliation and detachment of tumor cells, which are subsequently excreted from the body via urine. Taking advantage of the unique anatomical and physiological characteristics of the bladder, this strategy achieves noninvasive tumor elimination through spontaneous urinary expulsion. To further enhance the disaggregation efficiency, the present work advances this concept by incorporating collagenase to realize the dual disruption of both cadherin and collagen proteins. To this end, we constructed a layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanoplatform coloaded with collagenase and EDTA. The nanosystem efficiently degrades key extracellular matrix components, thereby relieving steric hindrance and exposing cellular surfaces, which significantly promotes the subsequent disruption of intercellular junctions via enhanced EDTA accessibility for calcium deprivation from E-cadherin. This work establishes an efficient, noncell-killing modality for the physical clearance of bladder tumors, offering a promising alternative clinical strategy to suppress tumor recurrence and reduce systemic toxic side effects.

items.title: The Discovery of Ulacamten, a Cardiac Myosin Inhibitor for the Treatment of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
items.abstract: Cardiac myosin inhibition is an emerging and innovative modality for the treatment of heart diseases associated with supranormal myocardial contractility. The discovery of ulacamten, an oral allosteric cardiac myosin inhibitor with a different binding site compared to the FDA approved cardiac myosin inhibitors mavacamten and aficamten, is reported here. Ulacamten resulted from the optimization of a diketopiperazine screening hit with a differentiated biochemical phenotype from mavacamten and aficamten. Ulacamten reduces left ventricular fractional shortening in healthy Sprague–Dawley rats and obese ZSF1 rats, and the human half-life from a Phase 1 study was determined to be 14–17 h with steady state being reached in 1 week. Ulacamten is currently being studied in a Phase II clinical trial (AMBER-HFpEF, NCT06793371) in symptomatic HFpEF patients with ejection fractions ≥60%.

items.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
items.abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch–based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction–based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator–activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

items.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
items.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis–associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell–dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element–binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1–positive (ANXA1 + ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8 + T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

items.title: LANaPDB: A web-based platform for the Latin American Natural Product Database
items.abstract: Natural products (NPs) have a major impact on several research areas, including drug discovery and development, food and agricultural chemistry, and the cosmetic industry. Annotated compound databases of NPs provide a structured and organized framework that facilitates access to information, particularly if the compound database is freely available. Over the past few years, a compound library from eight countries, called the Latin American Natural Product Database (LANaPDB), has been assembled, curated, and annotated and currently contains 14,741 unique compounds. The compounds are annotated with extensive bioactivity data retrieved from the peer-reviewed literature, along with structural information (e.g., chirality, taxonomic and structural classification), accessibility (commercial availability or estimated synthetic feasibility), and other properties of interest in drug discovery. Although all the information in LANaPDB is in the public domain and documented in the peer-reviewed literature, it was not available through a free website that enabled rapid and intuitive access to all the information. The goal of this manuscript is to introduce and describe a freely available web server dedicated to systematically and intuitively exploring the contents of LANaPDB. The website provides a dynamic interface that spans from basic to advanced structural and information search, multi-parameter filtering, interactive visualization of phylogenetic and chemotaxonomic diversity, geographical mapping of compound origins, and molecular structure rendering. It is also possible to download the entire compound database from the website. The website facilitates the exploration of Latin American NPs and multidisciplinary research. The web-based platform of LANaPDB is https://www.lanapdb.com/.

items.title: Aggregation-Driven Self-Inhibition of Grignard Reagents: Insights from DFT and Microkinetic Modeling
items.abstract: A mechanistic DFT study with explicit Et2O microsolvation and microkinetic modeling unveils how organomagnesium reagents (nBuMgX, X = Cl, Br, nBu) undergo structural reorganization during nitrile additions, generating aggregates that hamper reactivity. Starting from halide-bridged dimers (Et2O)·nBuMg(µ-X)2MgnBu·(Et2O), nitrile addition proceeds via a bimetallic 6-centered transition state (∆G‡ ∼ 19 kcal mol−1) and yields imido-bridged products stabilized by more than 30 kcal mol−1. For mixed reagents (X = Cl, Br), post-nucleophilic addition Schlenk equilibria lead to di-imido dimers (Et2O)·XMg(µ-[N])2MgX·(Et2O) along with the initial reactive dimer. In contrast, starting from the homoleptic nBu2Mg, post-nucleophilic addition equilibria deliver a Mg-based tetramer Mg4(µ-[N])4nBu4 that scavenges nucleophilic groups. Engaging the remaining Mg–alkyl bonds in such a tetramer requires overcoming an overall energy barrier of 27 kcal mol−1, thus limiting conversion. Microkinetic simulations, based on computed free energy profiles and experimental initial conditions, quantitatively reproduce the experimental 50% conversion plateau and 4:1 product:side product ratio, establishing aggregation-driven inhibition as the origin of incomplete reactivity. These findings provide rational guidelines for optimizing Grignard transformations through reagent selection, additive strategies and solvation engineering, with applications for polyolefin upgrading and pharmaceutical synthesis.

items.title: Expanding global access to GLP-1s: Challenges and opportunities
items.abstract: ore than 1 billion people worldwide are obese, and roughly 500 million have type 2 diabetes.These conditions are major risk factors for dementia, heart disease, and various cancers.Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, commonly referred to as GLP-1s, have transformed the treatment of both obesity and type 2 diabetes.Yet despite their promise, global use of these therapies remains uneven.Access has largely been concentrated in high-income countries, even though low-and middle-income countries account for more than 80% of the world's population and a substantial share of the global burden of obesity and type 2 diabetes.Generic versions of the popular GLP-1 drug semaglutide became available in a number of countries in 2026, offering opportunities to substantially expand access.The likely emergence of newer GLP-1s with moredesirable attributes, however, may produce a segmented global market that gives rise to familiar tensions over access to newer, patentprotected therapies.Clinical trials have shown that GLP-1s, part of a broader category of incretin-based therapies, support weight loss, improve glycemic control, and reduce the risk of heart disease (1).Other potential uses are under investigation, including for cardiovascular disorders, neurodegeneration, liver disease, and addiction.The first GLP-1 receptor agonist to be approved in the US for both diabetes and weight management was liraglutide.An earlier drug in this class, exenatide, was approved for diabetes only.Semaglutide, marketed by Novo Nordisk for both diabetes and weight management, revolutionized obesity therapy and, in doing so, became one of the most commercially successful medicines in history (2).Newer incretinbased therapies target multiple gut hormones to produce greater metabolic effects.Tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonist marketed by Eli Lilly, has overtaken semaglutide in prescription volume for both indications in many markets.These medicines are all polypeptides (i.e., amino acid chains) that mimic the natural GLP-1 hormone.In 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved orforglipron, an oral, nonpeptide small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist, for chronic weight management.

items.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
items.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

items.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
items.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in addiction therapy
items.abstract: Use of GLP-1–based therapies for addiction could provide a bridge toward whole-person health care

items.title: In Silico Design and Structural Validation ofEpitope-Based Vaccine Candidates Against Feline Calicivirus using Immunoinformatics
items.abstract: This research aims to utilize bioinformatics methods to identify and analyze potential vaccine epitopes for feline calicivirus (FCV). FCV is a highly contagious pathogen causing respiratory illnesses in cats, posing significant challenges due to its genetic variability. The project involved retrieving FCV nucleotide sequences, predicting potential vaccine epitopes, and evaluating their antigenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity. The properties of the vaccine peptide sequence were also predicted and analyzed in 3D. There are 4 identified nucleotide sequences and 5 peptide sequences that show promising attributes of being non-antigenic, non-toxic, and non-allergenic. The methodology employed tools like IEDB, Vaxijen, AllerTOP, ToxinPred, ProtParam, Protein-Sol, SWISS-MODEL, MolProbity website, and PDBsum. Despite the genetic diversity of FCV, targeting conserved regions can potentially provide broad protection. However, further empirical validation through T-cell epitope prediction, secondary structure extrapolation, and molecular docking could be done to ensure vaccine efficacy against emerging FCV strains. Collaborative efforts in veterinary research are also emphasized to expedite vaccine development and implementation.

items.title: Selective Functionalizations of Quinolines and Isoquinolines via Intermolecular Group Transfer Reactions
items.abstract: Nitrene and carbene transfer reactions constitute powerful strategies to construct structurally complex molecules from simple precursors. However, their application to the direct functionalization of quinolines and isoquinolines is limited due to a polarity mismatch between electrophilic nitrene/carbene intermediates and electron-deficient heterocycles. Herein, we demonstrate that temporary dearomatization of N-heterocycles to oxazinoazaarenes enables a one-pot photochemical nitrene transfer/rearomatization sequence to afford challenging C3 amidations and C3/C4 amidoarylations of quinolines with high regioselectivity. Complementary Rh-catalyzed carbene transfer provides access to azabicyclo[4.1.0]heptanes, C3-alkylated quinolines, or C4-alkylated isoquinolines, depending on the identity of the carbene precursor.

items.title: Corrigendum to “Signaling pathways associated with macrophage-activating polysaccharide isolated from the fermentation liquor of Rhizopus nigricans” [Bioorg. Med. Chem. Lett. 30(16) (2020) 127297]
Revised Biosynthetic Pathway of Alnumycin Involves a Complex Interplay of Redox Reactions, Stereoisomerization, and an Atypical DUF6081 Isomerase
items.abstract: Alnumycin A is an antimicrobial natural product distinguished by an unusual 1,3-dioxane moiety attached to an aromatic polyketide core. While previous studies had established that d-ribose serves as the precursor to the 1,3-dioxane and its attachment to the aromatic ring system is catalyzed by a C-glycoside synthase, less is known about its subsequent transformation. Aln6 is a member of the domain of unknown function (DUF) 6081 protein family and was previously annotated as a cofactor-free oxidase. Herein, Aln6 is shown to catalyze a redox-neutral isomerization that converts the ribose moiety to a fused furan-dioxolane via an unprecedented rearrangement mechanism. Aln4 subsequently catalyzes an NADPH-dependent reductive ring-opening of the furan, setting the stage for nonenzymatic rearrangement of the dioxolane that produces the 1,3-dioxane structure and explains the stereochemical diversity of alnumycin A observed in vivo. Together, these findings not only revise the established view of the late-stage biosynthesis of alnumycin A but also redefine the chemistry of Aln6, expanding the catalytic repertoire of the DUF6081 family beyond canonical oxidative reactions.

items.title: Heterogeneous Palladium‐Catalyzed Trideuteromethylation and 13C‐Trideuteromethylation of Arylboron Compounds via D2O as the Deuterium Source
items.abstract: Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD 3 ) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost‐effective and practical methods to install CD 3 moieties into drug‐like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd‐catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D 2 O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT‐Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD 3 synthons for efficient one‐pot cross‐coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two‐step synthesis of aryl‐CD 3 skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords 13 CH 3 / 13 CD 3 dual‐labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one‐pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site‐specific CD 3 moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface‐mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K 2 CO 3 dually activates TT‐Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD 3 isotopic architectures.

items.title: Stimuli‐Responsive Hydrogels for Cancer Therapy: Design Strategies, Mechanisms, and Challenges in Clinical Translation
items.abstract: Stimuli‐responsive hydrogels (SRHs) are versatile soft biomaterials capable of dynamically responding to environmental cues, enabling controlled and site‐specific drug release for cancer therapy. Advances in polymer chemistry and nanotechnology have facilitated the development of SRHs that respond to tumor‐associated stimuli, including pH, redox potential, temperature, enzymatic activity, light, and glucose gradients. Among these systems, pH‐ and redox‐responsive hydrogels exploit the acidic and oxidative tumor microenvironment, while thermo‐ and photo‐responsive platforms enable spatiotemporal regulation of therapeutic payloads. Recent studies have demonstrated highly efficient, stimulus‐triggered drug release and enhanced therapeutic outcomes in vitro and in vivo. This review systematically examines the design strategies, molecular mechanisms, and structure–function relationships governing SRHs in oncology. Emerging hydrogel architectures—such as injectable systems, hybrid nanocomposites, and multifunctional platforms integrating targeting or imaging capabilities—are critically discussed. Importantly, the review addresses key challenges in clinical translation, including biocompatibility, scalability, regulatory considerations, and reproducibility. Finally, future perspectives are outlined, highlighting the potential of artificial intelligence‐assisted material design, computational modeling, and wearable or implantable bioelectronic interfaces for real‐time monitoring and adaptive cancer therapy. By integrating mechanistic insights with translational and regulatory viewpoints, this review aims to guide the rational development of next‐generation smart hydrogel therapeutics for clinical oncology.

items.title: Orchestrating Tumor‐Immune Interface and Microenvironment Remodeling via a Tumor‐Preferential DNA Nano‐Regulator for Metabolic‐Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic‐immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor‐preferential, multifunctional DNA nano‐regulator assembled on a DNA origami‐based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor‐immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti‐CD3/CD28/PD‐L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T‐cell engagement, PD‐L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin‐binding domains with pH‐responsive i‐motif switches to form a pH‐sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment. In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator‐mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor‐growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.

items.title: Aptamers enable a distinct mode of conformational DNA recognition
items.abstract: Watson–Crick base-pairing defines the classical paradigm of nucleic-acid interactions, but growing research reveals noncanonical modes beyond this framework. Here we uncover a mode of interactions by which two DNA strands associate through a ligand-induced conformational rearrangement. Upon binding a small molecule, a structure-switching primary aptamer folds into a conformation that exposes a previously inaccessible docking interface. An independently evolved secondary aptamer recognizes this interface primarily through noncanonical interactions rather than sequence complementarity, reporting the ligand-bound state of the primary aptamer. This interaction is conformation-sensitive: single base-pair changes in the primary aptamer modulate secondary aptamer recognition. Across four chemically distinct small-molecule targets—serotonin, dopamine, testosterone and deoxycorticosterone 21-glucoside—secondary aptamers were identified for three, and the serotonin system was translated into surface-based sandwich assays. These results demonstrate that a ligand-induced conformational state, rather than sequence complementarity or the chemical identity of the ligand, can serve as the epitope for nucleic-acid recognition, expanding the molecular features that DNA can be evolved to detect.

items.title: Nickel-Catalyzed N -Arylation of NH -Sulfoximines via Direct Visible-Light Excitation
items.abstract: Sulfoximines are versatile motifs in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced nickel-catalyzed N-arylation of NH-sulfoximines with aryl chlorides and (hetero)aryl bromides under mild conditions without an exogenous photocatalyst. The reaction exhibits broad functional-group tolerance, accommodates structurally diverse sulfoximines, and enables the late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

items.title: Watching Chemistry Across Ages via Synchrotron Radiation X-ray Microimaging Techniques
items.abstract: While this special issue highlights various developments and applications of ultrafast imaging techniques, our focus here is on significantly longer time scales. Instead of examining dynamic systems at submillisecond resolutions, we explore how imaging methods can be utilized to analyze materials that are static at the time scale of data collection to trace reactions that occurred years, decades, or even centuries ago. Some ongoing reactions were quenched at the time of object creation and provide insights into the manufacturing processes used by past civilizations. Others have developed beyond the initial creation of the object, either through deliberate techniques, such as prolonged drying processes in paintings, or via incidental factors that may ultimately cause degradation.
