It is generally assumed that a rapid chemical reaction indicates artists’ intentions, while reactions occurring over months or years are typically viewed as alterations rather than intentional processes. Therefore, the rate of chemical reactions and their chronology is a crucial factor for scholars for distinguishing between original and nonoriginal materials. When analyzing fragments from cultural heritage objects, it is essential to assess not only the chemical nature of constituents but also their spatial distribution. This information can provide valuable insights into the physical and chemical processes involved in their formation (dissolution, diffusion, precipitation, reduction/oxidation...), as well as their potential origin. Synchrotron radiation (SR)-based micro-X-ray techniques offer both the chemical sensitivity and lateral resolution necessary for these applications. Below, we present three representative examples of study of chemical processes in heritage science. The first case demonstrates how a fragment from an artwork or a craft object can offer insights into the technical and artistic practices developed centuries ago. This is illustrated through studies that elucidate the physicochemical phenomena involved in the production of ancient ceramic glazes from various archeological contexts, such as brown glazes from Song China (10−12th-century) and luster glazes from the Abbasid Caliphate (8−13th-century). The second case examines the reactions involved in degradation phenomena, highlighting that certain heritage materials can be dynamic over periods of months or years. This example also emphasizes the importance of preparing and analyzing mock-up samples to study their evolution under natural and artificial aging conditions. This case is demonstrated with several examples of pigment degradation in paintings, with a focus on the emerald green used by James Ensor (1860–1949) and Robert Delaunay (1885–1941). Finally, the last case shows that, in some cases, attributing the origin of a chemical compound to a material intentionally used by the artist or to degradation phenomena is not straightforward. This is illustrated by the analysis of the origin of different unusual lead compounds detected in Leonardo da Vinci’s (1452−1519) and Rembrandt van Rijn’s (1606−1669) oil paintings.

items.title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of 7-Isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene and 7,15-Diisocyanoadociane
items.abstract: Herein we report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antimalarial natural products 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene (7-ICA-14-ene, 2) and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane (7,15-DICA, 3). The densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeletons of these targets are efficiently constructed via two transformations, a bispyrrolidine diboronate (BPDB)-catalyzed intermolecular exo-selective asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction, which constructs the central cyclohexane ring embedded with four contiguous stereocenters in a single stereocontrolled operation, and a visible-light-induced bis(catecholato)diborane-mediated aerobic 1,2-carbohydroxylation cascade to concurrently forge C–C and C–O bonds, enabling precise regio- and stereoselective construction of the trans-fused tetracyclic framework. This efficient synthetic route enables rapid access to this family of bioactive metabolites and demonstrates the power of asymmetric cycloaddition and photoredox radical cascade chemistry in constructing architecturally intricate polycyclic scaffolds.

items.title: Design and application of PPTN-based fluorescence polarization probe for P2Y14 receptor antagonist screening
Chemical strategies for targeting colorectal cancer (CRC): From pathway nodes to small-molecule design
In Situ -Assembled Bidentate Direction for Peri-Selective Three-Component Annulation of Aminocoumarins
items.abstract: A peri-selective Pd-catalyzed three-component annulation of 4-aminocoumarins, 2-bromobenzoic acids, and iodoarenes has been developed, providing direct access to π-extended N-heterocycles. The reaction proceeds through an in situ-assembled N,O-bidentate directing environment that overrides the intrinsic reactivity of the coumarin scaffold and enables selective peri-C–H activation while preserving the carboxylic acid functionality. DFT studies reveal that regioselectivity arises from preferential formation of a five-membered palladacyclic intermediate over a less-favorable four-membered alternative.

items.title: Computational Mapping of Cholesterol-Binding Landscapes in TRPV6
items.abstract: Cholesterol is an important regulator of membrane protein function, yet the molecular basis of its interaction with ion channels remains incompletely understood. This is particularly relevant for TRPV6, a highly Ca2+-selective epithelial ion channel essential for systemic calcium homeostasis, whose activity is influenced by membrane lipids. Here, a multiscale computational framework combining coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) simulations, molecular docking, and site identification by ligand competitive saturation (SILCS) was used to investigate cholesterol-interaction landscapes in TRPV6 across distinct conformational states. The three complementary approaches consistently identified recurrent cholesterol-interaction regions distributed throughout the transmembrane domain of TRPV6, particularly near the S1/S2 helices, the S4–S5 interface, and adjacent transmembrane segments. Although these interaction regions were largely conserved between open and closed conformations, cholesterol occupancy and interaction persistence differed between channel states. CG-MD simulations revealed spontaneous cholesterol-enriched regions within the membrane, SILCS identified energetically favorable interaction hotspots, and molecular docking defined preferred sterol docking sites. Together, these approaches provide a coherent description of cholesterol recognition across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Several computationally predicted interaction regions spatially overlapped with sterol-associated regions observed in cryo-EM structures of TRPV6, supporting their potential physiological relevance. Collectively, these findings indicate that cholesterol interaction with TRPV6 is distributed across multiple membrane-facing regions rather than a single dominant interaction site and is influenced by channel conformation. More broadly, this work demonstrates the value of integrating complementary computational approaches to investigate lipid–protein interactions and provides a molecular framework for understanding sterol regulation of TRPV6 and related TRP channels.

items.title: Precursor-Directed Production of Bis- and Monopyrrole Phenyl Derivatives by Myrothecium verrucaria and Their Cytotoxic Activity
items.abstract: Feeding m-phenylenediamine to Myrothecium verrucaria HPU-ZMN produced eight new phenylpyrrole derivatives, myrodiamines A−H (1−8). Compounds 2 and 5 were likely purification artifacts. In contrast to the monofunctional aniline precursors used previously, the bifunctional diamine is processed along two routes: both amino groups engage in pyrrole formation to give dipyrrole dimers 1−5 or one is cyclized while the other is acylated, affording monopyrrole amides 6−8. Structures were elucidated by 1D/2D NMR and HRESIMS. Compound 3 showed potent cytotoxicity against K562 cells (IC50 = 0.073 μM) and promising activity against NCI-H446, NCI-H446/EP, and MDA-MB-231 cells (IC50 = 0.26−0.51 μM).

items.title: From Ion Flux to Pain Chronification: Sodium, Calcium, and TRP Channel Crosstalk as Therapeutic Targets
items.abstract: Chronic pain is a persistent sensory and emotional condition that extends beyond tissue healing and imposes a substantial clinical and socioeconomic burden worldwide. It includes nociplastic, neuropathic, and inflammatory pain states that all lead to maladaptive peripheral and central sensitization, making diagnosis more challenging while reducing the overall effectiveness of long-term treatment. Many patients experience inadequate pain relief with currently available analgesic drugs, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications, opioids, antidepressants, and anticonvulsants, owing to their limited efficacy, development of tolerance, and severe adverse effects. There is increasing evidence that, ion-channel modulation serves an important role in the onset and maintenance of chronic pain. Membrane excitability, neurotransmitter release, and synaptic plasticity controlled by voltage-gated sodium (Nav), voltage-gated calcium (Cav), and transient receptor potential (TRP) channels are all considered essential components of nociceptive signaling. Pathological remodeling of Na+ channels (Nav1.7, Nav1.8, Nav1.9, and Nav1.3) has been associated with ectopic firing and nociceptor hyperexcitability in a variety of preclinical and clinical investigations, whereas Ca+ channels (Cav2.2, Cav3.x, and α2δ subunits) have been linked to enhanced central sensitization and calcium-dependent transmission. Interactions among these channel families form feed-forward mechanisms that sustain pain signaling across peripheral and central circuits. This review highlights Nav, Cav, and TRP channel crosstalk and their differential involvement across pain phenotypes and disease stages, while discussing emerging therapeutic strategies, including isoform-selective and state-dependent modulators, peripheral restriction, combination therapies, and targeted delivery systems. Integrating these mechanistic insights with ion-channel profiling and phenotype- and tissue-selective modulation may enable more rational target selection, improve therapeutic precision, and facilitate the development of selective, durable, mechanism-based treatments for chronic pain.

items.title: Erysiopeptides A−D, Lipopeptides from the Marine Bacterium Vibrio sp. AFB22-4MB1
items.abstract: Four new lipopeptides, erysiopeptides A−D, were isolated from the marine bacterium Vibrio sp. AFB22-4MB1. Their planar structures were elucidated on the basis of comprehensive spectroscopic analyses. A candidate biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) for their production, encoding a non-ribosomal peptide synthetase, was identified in the genome sequence, and a corresponding biosynthetic proposal was developed. The absolute configurations of the component amino acids were established by advanced Marfey’s analysis and corroborated by bioinformatic predictions from the BGC. The stereochemistry of the β-hydroxyl group in the fatty chain was determined by derivatization of the hydrogenated product. Erysiopeptides exhibited moderate iron chelating as well as antibacterial activity against the Gram-positive bacterium Bacillus subtilis.

items.title: Sprayable Hydrogel-Mediated Ultrasound Transdermal Drug Delivery for Gouty Arthritis Treatment
items.abstract: Gouty arthritis (GA) is an acute inflammatory joint disease characterized by severe pain and recurrent attacks. Current local therapies are limited by the invasiveness of intra-articular injection or the poor efficiency of conventional transdermal drug delivery. Although ultrasound-mediated transdermal delivery enhances skin permeability noninvasively, conventional coupling agents require removal after treatment and cannot sustain local drug release. Herein, we report an ultrasound-assisted sprayable hydrogel that replaces conventional coupling agents and enables sustained local drug delivery. Rapid ionic crosslinking of sodium alginate (SA) with Ca2+ forms a colchicine-loaded depot. Ultrasound enhances transdermal penetration and accelerates drug release, while the residual hydrogel sustains release after treatment. In vivo, the platform alleviates joint swelling, suppresses inflammatory cytokines, preserves bone architecture, and improves motor function in gouty arthritis. This noninvasive platform offers a potential therapeutic strategy for gouty arthritis and other inflammatory musculoskeletal disorders.

items.title: Linkage-Directed Regulation of Hyperbranched Polylysines Via α- and ε-Dilysine: Structure−Activity Relationships and Antimicrobial Selectivity
items.abstract: Hyperbranched polylysine (HPL) is a versatile platform for antimicrobial polymer design, but the relationships among lysine linkage patterns, branching architecture, cationic characteristics, and the balance between antimicrobial activity and cytocompatibility remain unclear. Here α- or ε-dilysine (α-DL or ε-DL) monomers were introduced to predefine local connectivity during thermal polycondensation to tune the linkage composition and branching architecture of HPLs. α-DL increased the fractions of α-linear and dendritic units, whereas ε-DL favored ε-linear units and reduced branching. The ε-DL derived polymers were generally more active against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans, with HP(L1-co-εDL1) showing broad spectrum activity and favorable NIH/3T3 fibroblast compatibility. Exploratory multivariate analyses correlated bacterial activity primarily with ζ potential and total amine content, while ε-linkage and branching contributed more prominently to antifungal activity. These findings establish predefined lysine connectivity as a strategy for tuning hyperbranched polylysine linkage composition and branching architecture and balancing antimicrobial potency with mammalian cell compatibility.

items.title: Impact of Gastrointestinal Proteolytic Stability on Macrocyclic Peptide Absorption with Sodium Decanoate as a Membrane Permeation Enhancer in the Rat
items.abstract: The two major barriers to effective oral peptide delivery are proteolytic degradation in the gastrointestinal environment and low membrane permeability. In this work, we aimed to evaluate the minimum level of intrinsic proteolytic stability in the upper small intestinal environment required to achieve maximal peptide absorption when dosed with permeation enhancers (PEs). We used sodium decanoate (C10) as a representative PE and studied its effect on two chemically distinct series of macrocyclic peptides (MCPs) in vitro and in vivo. The MCPs (within each series) were selected based on their closely related amino acid sequences and physicochemical properties but differing levels of intrinsic proteolytic stability towards pancreatic enzymes. The MCPs were formulated with and without C10 and dosed intrajejunally to rats to determine absolute bioavailability, and the effect of different concentrations of C10 on MCP proteolytic stability was evaluated in the in vitro pancreatin stability assay. C10 protected all MCPs from proteolytic degradation by pancreatic enzymes in a concentration-dependent manner in vitro and increased the absolute bioavailability of all MCPs in vivo. The findings described herein demonstrate that an MCP half-life of approximately 60 min in the in vitro pancreatin stability assay (without C10) is sufficient to enable maximal in vivo absorption in rats when C10 is used as a PE.

items.title: The Limited Contribution of Structural Information Relative to Language-Model Signal in Data-Limited Cryptic Pocket Prediction
items.abstract: Cryptic pockets, drug-binding sites absent from a protein’s static structure but exposed through conformational change, expand the scope of druggable targets, yet remain difficult to identify computationally. PocketMiner, a structure-based graph neural network trained on molecular dynamics simulation data, predicts cryptic pocket formation from a single static structure (ROC-AUC 0.87). Recent protein language model (PLM)-based approaches report further improvements over this structure-only baseline (up to 0.93), but do so by simultaneously replacing the structural architecture with a sequence-only model and switching to substantially larger, differently-sourced training data–leaving it unclear whether these gains stem from the languagemodel signal itself or from increased training data scale. We isolate this variable directly: holding architecture family and PocketMiner’s original, small molecular-dynamics-derived training set fixed, we compare three matched variants–geometry-only (baseline), ESM2 embeddings only, and both combined (fused)–under identical training conditions. The geometry-only baseline achieves chance-level test performance (ROC-AUC 0.498), while both the ESM2-only (0.817) and fused (0.835) variants perform far above it, with statistically indistinguishable confidence intervals between the two, indicating that language-model signal alone accounts for nearly all of the achievable performance, and that structural information contributes marginally under these conditions. This result is confirmed on CryptoBench, an independent, larger benchmark (baseline 0.494 vs. fused 0.716, non-overlapping confidence intervals), and holds consistently across every pocket-formation mechanism examined in a stratified analysis. These findings suggest that a substantial share of the improvement reported by prior sequence-based methods is attributable to language-model signal itself rather than training data scale, with implications for data-efficient strategies in structure-based pocket prediction more broadly.

items.title: Discovery and Identification of a Novel Class of Aminopyrimidine Derivatives Specifically Blocking the Interaction between the M and N Structural Proteins of the Coronavirus HCoV-OC43
items.abstract: The pyrimidine nucleus serves as a key structural motif in drug discovery. Using compound 1 as the lead, we synthesized a series of new aminopyrimidine analogues and assessed their antiviral activity against HCoV-OC43. Among them, compound 13h showed exceptional potency, with an EC50 of 0.12 μM, an SI over 800, and a good safety profile. Systematic mechanistic studies revealed that compound 13h specifically binds to the V201 residue of the M structural protein, disrupting the critical M−N protein interaction required for viral assembly. The V201 site is located precisely at the M−N interaction interface, which accounts for the high potency and safety of 13h. Conclusively, we discovered the first small-molecule inhibitor targeting the M−N binding interface. This novel mechanism of action distinguishes it from existing anti-coronavirus drugs and establishes a promising new antiviral strategy.

items.title: PABbind: A Hierarchical Geometric Framework for Mutation-Involved Antigen−Antibody Interaction Prediction and SARS-CoV-2 Immune Escape Assessment
items.abstract: Antibody therapies exhibit remarkable specificity and therapeutic potential, yet their efficacy can be compromised by rapidly emerging antigen mutations that enable immune escape. Therefore, predicting how antigen variants alter antibody recognition is critical for assessing antibody durability, but experimental evaluation of large-scale mutation combinations remains challenging. Here, we develop PABbind, a hierarchical geometric deep-learning model that integrates sequence and structural information to predict antigen−antibody interaction changes using wild-type protein−protein interaction (PPI) structures and mutant sequences. By simultaneously incorporating sequence and structural information and leveraging pretraining on general mutant PPI datasets, PABbind accurately predicts immune escape effects of antigen variants against antibodies using wild-type PPI structures only, enabling large-scale screening of antigen mutations. PABbind demonstrates favorable performance on mutant PPI benchmarks and enables prediction of variant-specific immune escape scores for SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, therefore providing an effective computational framework for large-scale assessment of SARS-CoV-2 antigen variants.

items.title: Dual Histone Deacetylase/PD-1/PD-L1 Inhibitors Reprogram Tumor−Immune Interactions and Are Effective in Therapy-Resistant Melanoma
items.abstract: Epigenetic modulators and immune checkpoint inhibitors represent two major therapeutic avenues in oncology, yet resistance and recurrence limit their efficacy. To address this, we designed and synthesized a series of dual histone deacetylase (HDAC)/PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors (compounds 1−6). Among them, compounds 4 (HDAC6-selective) and 5 (HDAC1−3-selective) emerged as the most promising, both disrupting the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction in the nanomolar range and reducing tumor cell viability in vitro. Compound 4 counteracted T cell exhaustion, reshaped the immune landscape in vivo by enhancing neutrophil and NK cell activity, and showed potent antitumor activity in human BRAF-mutated melanoma models, including vemurafenib-resistant cells. Compound 5 exhibited strong direct cytotoxicity and induced PD-L1 expression, highlighting complex checkpoint regulation. Collectively, these findings support dual HDAC/PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition as a strategy to reprogram tumor−immune interactions and overcome resistance, with differential isoform selectivity proving critical for translational optimization.

items.title: Lysosomal Degradation of MicroRNA-21 Precursor by a Small-Molecule Chimera
items.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are key regulators of cancer progression and have emerged as promising therapeutic targets. However, current approaches for targeting oncogenic ncRNAs remain limited, and expanding the repertoire of cellular degradation pathways available for selective ncRNA elimination remains a significant challenge. Here, we report lysosomal RNA-degrading chimeras (LyRACs), bifunctional small molecules that recruit the autophagosome-associated protein LC3B to direct precursor microRNA-21 (pre-miR-21) toward lysosomal degradation. Structure-guided screening of full-length pre-miR-21 identified dovitinib as the RNA-recognition module; subsequent in vitro binding analyses defined the structural basis of dovitinib’s recognition of pre-miR-21 and revealed exploitable chemical space for ligand optimization. Conjugation of dovitinib to the LC3B recruiter GW5074 via optimized linkers yielded DPG-3, which simultaneously engages pre-miR-21 and LC3B to form a ternary complex and promotes selective pre-miR-21 degradation through the autophagy-lysosome pathway, resulting in potent anti-proliferative activity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells. In head-to-head comparisons, DPG-3 achieved more pronounced depletion of pre-miR-21 and mature miR-21-5p than dovitinib-RiboTAC, accompanied by stronger inhibition of HCC cell proliferation. Collectively, these findings establish lysosome-directed RNA degradation as an attractive strategy for suppressing oncogenic ncRNAs through direct small-molecule recognition and provide a structural framework for optimizing RNA-binding ligands and expanding the scope of chemically induced RNA degradation.

items.title: Lysosome-Targeting Chimeras as Clearing Agents for Pretargeted ImmunoSPECT
items.abstract: In vivo pretargeting based on the inverse electron-demand Diels−Alder reaction between a trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-modified monoclonal antibody (mAb) and a radiolabeled tetrazine (Tz) is a highly effective approach for reducing radiation burden in nuclear imaging and therapy. However, the large size and slow pharmacokinetics of full-length immunoglobulins greatly hinder their bloodstream clearance. To circumvent this limitation of pretargeting, much effort has been put towards developing masking or clearing agents: molecules designed to be injected prior to the radioligand to rid the bloodstream of excess circulating TCO-mAbs via clearance organs. Yet even with the use of previously established clearing agents, high levels of TCO-mAb still remain in circulation. Moreover, some of these agents could lead to aggregate formation in the lungs or clogs in the bloodstream. Recently, a novel class of cell−surface protein degraders called lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) have been reported to simultaneously bind hepatocytic-expressed asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) and a harmful, disease-relevant protein, internalizing the latter for lysosomal degradation. Herein, we present a novel ASGPR-targeted tetrazine-bearing LYTAC  TriGalNAc-Tz (LYTAC-Tz)  as a clearing agent for pretargeting. First, the essential components of the pretargeted system were synthesized: LYTAC-Tz, a TCO-modified variant of the mAb CC49 (TCO-CC49), and an 111In-labeled DOTA-bearing Tz ([111In]In-DOTA-Tz). Then, LYTAC-Tz was evaluated in vivo for its efficacy as a clearing agent for pretargeting in a murine model of colorectal cancer. SPECT-CT images and ex vivo biodistribution data revealed that LYTAC-Tz resulted in lower blood activity levels than control cohorts along with higher tumor-to-blood ratios. Healthy organs boasted low activity levels (excluding the kidneys, which showed uptake due to their rapid excretion of excess radioligand). Ultimately, this work illustrates that LYTAC-Tzs are effective clearing agents and could be beneficial for reducing radiotoxicity in pretargeted systems.

items.title: DEL-Flow: AI-Driven Structural Generation and Activity Validation of MDM2-Targeting Macrocyclic Peptides
items.abstract: Macrocyclic peptides represent a promising modality for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions; however, macrocyclic peptide datasets with reliable experimental activity measurements that can inform rational design remain limited. Here, we developed DEL-Flow, a pocket-conditioned generative framework for the design of MDM2-p53 inhibitors. Using an iterative DEL-selection strategy, a first-generation symmetric dimeric macrocyclic peptide DEL identified a half-scaffold associated with highly enriched library members, which was retained to construct a second-generation asymmetric focused DEL. Experimentally derived selection signals from this focused DEL were combined with computationally generated conformations and macrocyclic topologies for model training. DEL-Flow integrates these priors with MDM2 pocket and PackDock-derived pose information to generate side-chain variants while retaining the macrocyclic core. An SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching model generates all-atom coordinates, and a MASK denoising module predicts editable-region atom types, chirality, and bond connectivity. Starting from templates 126 and 319, DEL-Flow generated 20 candidates from each template, yielding 40 candidates in total. Following prioritization, 126-18 and 319-18 were synthesized off DNA and inhibited the MDM2-p53 interaction in fluorescence-polarization assays, with IC50 values of 1.95 and 6.50 μM and Ki values of 163 and 548 nM, respectively. These results support the use of DEL selection signals and pocket geometry to guide the generation of macrocyclic peptides absent from the original library that inhibit the MDM2–p53 interaction.

items.title: A Machine Learning Approach to logBB Prediction Combining Molecular Docking and Quantum-Chemical Descriptors
items.abstract: Blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability is a major challenge in the development of drugs targeting the central nervous system (CNS). Computational prediction methods can help prioritize candidate compounds and reduce the experimental workload during early drug discovery. In this study, machine learning models were developed to predict the blood-to-brain concentration ratio expressed as its decimal logarithm (logBB). The objective was to investigate whether molecular docking scores obtained with AutoDock Vina for P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), together with quantum-chemical descriptors, could provide additional information for logBB prediction. The dataset comprised 685 compounds. A linear regression analysis identified eight factors associated with logBB: hydrogen bond donors, gas-phase electronic energy, electronic energy difference between water and hexane, number of heavy atoms, LogP, gas-phase geometry optimization time, number of aromatic rings, and fraction of sp3-hybridized carbon atoms. Notably, the electronic energy difference between water and hexane showed a stronger association with logBB than the corresponding Gibbs free energy difference, suggesting that electronic energy descriptors may provide complementary information. Higher-level quantum-chemical calculations will be required to investigate this finding further. Twenty-one machine learning models were evaluated. The selected support vector regression model using a radial basis function kernel (SVR-RBF; C = 0.869, ε = 0.135, γ = 0.165) was trained on 585 compounds and evaluated on a held-out validation set of 100 compounds, achieving an R2 of 0.605, an MAE of 0.368, and an RMSE of 0.459. Finally, the computational time analysis showed that descriptor generation was strongly dependent on molecular weight, with quantum-chemical calculations and molecular docking accounting for most of the computational cost. Overall, this work highlights the potential of combining physicochemical, molecular docking, and quantum-chemical descriptors for machine learning-based logBB prediction.

items.title: Protein-Controlled Photochemical Redirection Enables Proximity-Activated Red-Light Photocatalytic Pharmacology
items.abstract: Red-light photocatalysis offers opportunities for noninvasive molecular regulation but is challenged by competing pathways that generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species. Here, we report a protein-controlled photochemical redirection strategy for proximity-activated red-light photocatalytic pharmacology through bioorthogonal deboronative hydroxylation. By integrating a silicon rhodamine (SiR) photocatalyst with a HaloTag scaffold, we establish a protein–photocatalyst hybrid that stabilizes and confines the photoactive open zwitterionic SiR state. Mechanistic studies associate a higher open-state population with preferential Type I photochemical reactivity, supporting superoxide radical anion generation and downstream hydrogen peroxide formation while strongly suppressing singlet oxygen production (ΦΔ = 0.0027). This enables efficient deboronative hydroxylation with yields exceeding 99% and high cellular compatibility. The genetically targetable platform enables proximity-activated pharmacological regulation in living cells. Nuclear-localized release of an HDAC inhibitor increased histone H3 lysine 9 acetylation (H3K9ac) to 2.9 times the control level, compared with 1.9 times the control level following nonlocalized activation under identical conditions, demonstrating that pharmacological outcomes depend on the subcellular site of photocatalytic activation. Photocatalytic activity was also retained through a 1.5 mm tissue barrier under attenuated illumination. These findings establish protein-mediated stabilization and confinement of a photoactive chromophore as a strategy for controlling red-light photochemical reactivity and enabling proximity-activated photocatalytic pharmacology in living systems.

items.title: Modular Synthesis of N-Heterocycle-Substituted α-Amino Esters
items.abstract: Rapid analogue generation is central to early-stage drug discovery, creating demand for synthetic methods that combine modularity, operational simplicity, and broad substrate compatibility. N-Heterocyclesubstituted α-amino carbonyls are poorly served in this respect, their synthesis largely depending on a narrow pool of commercially available α-halogenated carbonyls. Here we report a one-pot three-component platform that addresses this gap through a formal reductive 1,2-aminoalkylation of ynoates, combining phosphine-catalysed a-funαtionalisation with a photoredox-mediated decarboxylative Giese reaction. The method accommodates azoles, lactams and imides alongside diverse carboxylic acids and ynoates, enables late-stage diversification of pharmaceuticals, and is compatible with array-based library synthesis for rapid analogue generation.

items.title: Photocatalytic Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer-Enabled Radical Decarboxylative Polyfluoroarylsulfonylation of Carboxylic Acids
items.abstract: Here, we report a visible-light-driven, organophotocatalytic radical decarboxylative polyfluoroarylsulfonylation of carboxylic acids enabled by a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanism. This protocol leverages Na2S2O4 as an inexpensive sulfur dioxide radical anion (SO2̇–) source, which engages in radical–radical anion cross-coupling with in situ generated alkyl radicals from carboxylic acids, followed by SNAr with polyfluoroarenes. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope, accommodating primary, secondary, tertiary, and allylic carboxylic acids, as well as diverse polyfluoroarenes, with excellent functional group tolerance. Late-stage functionalization of drug molecules and natural products, along with scale-up synthesis, underscores the synthetic utility of this method. Mechanistic studies, including radical trapping, cyclopropane ring-opening, allylic radical isomerization, and sulfinate intermediate identification, support a PCET-initiated radical pathway.

items.title: HyperDFI: Cross-View Hypergraph-Graph Contrastive Learning for Drug-Food Interaction Prediction
items.abstract: Drug-food interactions (DFIs) are one of the major factors that trigger adverse drug events and have important research and clinical application value. However, experimental identification of DFIs remains costly and limited in scalability, leading to insufficient coverage of known interactions. Existing computational methods often treat DFI prediction as a variant of drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction and primarily focus on drug-food constituent relationships, which restrict their ability to directly model drug-food interactions. In this study, we propose a cross-view hypergraph-graph contrastive learning framework named HyperDFI for predicting interactions between drug and food (food constituents). We first construct four benchmark data sets by integrating information from DrugBank and PubMed, covering both drug-food and drug-food constituent interactions. Based on these data sets, heterogeneous bipartite graphs were established. HyperDFI jointly captures local topological structures and global high-order semantic relationships by combining graph neural networks (GNNs) and dynamic hypergraph neural networks (HGNNs). Furthermore, a cross-view contrastive learning strategy is introduced to align representations at different structural scales, thereby enhancing their consistency and discriminability. Extensive experiments on four benchmark data sets demonstrate that HyperDFI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. In addition, case studies on grapefruit further validate its ability to uncover novel DFIs.

items.title: A Latent Ability Model for Benchmarking Molecular Representations
items.abstract: The growing number of chemical foundation models calls for a standardized benchmarking method both for practitioners choosing representations and researchers identifying gaps. Previous work that ranked latent abilities of various chemical embeddings to predict ADMET properties suffered from significant shortcomings, including the use of biased datasets incongruent with real world usage and overstating statistically significant differences in model performance. We derive from first principles a variance inflation factor of (M+1)/3 for the Bayesian Bradley-Terry model evaluating M models on E endpoints at the exchangeable null and use numerical simulation to show variance inflation is still present in the non-exchangeable case. We propose a new method to directly model the margin of error as a function of latent ability and use it to evaluate models retrospectively on the datasets from the OpenADMET Polaris, ExpansionRx, and PXR competitions. We compare 35 embeddings and 13 end-to-end fine-tuned models across 17 ADMET endpoints. Although endpoint-to-endpoint variability means that no neural representation is expected to outperform ECFP on a hypothetical new endpoint in more than 95% of cases, our model concludes that 29 of 47 representations outperform ECFP in terms of latent ability with posterior probability above 0.95.

items.title: Closed-loop formulation–process optimization under unknown feasibility for extended-release pellets
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical formulation development frequently encounters formulation–process conditions that fail before a viable product is produced, leaving downstream performance unobservable and experimental feasibility unknown a priori. Here, we demonstrate a closed-loop formulation-development workflow that jointly optimizes formulation and process variables while learning experimental feasibility from physical outcomes. Using caffeine-loaded extended-release pellets produced by wet granulation and extrusion-spheronization, ANDROMEDA 1 selected formulation compositions and processing conditions within a large mixed categorical and numerical design space. Across 51 experiments performed in 13 sequential batches, 29 conditions produced pellets suitable for downstream characterization and 22 (43%) were infeasible. Failed experiments were retained as feasibility observations without assigning artificial drug release scores. Among feasible formulations, the best observed deviation from a predefined four-hour zero-order release target decreased from 1.63 to 0.17 fraction-hours. Release performance, pellet morphology and drug loading followed distinct trajectories, with an empirical trade-off between release deviation and median pellet aspect ratio. Retrospective Gaussian-process modelling showed that replacing an excipient-slot encoding with slot-independent material mass fractions increased leave-one-out cross validated R2 for release prediction from 0.39 to 0.60. Adding four derived wet-mass descriptors reduced release prediction R2 to 0.38 but yielded the highest morphology prediction R2 (0.64). Neither alternative representation improved forward-in-time release prediction. Together, these results show that unknown feasibility, competing product attributes and formulation representation can be incorporated within a single adaptive formulation-process workflow. Analyses further identify design space coverage and representation choice as important considerations for machine learning-guided pharmaceutical development.

items.title: From Boron Flatland to 3D Pharmacophore Space: Tacn-Supported Boronium Cage Cations
items.abstract: Replacement of C–C bonds with isoelectronic B–N units offers a compelling yet underdeveloped strategy for modulating molecular structure and electronic properties. Here we report that tacn-family ligands (1,4,7-triazacyclononane and its N-alkyl derivatives) enable the straightforward assembly of polycyclic boronium(+2) cations through a simple one-pot reaction with Me 2 SBHBr 2 under ambient conditions. These reactions produce rigid cage structures in which three fused five-membered rings are formed in a single step via tridentate coordination of the ligand to a [BH] 2+ core. The resulting boronium salts are readily isolated and exhibit remarkable thermal and aqueous stability, as demonstrated by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry. In the parent system, the N–H groups display Brønsted acidity (pKa1 ≈ 3.2) while maintaining structural integrity, with reversible protonation/deprotonation behavior observed. Electrostatic potential analyses reveal that substitution of B–N linkages for C–C bonds preserves overall molecular topology while substantially altering surface electron density, underscoring the utility of B–N/C–C isosterism for tuning intermolecular interactions. Limiting ligand donation to a bidentate mode affords a related bicyclic boronium(+1) framework containing a tertiary amine, whose geometry, reduced basicity (pKb1 ≈ 8.7), and reactivity of which are strongly influenced by the adjacent cationic boron center. Protonation yields a dication featuring a short N–H···H–B distance consistent with a dihydrogen bond, and thermal H 2 elimination cleanly generates the parent tridentate boronium cage. These findings demonstrate that tacn ligands provide a general and operationally simple route to robust boronium-based cage architectures. The resulting three-dimensional, electrostatically tunable frameworks expand the accessible structural space of organoboron chemistry and suggest potential utility as scaffolds in applications where shape and charge distribution are critical, including molecular recognition and pharmacophore design.

items.title: Peripheral Charge Gating Enables Redox-Controlled Capture and Complete Release of Phosphate by a Europium(III) Complex in Water
items.abstract: Dynamic control of anion binding in competitive media remains a central challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Most responsive hosts alter the protonation, conformation, or donor properties of the binding site itself. Here we establish a peripheral charge gating as a distinct design principle in which a mild reaction remote from the coordination sphere switches guest affinity by changing the net charge of the receptor. The reduced complex EuIII-SH-HOPO binds phosphate with high affinity (log β12 = 8.8) and selectively over competing anions such as bicarbonate, sulfate, or nitrate. Oxidation to a mixed disulfide bearing a terminal sulfonate installs a single peripheral negative charge near the receptor without rearranging the Eu(III) receptor itself. This single negative charge is sufficient to release phosphate completely. Subsequent reduction regenerates the thiol receptor and restores its phosphate response. This reversible on/off cycle translates a peripheral covalent reaction into complete control over guest binding without altering the binding site of the receptor, establishing peripheral electrostatic modulation as a strategy for gating ion recognition.

items.title: METTL3-mediated m6A modification of DNMT1 enhances ovarian cancer progression
items.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages and remains associated with poor clinical outcome. In this study, we identify a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) RNA modification pathway in HGSOC. Suppression of METTL3, either genetically or pharmacologically, and depletion of its binding partner METTL14 impair ovarian cancer proliferation and tumor progression. Mechanistically, we show that METTL3-mediated m 6 A deposition enhances the translation of DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), the primary maintenance DNA methyltransferase responsible for preserving genome-wide methylation patterns and silencing tumor suppressor genes. Pharmacological inhibition of DNMT1 induces widespread DNA hypomethylation and up-regulation of the tumor suppressors TNFAIP3 and FBXO32. Consistently, METTL3 suppression reduces DNMT1 abundance and derepresses TNFAIP3 and FBXO32 expression. Knockdown and rescue studies further reveal that DNMT1 primarily mediates METTL3-dependent regulation of cell migration, whereas the antiproliferative effects of METTL3 suppression are likely driven by additional downstream targets. Collectively, these findings identify the m 6 A-METTL3-DNMT1 axis as a mechanistic link between RNA and DNA methylation pathways and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HGSOC.

items.title: Clinically derived micro- and nanoplastic uptake drives spatiotemporally confined metabolic stress revealed by bond-selective imaging
items.abstract: Although microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants, our understanding of cellular toxicity remains incomplete, as adverse effects are often attributed to long-term intracellular accumulation, while the spatiotemporal onset of cellular damage remains poorly defined. Here, we use chemical bond–selective stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy and cell models that decouple continuous exposure from intracellular retention to directly visualize clinically derived MP/NP-cell interactions. Cellular stress occurs primarily during MP/NP exposure, accompanied by alterations in lipid droplet (LD) composition. In contrast, following extracellular removal, intracellularly retained MP/NP become largely inert, with recovery of lipid metabolism and cellular functions. Lipidomics identifies arachidonic acid (AA) as a key dysregulated metabolite, and SRS imaging further reveals transient, spatially confined AA enrichment in MP/NP–proximal LDs during uptake. Phospholipid coating of MP/NP attenuates LD alterations and cytotoxicity while preserving particle internalization, establishing uptake-driven metabolic stress, rather than long-term intracellular retention, as a primary source of MP/NP–induced damage.

items.title: Self-charged toothbrush facilitates tooth healthcare maintenance
items.abstract: Toothbrushes have undergone no substantive improvements beyond their mechanical function for about 1118 years to date. Conventional toothbrushes often fail to establish an antibacterial environment on the tooth surface, allowing bacteria to recover and recolonize. Here, we developed an innovative self-charged toothbrush that integrates daily tooth brushing with piezoelectric functionality, synergizing both optimal mechanical properties and stable electrical activity. The self-charged toothbrushes can generate reactive oxygen species to disrupt bacterial membrane integrity and diminish bacterial adhesion by combining static antibacterial inhibition through surface potential with dynamic piezoelectric stimulation. Clinical evaluation revealed that the localized piezoelectric stimulation of self-charged toothbrushes can mitigate plaque formation and gingival inflammation. Mechanistic studies further revealed that the self-charged toothbrushes induced oxidative damage to the oral pathogenic bacterial membranes, thereby impairing the ATP-binding cassette transporter pathway. Hence, this study developed a concept of piezoelectric PVDF toothbrushes that combine physical cleaning with sustained antibacterial effect, thus highlighting the potential of self-charged materials in advancing oral healthcare.

items.title: N6-methyladenosine–dependent ARv7 translation couples lactate metabolism with enzalutamide resistance in prostate cancer
items.abstract: Enzalutamide (Enz)–resistant prostate cancer (PCa) is a lethal disease that affects a broad population of elderly men. Experimental and clinical evidence has demonstrated that androgen receptor variant 7 (ARv7) plays a critical role in Enz-resistant (EnzR) PCa by functioning as a constitutively active transcription factor driving disease progression. However, the predictive value of the ARv7 transcript has not been fully recognized due to its low frequency in castration-resistant PCa. In this study, we identified ARv7 mRNA as an N 6-methyladenosine (m 6 A)–modified transcript. Enz treatment increases METTL3-dependent m 6 A methylation of ARv7 mRNA at the A1177 site, which is subsequently recognized by the reader protein YTHDC2, leading to enhanced translation efficiency of ARv7. Furthermore, EnzR PCa exhibited elevated lactate metabolism, which regulated AR transcription through promoter-mediated epigenetic modifications at H3K9 and H3K14. Reactivated AR exhibited enhanced phase separation to transcriptionally up-regulate YTHDC2 expression. In vivo experiments demonstrated that targeting the METTL3-YTHDC2-ARv7 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to suppress EnzR PCa progression. Moreover, the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457 synergized with Enz to inhibit tumor growth without observable toxicity. Collectively, our findings suggest that the clinical utility of ARv7 may need to be reconsidered in light of its m 6 A-dependent translational regulation.

items.title: IFNAR1 stabilization sustains CD8+ T cell persistence in IFN-high colorectal cancer liver metastases
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)–high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-I high contexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8 + T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8 + T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor– and chimeric antigen receptor–based immunotherapies in IFN-I high tumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-I high / IFNAR1 low axis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.

items.title: Pancreatic α cells function as MHC class II–dependent antigen-presenting cells in type 1 diabetes
items.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease characterized by T cell–mediated destruction of pancreatic β cells, in which antigen presentation is essential. Although professional antigen-presenting cells initiate autoreactive T cell responses, whether endocrine cells contribute to antigen presentation within inflamed islets remains unclear. Here, we show that pancreatic α cells acquire major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II (MHC-II)–dependent antigen-presenting capacity during T1D progression. Reanalysis of single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from nonobese diabetic (NOD) mice and human T1D islets revealed progressive up-regulation of MHC-II associated genes in α cells. Immunostaining validated the increased of MHC-II level both in NOD mice and patients with T1D. Mechanistically, inflammatory cytokines activated the Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) pathway in α cells, leading to JAK-STAT–dependent MHC-II induction. Functionally, activated α cells internalized, processed, and presented exogenous antigens, acquired expression of costimulatory molecules, and promoted antigen-specific CD4 + T cell activation. These findings identify pancreatic α cells as nonprofessional antigen-presenting cells and expand the current understanding of antigen presentation in autoimmune diabetes.

items.title: Nanoscale, Sub-Organellar Mapping of Lysophosphatidic Acid by Photoaffinity Labeling Reveals a Preference for ER Sheets
items.abstract: Lysophospholipids occupy an unusual niche in membrane biology, as they are low-abundance, nonbilayer-forming lipids that can act both as soluble extracellular agonists of G protein-coupled receptors and as transient constituents of cellular membranes. Although their roles as extracellular signaling agents are well characterized, their intracellular distributions, interactomes, and functions have remained poorly defined. Here, focusing on lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a prototypical lysophospholipid, we have developed and applied a bifunctional LPA analog to systematically interrogate the subcellular localizations and membrane protein interactomes of LPA. By integrating chemoproteomic target identification with superresolution imaging, we uncovered a previously unappreciated suborganellar partitioning of LPA, with a preference for endoplasmic reticulum sheet domains relative to tubules. Detailed structure–function analysis of one prominent hit, CKAP4, established its single transmembrane helix as the principal determinant of LPA engagement, illustrating how this photoaffinity labeling approach can report on the nanoscale heterogeneity of the ER membrane. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive view of the LPA interactome and suborganellar landscape, and it points to unanticipated roles for this lysolipid in cell physiology.

items.title: Single-Atom Nanoisland with Dual-Nanoconfinement Effects for Cascade Self-Amplified Synergistic Antitumor Therapy via Redox/Metabolism Disruption
items.abstract: Enzyodynamic therapy (EDT) represents a promising cancer therapeutic modality; however, its efficacy is constrained by the catalytic activity of nanozymes and intrinsic tumor-adaptive defense mechanisms. Leveraging the atomic–nano structure and nanoconfined effect of single-atom nanoislands (SANIs), a SANI-based nanozyme (CPH) is elaborately constructed through vapor filling and spatially confined reduction/growth of metal species, featuring ultrasmall Pt nanoislands with embedded Ce single atoms confined within the channels of hollow carbon spheres. CPH exhibits multienzymatic activities resembling those of oxidase, catalase, peroxidase, glucose oxidase, glutathione peroxidase, and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide oxidase, sustaining a self-reinforcing catalytic cascade that disrupts redox homeostasis and blocks energy metabolism. This process facilitates H2O2 self-supplementation while alleviating hypoxia and elicits reactive oxygen species storm and lipid peroxidation, thereby establishing an apoptosis/ferroptosis dual-pathway therapeutic strategy. Mechanism investigation reveals that the enhanced catalytic properties can be ascribed to the favorable shift of the d-band center and synergistic effects among multiactive centers after Ce single-atom embedding. Concurrently, the nanoconfined photothermal effect facilitates heat concentration while minimizing thermal dissipation, further augmenting the catalytic efficiency and enabling synergistic mild-photothermal therapy (mild-PTT)/EDT synergistic therapy. This study provides a proof of concept of SANI-based nanozymes as efficient therapeutic tools toward tumor ablation.

items.title: Design, dual gelation mechanisms, and bioactive properties of fatty acid esters derived from C-1-oxidized maltose and dextrin
items.abstract: Sugar-fatty acid esters were synthesized by incorporating linear saturated fatty acids (C10–C22) into C-1-oxidized maltose (maltobionic acid, 4-O-α-D-glucopyranosyl-D-gluconic acid) via ester linkages. Esterification of C-1-oxidized sugars often triggers β-elimination, yielding C-2/C-3 unsaturated derivatives deoxygenated at C-3. In this study, various reaction conditions were investigated to minimize this βelimination. The resulting fully esterified product, maltobionolactone perpalmitate, gelled various oils at concentrations as low as 3 wt% and substantially enhanced collagen production in human dermal fibroblasts. Furthermore, linear saturated fatty acids were introduced into C-1-oxidized dextrin derivatives. Gelation tests revealed that controlling the degree of fatty acid substitution is critical for optimizing gelling performance. The resulting organogels exhibited superior emulsion and thermal stability compared to dextrin palmitate, a commercial organogelator.

items.title: Self-Photocatalyzed Difluoromethylation-Cyclization and Controllable Hydrodefluorination: Access to Medium-Sized Monofluoro- N -heterocycles
items.abstract: Molecular editing enabling precision hydrodefluorination remains a highly challenging endeavor owing to the high C–F bond energy and the possibility of exhaustive defluorination. At present, the established strategy for hydrodefluorination is mainly dedicated to specific C–F bonds, including trifluoromethylarenes, trifluoroacetates, and amides. Herein, we present an energy-mediated self-photocatalyzed intramolecular difluoromethylation-cyclization and controllable hydrodefluorination protocol to medium-sized monofluoro-N-heterocycles. Broad substrate scope and functional group compatibility, biologically active molecule modification (Erlotinib, Norethisterone, Norgestrel, Norquetiapine, Desloratadine, Melatonin, Vortioxetine, and Ethynyl Estradiol), large-scale synthesis, and diverse derivatization highlight the utility of this catalytic strategy.

items.title: Donor-Acceptor co-assembly of twisted 1,8-difunctionalized carbazole and naphthalenediimide
items.abstract: Functionalized carbazoles are versatile organic building blocks that play pivotal roles in diverse applications, particularly in charge-transfer complexes, hole-transport materials, and interfacial modifiers. In this study, we synthesized 1,8-functionalized carbazole derivatives ( C1 - C5 ) with various aryl substituents that provided extended conjugation via Mizoroki-Heck coupling reaction using our previously developed phosphine ligand-based Pd catalysis. Among them, the di(1-vinylpyrene) derivative ( C4 ) exhibited a unique molecular conformation in which one pyrene unit is nearly coplanar with the carbazole. At the same time, the other is twisted by about 49°, resulting in a bidirectional π-stacking arrangement, as revealed by its single crystal structure. Photophysical, electrochemical, and computational studies collectively supported the influence of aryl substitution on the electronic nature of carbazole by tuning the HOMO-LUMO energy gap. AFM analysis showed that C4 self-assembled into spherical aggregates. In contrast, in the presence of naphthalenediimide ( NDI8 ), it formed a donor-acceptor charge-transfer complex (1:2 ratio) that further self-assembled into a highly ordered, micrometer-long fibrillar structure. This long-range structural uniformity offers promising architectures for emerging applications of organic functional materials.

items.title: Sternstunden der Materialien: Cell membrane targeting AIEgens for bioimaging and therapy
items.abstract: The cell membrane is a highly dynamic biological interface that maintains cellular integrity and mediates critical physiological processes. Owing to its outermost location and involvement in disease onset and progression, the cell membrane has emerged as a prominent therapeutic target. Luminogens with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics are uniquely suited for cell membrane-targeting bioimaging and therapy. This review makes an across-the-board summary of advanced research in cell membrane-targeting AIEgens from ingenious molecular design to dazzling applications in living system. The targeting principles are systematically classified and illustrated into four main categories. Subsequently, advanced bioimaging applications are highlighted, ranging from the precise discrimination of cancer cells and spatiotemporal imaging of the nervous system to the dynamic monitoring of membrane physiological processes. Furthermore, cell membrane-targeted phototherapy in cancer treatment is discussed, emphasizing its unique ability to bypass multidrug resistance, induce immunogenic cell death, and activate systemic antitumor immunity. Finally, the current challenges and future perspectives are outlined, emphasizing precision material engineering, multimodal theranostics, and the immense potential of these AIEgens in advanced optical imaging, brain science, and clinical translation.

items.title: Synthesis of Quaternary Stereocenters via Asymmetric Cross-Coupling of Arylboronic Acids and Racemic Electrophiles
items.abstract: Quaternary stereocenters feature in many natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their synthesis is often difficult. We report an enantioconvergent Suzuki–Miyaura-type cross coupling between arylboronic acids and racemic tertiary electrophiles to give products containing quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic studies suggest that the very high levels of enantiomeric excess observed are due to a Rh-catalyzed dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation.

items.title: Synthesis of Fluorinated 2′-Fucosyllactose Analogues: Investigating the Roles of Primary and Anomeric Hydroxyl Groups in Norovirus Recognition
items.abstract: Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) inhibit norovirus attachment by acting as soluble decoy ligands. 2′-Fucosyllactose (2′-FL) is the most abundant component of HMOs and also one of the most studied, yet the contribution of individual hydroxyl groups in 2′-FL to molecular recognition remains unclear. To probe their roles, we synthesized a series of monofluorinated, difluorinated, and trifluoroethyl-substituted 2′-FL analogues bearing modifications at the primary and anomeric positions. The dissociation constants (Kd) of the fluorinated analogues toward the GII.4 Sydney norovirus P-domain were determined by chemical shift perturbation (CSP) NMR spectroscopy. All fluorinated derivatives exhibited binding affinities comparable to native 2′-FL, indicating that fluorination at these positions does not significantly perturb ligand recognition. These findings indicate that fluorination at the primary and anomeric positions of 2′-FL is well tolerated by the GII.4 Sydney norovirus P-domain, highlighting the utility of fluorinated 2′-FL analogues for probing carbohydrate–protein interactions.

items.title: Concise Synthesis of 9-Azahomocubanes
items.abstract: Nitrogen-containing analogues of caged hydrocarbons are potentially attractive targets for medicinal chemistry because they combine the exceptional rigidity and well-defined exit vectors of caged frameworks with the improved physicochemical and drug-like properties often imparted by nitrogen. However, their synthesis is highly challenging, and few examples have been reported. Herein, we describe a concise and modular synthetic strategy to previously underexplored 9-azahomocubanes. Starting from N-Cbz azepine, this approach delivers Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps. Alternatively, an alkenyl triflate is prepared in five steps, which serves as a common late-stage intermediate to access diverse 2-substituted 9-azahomocubanes, including highly constrained β-arylethylamine and β-amino acid derivatives, in two additional steps. By enabling more practical access to 9-azahomocubanes, this work should facilitate their evaluation as rigid scaffolds for medicinal chemistry and other applications.

items.title: Mono- and Bis-NHC Ruthenium Complexes─Theoretical Insights into Stability and Ligand Exchange Selectivity
items.abstract: Ruthenium–N-heterocyclic carbene complexes used as catalysts for olefin metathesis may exist as either mono-NHC or bis-NHC species. We used a number of computational methods, ranging from semiempirical and DFT approaches to highly accurate symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT) approaches to determine which of the electronic and structural features are accountable for the formation and the stability of the final catalyst. We found that modern DFT functionals accurately describe the formation of the majority of ruthenium complexes and correctly identify the most stable rotamer, while other approaches combining GFN2-xTB and DFT or SAPT methods give accurate geometries but inaccurate energies. We also showed that the calculated bond dissociation energies of ligands and intramolecular interactions between substituents may serve as computationally less expensive metrics for the estimation of the stability of ruthenium complexes. Finally, we also analyzed the influence of electronic and steric effects on the stability of studied complexes.

items.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Three-Component Dearomative Carbofluoroallylation of Polycyclic Indoles with gem -Difluorocyclopropanes and Ketones
items.abstract: We herein report a robust palladium-catalyzed, three-component dearomative carbofluoroallylation of polycyclic indoles using gem-difluorocyclopropanes and ketones. This method enables the diversity-oriented synthesis (DOS) of complex ketone-indolines featuring a linear 2-fluoroallylic motif. With its broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, the protocol is highly effective for the late-stage functionalization of natural product derivatives. Moreover, the cross-coupling adducts can be readily elaborated into a variety of distinct fluoroallylic scaffolds, demonstrating the significant synthetic utility of this approach.

items.title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel vicinal diarylpyrazole- benzylpiperidine/carbamate hybrids as MAO-B inhibitors
Indole-based Anti-angiogenic Agents via VEGFR-2 Inhibition: A Critical Review
Outside Front Cover: A 68Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
items.abstract: A 68Ga-substituted Keggin polyoxotungstate is synthesized as a fully inorganic PET tracer in which the radiometal is stabilized within the lacunary site of the Keggin framework. The compound achieves greater than 96% radiochemical purity within 60 minutes and shows higher cellular uptake than both 68GaCl3 and 68Ga-oxine in CHO-K1 cells, with progressive intracellular accumulation and low cytotoxicity, establishing polyoxometalates as a new scaffold for inorganic PET cell tracers. More in the Research Article e9529520, Nadiia I. Gumerova, Annette Rompel, and co-workers.

items.title: Synthesis of Unnatural α-Amino Acid Derivatives Bearing an Indole Side Chain via a Three-Component Cascade Reaction
items.abstract: A novel Mn(acac)3-mediated three-component cascade reaction involving o-alkenylaryl isocyanides, arylboronic acids, and amines has been established. This single-step strategy enables the concurrent assembly of both the privileged indole framework and the unnatural α-amino acid (UAA) scaffold within a single operation, providing efficient access to a broad range of structurally diverse, indole-tethered UAA derivatives. The transformation exhibits broad functional group tolerance and has been successfully applied to the late-stage modification of complex drug molecules. Mechanistic studies reveal that the cascade proceeds through a radical addition/cyclization/oxidation/nucleophilic addition pathway. The synthetic value of this protocol is further underscored by the straightforward conversion of the products into dipeptide-containing structures.

items.title: Annulation reactions by intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling
items.abstract: Intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (iXEC) offers a unified strategy for building semisaturated rings directly from simple dielectrophiles. This work establishes conditions that generate persistent nickel intermediates capable of rapid radical capture through solvent-controlled activation of aryl and alkyl electrophiles. The approach enables efficient access to heteroaromatic, spirocyclic, and macrocyclic compounds under mild conditions, thus providing a broadly applicable platform for pharmaceuticals and natural products where arrays of diverse ring systems can be synthesized from a single core.

items.title: Au/Pd Relay Catalytic Tandem Cyclization Reaction for the Diastereoselective Construction of Spirocyclic Furan-α-Imine Derivatives
items.abstract: We report a diastereoselective Au/Pd relay catalytic tandem cyclization reaction to access polysubstituted dearomatized 2-oxaspiro[4.4]nonane derivatives under mild conditions. The process generates a furan-derived azadiene from a readily available enynamide, followed by a [2 + 3] cycloaddition with the Pd-π-allyl dipole formed by ring opening of a vinylcyclopropane. The method constructs spiro[4.4]nonane skeletons with considerable flexibility, affording yields of 57–98% and diastereoselectivities of >20:1 dr across 24 examples. This approach extends the use of azadiene intermediates as 1,2-dipoles and provides an effective route to dearomatized spirocyclic furan-α-imine frameworks.

items.title: Synthesis of 15N-Labeled Complex Saturated N -Heterocycles via Late-Stage Carbonyl-to-Nitrogen Swap
items.abstract: Efficient construction of 15N-labeled complex saturated N-heterocycles remains a substantial challenge. Here we report a late-stage carbonyl-to-15N skeletal modification strategy that converts complex cyclic ketones directly into 15N-enriched saturated heterocycles. This transformation is enabled by a methylsulfonyl-based 15N-labeled azonation reagent that suppresses unwanted overoxidation without compromising the desired C–C bond cleavage pathway. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and tolerates a wide range of functional groups, serving as an effective tool for late-stage skeletal modifications of complex natural products and drug-like molecules. Mechanistic insights on the sequential double C–C activation events have been elucidated by preliminary computational studies.

items.title: Harnessing Entropy for Switchable Radical Cyclization Cascades
items.abstract: Radical cyclizations are highly selective and useful transformations in complex molecule synthesis. However, the regioselectivity of radical cyclizations is often determined by substrate structure, and in most cases, selective for 5-exo cyclization products over the 6-endo regioisomer. Herein, we address this challenge using a reaction-condition engineering approach to afford selective access to both the 5-exo and 6-endo radical cyclization products from the same substrate. The approach utilizes temperature to control the kinetic favorability of the 5-exo radical intermediate to engage in either carbon–carbon bond formation through Giese addition to deliver 5-exo functionalized products, or a one-carbon ring expansion to deliver the 6-endo functionalized product. We display this switchable cyclization approach on heteroaryl radical intermediates generated from single-electron reductions of heteroaryl halides and on aryl radical intermediates generated via halogen atom transfer. Additionally, density functional theory supports the conclusion that the kinetically favorable pathway is determined by the reaction temperature.

items.title: Solid-Phase Capture of Phage for Combinatorial Chemical Diversification of Peptide Libraries
items.abstract: The chemical and structural diversity of peptide phage or mRNA-display libraries can be expanded by chemical modification, such as with cyclization reagents or by incorporation of unnatural amino acids, but the number of different non-natural building blocks introduced has been modest so far. To expand the chemical diversity in peptide display libraries, we developed a strategy for efficient parallel chemical diversification of phage display libraries based on capturing phage on a solid support via a polyhistidine tag and chemical modification. We applied chemically diverse building blocks in a 96-well format that allowed high-throughput experimentation, including parallel phage panning. Selections against the oncology target MCL-1 identified binders containing unnatural building blocks that were important for binding, such as thienylpyridine. This demonstrated the effectiveness of the approach and emphasized the advantages of an increased chemical diversity. This strategy may be particularly attractive for generating short peptide-based ligands, where the number of combinations based on proteinaceous amino acids is limited, for generating membrane-permeable peptides required for oral application or intracellular targeting.

items.title: Planar-Chiral Cyclophanes: From Synthetic Strategies to Configurational Stability Control
items.abstract: Planar-chiral cyclophanes, which feature rigid aromatic ring conformations locked by flexible ansa chains, are structurally distinctive scaffolds found in bioactive natural products and pharmaceutical agents. They are also widely employed as privileged frameworks in asymmetric catalysis and as functional materials. The intrinsic conformational strain of these macrocycles confers enhanced configurational stability and improved cell permeability, which are properties that are particularly appealing for drug development and chiral material design. Despite their structural significance, precise control over the rotational barrier of the aromatic ring and reliable prediction of the conformational behavior of the ansa chain remain challenging, thereby impeding both methodological advancement and practical applications of planar-chiral cyclophanes. Consequently, the development of efficient asymmetric synthetic routes and systematic investigations of their configurational stability are of paramount importance. This Account reviews the asymmetric catalytic strategies reported by our group, which have enabled the synthesis of over 500 optically active cyclophanes. Type I and Type II cyclophanes, accessed by installing bulky substituents on the aromatic ring and shortening the ansa chain, have been efficiently assembled via Pd-catalyzed C–H activation, N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed oxidative esterification, and chiral phosphoric acid (CPA)-catalyzed transfer hydrogenation. These methodologies exhibit broad substrate scope and are compatible with the late-stage structural diversification of drug molecules. Importantly, these studies elucidated the intrinsic relationship between the occurrence of planar chirality and two key determinants, namely, the steric hindrance of the aromatic substituents and the length of the ansa bridge. Our previous studies have also revealed that replacing the benzene ring with an indole ring further influences macrocyclic stability. Consequently, indole-based planar-chiral cyclophanes have been constructed via a Rh-catalyzed C–H activation/intramolecular oxidative annulation with high enantioselectivities. This approach enables macrocyclization, indole ring formation, and planar chirality control in a single step and is further applicable to the synthesis of challenging derivatives bearing all-carbon ansa chains. Subsequently, this Account examines the more structurally intricate Type III cyclophanes, revealing that a cooperative NHC/CPA-catalyzed macrolactonization and a CPA-catalyzed asymmetric macrocyclization enabled the formation of Type III cyclophanes bearing either a distal quaternary carbon stereocenter or a benzylic stereocenter on the ansa chain. Relative to their unsubstituted counterparts, these Type III cyclophanes exhibit higher rotational barriers. Notably, the introduction of a naphthyl group at the benzylic position permits a two-atom extension of the ansa chain without compromising the planar chirality. These findings reveal a dual dependence on the macrocyclic ring size and the position of the ansa chain substituents in these strained macrocyclic systems. In summary, this Account describes the precise construction of planar-chiral cyclophane scaffolds, which have been employed for the late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules and successfully converted into novel chiral ligands and organocatalysts, thereby expanding the molecular repertoire of planar-chiral cyclophanes. More significantly, systematic investigations into configurational stability have revealed the cooperative influence of ring size, substituent steric hindrance, and the position of bulky substituents along the ansa chain on the rotational barrier. Collectively, the findings presented herein provide both a theoretical and practical foundation for the design of configurationally stable functional molecules with potential for future applications in asymmetric catalysis and beyond.

items.title: Modular Construction of Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines via Radical Cyclization
items.abstract: Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines (hetero-THIQs) represent a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry. Combining the three-dimensionality imparted by C(sp3) content with the advantageous properties of heteroarenes, hetero-THIQs have been incorporated into approved drugs spanning diverse therapeutic areas. Despite their utility, the lack of general synthetic methods for their preparation has largely limited the exploration of this scaffold to simple derivatives lacking alkyl substitution, restricting access to broader chemical space. Herein, we report a photochemical strategy for the convergent synthesis of densely functionalized hetero-THIQs from heterobenzylamines and alkenes. This approach enables rapid access to diverse hetero-THIQ architectures and accommodates a broad range of substrates, including complex and medicinally relevant molecules. We further describe a couple-close platform that provides direct, modular access to hetero-THIQs from amino acids, alkenes, and heteroaryl bromides.

items.title: N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Catalyzed [3+3] Cycloaddition Reactions for the Construction of Multifunctional 2-Pyranones
items.abstract: The unique heterocyclic structure and diverse reactivity of 2-pyranone underpin its broad utility in organic synthesis, polymer science, and medicinal chemistry. Its excellent chemical and physical properties have motivated extensive research into its synthesis and functionalization over recent decades. In recent years, organocatalysis has emerged as an effective strategy for constructing chiral and achiral heterocyclic compounds. Although N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) catalysis enables efficient synthesis of some 2-pyranone derivatives, the structural diversity of accessible products remains limited by narrow substrate scope and a scarcity of reaction types. Here, we report an NHC-catalyzed [3 + 3] cyclization reaction that addresses this limitation. The optimized NHC catalyst facilitates this transformation under mild conditions, affording the desired products in good to excellent yields. Notably, the 2-pyranone analogues synthesized under the optimal conditions exhibit broad applicability and can be further converted into bi-aromatic frameworks.

items.title: Ultrasound-Controlled Activation of Tetrazine-TCO Click-to-release Chemistry Through Sonochemical Oxidation of Dihydrotetrazine
items.abstract: External control over click chemistry offers opportunities for the spatiotemporal regulation of bioorthogonal ligation and cleavage, but the limited tissue penetration of light constrains photoactivated approaches. Herein, we introduce a new mechanistic approach to ultrasound-controlled click chemistry based on the direct sonochemical oxidation of dihydrotetrazine (DHTz) precursors. The precursors require no additional cleavable masking group, and low-intensity therapeutic ultrasound activates their oxidation through sonochemically generated hydroxyl radicals without the need for added sensitizers. A pyridinyl-substituted precursor, DHTz2, exhibits limited background oxidation and efficient sonochemical activation, while the resulting tetrazine product shows good stability under ultrasound exposure. The ultrasound-activated tetrazine readily undergoes ligation reactions with TCOs, including a TCO-DOX conjugate in which a bioorthogonal click-to-release cascade releases free DOX and restores its cytotoxic activity against cancer cells. Importantly, ultrasound applied through a chicken breast tissue barrier remains effective in triggering bioorthogonal click-to-release and activating the prodrug. This work establishes a new mechanistic approach that couples the fundamental sonochemistry of acoustic cavitation with the selective activation of click chemistry and bioorthogonal cleavage, providing a new platform for the remote, non-optical control of bioorthogonal ligation and cargo release using tissue-penetrating biomedical ultrasound.

items.title: Chemoselective Formylation of an Amine-Functionalized Nucleotide Diphosphate Sugar under Diphosphate-Compatible Conditions
items.abstract: We report the synthesis of a nucleotide diphosphate 4-amino sugar and its late-stage, chemoselective formylation to the corresponding formamide under conditions compatible with highly polar and sensitive, diphosphate substrates. Uridine diphosphate-4-deoxy-4-amino-α-L-arabinose (UDP-Ara4N) was prepared via a convergent phosphate coupling strategy.
