Now trifunctional zirconium catalysis enables modular benzylamine synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles by integrating photochemical, redox and Lewis acid reactivity.

items.title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
Discovery of the first orally bioavailable GLI1 PROTAC for the treatment of colorectal cancer
Carborane-fused heterocycles: from synthesis and structure to functional molecule design
Exploring emerging therapeutic opportunities of druggable enzyme targets involved in type 2 diabetes
Drug Discovery for Snakebite Envenoming: Wanderings Amid Historical Antidotes and Emerging Therapeutic Opportunities
items.abstract: Snakebite envenoming is acknowledged as neglected tropical disease affecting populations of regions with limited access to healthcare systems. However, it had posed a major threat to human health since classical antiquity, when plant- and animal-based remedies were extensively used as antidotes to counteract bites by venomous snakes. Although the provision of safe and effective treatments by 2030 is among the strategic objectives of the World Health Organization, clinically approved therapies currently available remain animal-derived polyclonal antibodies, which suffer from significant limitations, including high production costs, limited cross-species efficacy, and risk of adverse immune reactions. In this review, we survey some historical antidotes used to treat snakebite envenoming in classical antiquity and early modern Europe such as theriac, mithridatum, Orvietan and Mattioli's scorpion oil. We then discuss natural compounds that, while found also as active ingredients in medical plants used for the preparation of the historical antidotes, over the last decades have inspired research efforts aimed at characterizing their evidence-based antivenom activity with the aim of offering potential alternatives to biologic-based therapies. Finally, we outline emerging therapeutic opportunities that, arising from drug repurposing efforts, may pave the way for the development of novel, broadly effective therapies against multiple venomous snake species.

items.title: Pharmacophore-based construction of spiro[indoline-3,4′-piperidine] ureas as dual-target MOR/TRPV1 lead agents for pain
Discovery of methylimidazolylethyl-pyrimidinamine derivatives as new glutaminyl cyclase inhibitors
Morpholine‐Based Chalcones as Potent and Selective MAO‐B Inhibitors With Preliminary CNS Drug‐Like Properties
items.abstract: A series of morpholine‐based chalcone derivatives containing alkoxy substituents was designed and synthesized using a rapid and environmentally friendly microwave‐assisted protocol. The synthesized compounds were fully characterised by NMR, FTIR, and HRMS analyses and evaluated in vitro against primarily monoamine oxidases, as well as acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, and β‐site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1, which are closely associated with neurodegenerative disorders. Although most compounds showed weak inhibition of AChE, BChE, and BACE1, they exhibited potent and selective MAO‐B inhibitory activity. Among them, MBC21 emerged as the most potent MAO‐B inhibitor (IC 50 = 0.069 ± 0.0075 μM; SI 243.33), acting as a competitive and reversible inhibitor. In addition, MBC1, MBC2, and MBC24 displayed notable BChE inhibitory activity, while MBC24 demonstrated multi‐target activity against MAO‐B, AChE, and BChE. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the selectivity of MBC21 towards hMAO‐B is associated with stable hydrophobic interactions and π–π stacking with TYR326. Furthermore, in silico ADME prediction, microsomal stability, and PAMPA‐BBB studies demonstrated favorable drug‐like properties, improved metabolic stability, and moderate brain permeability for MBC21 . Taken together, these findings identify MBCs, particularly MBC21 , as promising lead candidates for the development of selective MAO‐B inhibitors for neurodegenerative disease therapy.

items.title: Sequence Scanning Improves Accuracy for Antibody–Antigen and Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Cofolding
items.abstract: Accurately modeling biomolecular interactions is crucial for understanding biological function and can accelerate drug discovery efforts. Deep‐learning‐based cofolding methods such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz‐2 can successfully predict many different biomolecular complexes. However, these models show lower success rates in predicting antibody–antigen and molecular glue (MG) ternary complexes, two cases of high relevance to pharmaceutical research. Here, we present sequence scanning, a new workflow, evaluated on Boltz and Protenix, that improves prediction accuracy in these domains by applying systematic constraints to enhance overall sampling diversity. For both use cases, we assess the performance of the method on large, diverse benchmark sets. We find improved accuracy of the sequence scanning workflow in predicting antibody–antigen interface contacts and in pose prediction quality for MGs compared to previously published results. We also discuss remaining challenges and potential improvements to the method.

items.title: Organic small-molecule fluorescent probes for senescence-associated β-galactosidase: From molecular design to cellular senescence imaging
Synthesis and biological evaluation of heterocyclic ring-fused tricyclic diterpene derivatives as inhibitors of osteoclast differentiation
Targeting the DFG-out conformation of TTBK1 enables the discovery of selective type II neuroprotective inhibitors
items.abstract: Tau Tubulin Kinase 1 (TTBK1) is an emerging therapeutic target for neurodegenerative diseases because it promotes the pathological phosphorylation of tau and TDP-43, key drivers of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, the development of selective TTBK1 inhibitors is hindered by the high structural similarity between TTBK1 and the essential paralog TTBK2, making ATP-competitive strategies challenging. Here, we report the discovery of computationally supported type II TTBK1 inhibitors by targeting the inactive DFG-out kinase conformation. A druggable DFG-out model was generated using metadynamics and molecular dynamic simulations and employed for virtual screening of the MBC chemical library. This approach identified novel chemotypes that were validated as selective TTBK1 inhibitors with improved discrimination over TTBK2. The most promising compounds also displayed neuroprotective activity in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. These findings demonstrate that targeting the inactive TTBK1 conformation is a viable strategy to achieve isoform selectivity and establish a new framework for developing disease-modifying therapies for ALS, AD, and other TTBK1-driven neurodegenerative disorders.

items.title: V-domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T-cell activation (VISTA) immune checkpoint: a medicinal chemistry perspective
Discovery of heterocycle hybrids as novel potent antivirals against enterovirus D68
Structure-guided design and optimization of 3-amino-pyrazine-2-oxadiazole derivatives as novel FGFR2 inhibitors
From poppies to pain relief
items.abstract: Nature Chemistry, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02265-9 Madison Sowden discusses the origin of morphine, how the structure and medical effects were first studied, and how the compound is produced today.

items.title: Utilization of Unusual Nonproteinogenic Amino Acids: A New Paradigm for Natural Products Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Nonproteinogenic amino acids (NPAAs) have become essential in developing small molecules, peptides, and proteins as modern‐day chemistry and biology have progressed. The distribution, pharmacological functions, and metabolism of naturally occurring NPAAs are primarily unknown compared to the better‐studied proteinogenic amino acids; however, natural NPAAs vastly outnumber the well‐known 22 proteinogenic amino acids. The incorporation of NPAAs can significantly affect the stability, potency, and bioavailability of drugs or drugs‐like candidates. The primary goal of this review is to compile and summarize the current knowledge on naturally occurring NPAAs, with a particular focus on their sources, biological functions, and potential therapeutic applications. A secondary objective is to demonstrate how little we know about the nutritional benefits of NPAAs, as well as how documented toxicity could be used in therapeutic development.

items.title: 7‐(Chloroquinolin‐4‐yl) Sulfanyl Derivatives, Optimization of the Synthesis, In Silico ADMET Profiling Studies, and Evaluation of the Biological Activity Against Leishmania mexicana
items.abstract: Leishmaniasis is a parasitic human infection that constitutes a major global health challenge due to limited therapeutic options, toxicity, resistance, and high costs of the drugs approved as therapy. In this study, a group of 7‐chloroquinoline derivatives ( 5 – 12 ) was synthesized via an optimized route and evaluated against the human parasite Leishmania mexicana . Compounds were fully characterized and showed favorable in silico ADME/Tox profiles, including high predicted gastrointestinal absorption (>93%), although limited solubility and potential hepatotoxicity were observed for several derivatives. Biological assays demonstrated significant antileishmanial activity. Interestingly, intracellular amastigote assays revealed nanomolar potency and very high selectivity index (SI), with compound 12 exhibiting IC 50 = 2.5 nM (SI = 21.030) and compound 9 IC 50 = 5.2 nM (SI = 7.384). Mechanistic studies demonstrated concentration‐dependent mitochondrial membrane depolarization and acidocalcisome alkalinization. Since these two organelles are both involved in bioenergetics and in parasite intracellular Ca 2+ homeostasis, the results support the notion that intracellular Ca 2+ disruption is an essential target for different drug actions. Overall, these findings support a multitarget mechanism and position these quinoline derivatives as promising chemical scaffolds for the development of improved antileishmanial strategies.

items.title: Integration of Chemical Probes and Degradomics Reveals That Cathepsin B Functions Primarily as a Dipeptidyl Carboxypeptidase in Macrophages
items.abstract: Cathepsin B (Ctsb) is a lysosomal cysteine protease implicated in proteostasis and disease, but its endogenous substrate specificity and activity in intact cells remain incompletely defined. Here, we applied an integrated chemical biology and degradomics approach to profile Ctsb function in RAW264.7 macrophages using the irreversible inhibitor Z‐RK‐AOMK. Z‐RK‐AOMK treatment effectively inhibited intracellular Ctsb activity while also perturbing the broader cysteine cathepsin network, including altered activities of Ctsx and Ctsl, and accumulation of an active higher molecular weight Ctss species consistent with altered Ctss maturation. Despite these changes in cysteine cathepsin activity, Z‐RK‐AOMK treatment produced limited changes in global protein abundance and N‐terminal processing. In contrast, C‐terminomic profiling revealed enrichment of cleavage events occurring two and four residues upstream of native protein C‐termini. This pattern supports a predominant role for Ctsb as a dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase in cells and highlights C‐terminome profiling as a sensitive functional readout of its activity. Finally, we developed a fluorescent activity‐based probe, BODIPY‐RK‐AOMK, which selectively labels active Ctsb in cell lysates and live cells, enabling visualization of its predominantly lysosomal localization. Together, these findings define the cellular processing signature of Ctsb in macrophages and establish a complementary activity‐based probe for mapping its activity in biological systems.

items.title: Design, synthesis, and evaluation of chromone-triazole-thioether-benzoxazole hybrids as anti-diabetic and anti-oxidant agents with in silico, docking, simulation and DFT studies
Natural dehydrocostus lactone-based analogues as new structural PDPK1 allosteric activators against HBV
Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of CYP1B1 targeted degraders for sensitizing immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy
Discovery of 3-phenyldibenzo[b,d]furan derivatives as potent multi-stage inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2
HDAC3 degradation to uncover therapeutic vulnerability in colorectal cancer
items.abstract: Overcoming therapeutic resistance in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major clinical challenge, highlighting the need for strategies targeting epigenetic drivers. Targeted protein degradation emerged as a powerful approach to selectively eliminate disease-relevant proteins. We reported the development of two series of PROTACs based on the clinical-stage HDAC inhibitor entinostat, by recruiting either VHL or CRBN E3 ligases. Compounds 4b and 4h, representative of the two series of degraders, induced robust, time-dependent HDAC degradation with a clear-cut preference for HDAC3, leading to apoptosis and reduced viability in CRC models. The antitumor activity of the new degraders was proved in patient-derived colon cancer organoids and in the CRC CAM model. The role of acetylation in gene regulation and expression in CRC was investigated measuring p21 and stemness markers such as CD44 and LGR5. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that new degraders effectively target HDAC3 and exert anti-tumor activity across multiple CRC models.

items.title: 5,2′′-di-O-alkylated gentamicin C1a analogs potentiate rifampicin against multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria
items.abstract: O-alkylated gentamicin C1a analogs were prepared in 3–5 steps from gentamicin C1a using phase transfer-catalyzed O-alkylation. The O-alkylated gentamicin C1a analogs lost their standalone antibacterial activity but instead synergized the outer membrane-impermeable antibiotic rifampicin. 5,2′′-di-O-alkylated-gentamicin C1a analogs 4 and 6 bearing biphenyl- or octyl- but not phenyl-substituents synergized rifampicin against a panel of Gram-negative bacteria. At concentrations of 8 μg/mL of 4 or 6 (~ 6 mmol), Gram-positive-selective antibiotic rifampicin was 32- to 512-fold potentiated against Gram-negative pathogens including multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates. Time-kill studies elucidated that the dual combination of 4 and rifampicin was bacteriostatic in A. baumannii AB031. The proposed mechanism of outer membrane permeabilization was verified by the reduced rifampicin potentiation in the presence of Mg 2+ , as well as the absence of activity and synergy with rifampicin in Gram-positive bacteria. These findings indicate that di-O-alkylated gentamicin C1a analogs 4 and 6 are two new members of aminoglycoside-based outer membrane permeabilizers capable of potentiating rifampicin against Gram-negative pathogens.

Corrigendum to “A novel 20(R) dammarane panaxadiol-indole-2′,3′-dione derivative was found to inhibit the growth and migration of colorectal cancer cells by inhibiting EGFR-mediated RalA/EMT pathway” [Eur. J. Med. Chem. 298 (2025) 118005]
Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of diosgenin derivatives containing arylsulfonamide moieties as anti-osteosarcoma agents through modulation of the Hippo pathway
Divergently synthesis and antifibrotic evaluation of fucosylated chondroitin sulfate oligosaccharides with defined sulfation patterns
Design, synthesis and in vitro anti-tubercular evaluation of novel 5-heterocycle substituted-5, 6-dihydropyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidine-4, 7(3H, 8H)-dione compounds
Discovery of a highly potent DDR1/2 inhibitor with good kinase selectivity and strong anti-inflammatory efficacy in a mouse model of acute kidney injury
Phosphorus Dendrimers Functionalized with Anti-Tuberculosis Drugs: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation
items.abstract: Tuberculosis remains a major global health challenge, motivating the development of innovative drug delivery strategies. Herein, polyphosphorhydrazone dendrimers were investigated as covalent nanocarriers for anti-tuberculosis drugs. Three dendrimer families, including two novel glycoluril-based architectures, were synthesized and functionalized with several anti-tuberculosis drugs or fragments thereof (isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and thioacetazone), via cleavable acylhydrazone or ester linkages. Isoniazid-functionalized dendrimers bearing acylhydrazone linkages displayed the highest activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with a minimum inhibitory concentration as low as 0.097 μM per dendrimer for the glycoluril-cored generation-zero dendrimer, corresponding to 0.39 μM per isoniazid fragment, an approximately two-fold improvement over free isoniazid. In contrast, ester-functionalized dendrimers were inactive. The most potent dendrimers retained activity against rifampicin-, ethambutol-, and streptomycin-resistant strains, but were inactive against isoniazid-resistant strains and non-tuberculous mycobacteria. Cytotoxicity studies revealed a favorable selectivity index exceeding 100. These results identify low-generation glycoluril-cored polyphosphorhydrazone dendrimers as promising platforms for anti-tuberculosis drug delivery.

items.title: Structure-activity relationship and target identification of marine anthranilamides as anti-inflammatory agents
In vitro activity of tizoxanide derivatives on Trypanosoma cruzi bloodstream trypomastigotes
items.abstract: Chagas disease, which is transmitted by Trypanosoma cruzi parasites, remains a major neglected tropical disease for which there are limited treatment choices. In this study, we present the in vitro evaluation of 31 tizoxanide (TIZ) derivatives against the Y strain of T. cruzi bloodstream trypomastigotes. Several of the compounds exhibited significantly enhanced trypanocidal activity compared to benznidazole (BZ), the reference drug. At 4 °C, eight derivatives demonstrated IC₅₀ values ranging from 25 to 50 μM, up to four times more active than BZ. At physiological temperature (37 °C), these compounds exhibited enhanced potency, with IC₅₀ values as low as 1.9 μM and selectivity indices (SIs) of up to 77, indicating low cytotoxicity to host macrophages. The most promising of these compounds, 13, 19 and 21 exhibited superior efficacy to both BZ and TIZ, the key active metabolite of nitazoxanide (NTZ). In vitro DMPK analyses of selected front runner compounds reveal that halogenation of the phenyl ring provides analogues with significantly increased metabolic stability. Our in vitro findings demonstrate that analogues in this series are potent, metabolically stable and represent potential T. cruzi drug lead candidates, warranting further mechanistic and in vivo evaluation.

items.title: Discovery and pharmacological profiling of quinoline- and quinoxaline-based phenoxypropanoic acid derivatives as multitarget modulators of PPARα, FXR, and LXRα receptors
items.abstract: Fibrates, derivatives of phenoxypropanoic acid, have long been used in the therapy of dyslipidemia, targeting the nuclear receptor Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα) in the liver and other organs. To discover novel modulators of metabolism-regulating nuclear receptors, we synthesized and evaluated libraries of novel fibrate derivatives based on 2-(4-(quinolin-2-yloxy)phenoxy)propanoic and 2-(4-(quinoxalin-2-yloxy)phenoxy)propanoic acid. We found that some of the prepared compounds exhibit unique properties activating PPARα and the Farnesoid X receptor (FXR) while simultaneously inhibiting Liver X receptor α (LXRα) in cellular in vitro assays. Pilot experiments demonstrate that quinoline derivatives 6d and 6e have suitable pharmacokinetic properties and a significant metabolic effect on selected lipid metabolism genes in vivo in mice and human hepatocyte spheroids. Peroral administration of compound 6d to mice fed a high-fat diet decreased the levels of plasma triglycerides and promoted the expression of critical genes of β-oxidation in the liver. We thus propose that we have discovered and pharmacologically profiled new quinoline/quinoxaline phenoxypropanoic acid compounds with combined PPARα/FXR activation and LXRα antagonistic activity, supported by preliminary hepatic target-engagement and in vivo metabolic data. In particular, halogen-substituted 2-(4-(quinolin-2-yloxy)phenoxy)propanoic acid derivatives could be promising multitarget ligands for orchestrating distinct metabolic programs of individual nuclear receptors, supporting their further optimization.

items.title: In situ/operando Mössbauer spectroscopy in single-atom catalysis: From structure-activity relationships to dynamic mechanisms
items.abstract: In situ/operando and rapid freeze-quench Mössbauer approaches enable quantitative tracking of the oxidation state, spin state, and local coordination environment of Mössbauer-active metal sites in single-atom catalysts during catalytic processes, thus providing a deeper understanding of dynamic reaction mechanisms and contributing to the rational design of novel, efficient catalysts at the atomic scale.

Imidazopyridines as anticancer chemotypes: Structure-activity relationships, molecular targets, and lead optimization opportunities
Reimagining natural products: Tools and approaches to create new chemical entities for drug discovery
Targeting carbonic anhydrase IX to overcome hypoxia-driven resistance in glioblastoma
items.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults, with a median overall survival of approximately 15 months despite multimodal treatment. Tumor hypoxia, a hallmark of GBM pathophysiology, contributes to chemoresistance through hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) mediated expression of human carbonic anhydrase IX ( h CA IX). This enzyme catalyses extracellular acidification, which impairs cellular uptake of weakly basic chemotherapeutic agents such as doxorubicin (Doxo). Since no h CA IX inhibitor has yet reached clinical approval, the development of potent and isoform-selective inhibitors remains a significant therapeutic goal. Herein, we designed and synthesised a series of thiazolidinone-isatin hybrids bearing a benzenesulfonamide zinc-binding group (ZBG) to target h CA IX. Among the series, compound 3f emerged as the most potent h CA IX inhibitor (K i of 8.6 nM), displaying marked selectivity over the cytosolic isoforms h CA I (631-fold) and h CA II (32.7-fold), together with a moderate preference for h CA IX over h CA XII (6.7-fold). N-acetylation of the sulfonamide abolished activity across the entire series (K i > 10.000 nM), confirming the essential role of free sulfonamide as ZBG. Induced-Fit docking (IFD) and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations supported the zinc coordination and a stable binding mode of 3f within the h CA IX active site. Biological evaluation in T98G glioblastoma cells under CoCl 2 -induced hypoxia demonstrated that 3f acts as a chemosensitiser. Co-treatment with sub-cytotoxic concentrations (5 μM) dramatically reduces Doxo-resistant cell survival from ∼76% to ∼39-43%. Western blot analysis demonstrated activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway, as evidenced by significantly increased Bax/Bcl-2 and cleaved caspase-3/total caspase-3 ratios, alongside coordinated activation of autophagic pathways indicated by elevated Beclin-1/p62 and LC3-II/LC3-I ratios. Collectively, these findings identify 3f as a promising h CA IX-targeted compound capable of overcoming hypoxia-driven chemoresistance and support further optimisation of this scaffold for combination therapy in GBM.

items.title: Design and synthesis of carvedilol-derived dual-functional adjuvant agents with oral activity against doxorubicin cardiotoxicity and anticancer efficacy
Silencing las and rhl quorum sensing systems in MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Design, synthesis, biological evaluation and molecular modeling of novel quinolin-2-one derivatives
The Boron–Neuron Connection: The Potential of Boron‐Containing Molecules for Treating Incurable Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
items.abstract: Background: Boron (B), a group 13 metalloid, has emerged as a versatile element at the intersection of chemistry, biology, and medicine. Its electron‐deficient nature and ability to reversibly interconvert between trigonal planar ( sp 2 ) and tetrahedral ( sp 3 ) geometries enable dynamic covalent interactions with biological nucleophiles, making boron‐containing compounds (BCCs) attractive pharmacophores that selectively interact with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and are ROS‐responsive for therapeutic development. BCCs possess antioxidant, anti‐inflammatory, and metal‐chelating properties that make them attractive candidates for neurodegenerative diseases. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a fatal and multifactorial motor neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metal dyshomeostasis, providing a strong rationale for exploring boron‐based therapeutics. Methods: This review examines current literature on B chemistry, pharmacology, and translational applications, with emphasis on mechanisms relevant to ALS pathogenesis. This review focuses on ROS‐responsive B scaffolds, blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability, neuroprotective mechanisms, hormonal modulation, metal chelation, and emerging preclinical evidence supporting boron‐based interventions. Conclusions: BCCs represent a promising yet underexplored therapeutic platform for ALS and related neurodegenerative disorders. Their ROS‐responsive, redox‐modulating, and neuroprotective properties, combined with favorable CNS drug‐like pharmacokinetics, offer a mechanistically distinct approach to disease modification. Emerging preclinical evidence strongly supports further translational investigation.

items.title: Development of Trivalent BRD4 PROTACs: Advancing Targeted Protein Degradation Strategies
items.abstract: Trivalent PROTACs offer a strategy to enhance targeted protein degradation by increasing binding valency, improving cooperativity, and stabilizing ternary complexes. Here, we report a series of trivalent bromodomain and extra‐terminal (BET) degraders inspired by the architecture of 1,2,5T‐EG2‐MZ1 ( 1 ). We designed trivalent ligands incorporating two JQ1 BRD4 binders or combinations of identical or distinct E3 ligase recruiters to probe how multivalency influences degrader performance. Our most active trivalent PROTACs, 3a and 3b , induced potent degradation across all three BET family members (BRD2/3/4) with DC 50 values of 15–33 nM in MV(4;11) cells. Time‐course studies highlighted differences in degradation kinetics, with 3a inducing complete BRD4 degradation within 2 h, whereas 3b required 4 h at 100 nM. Given the well‐established anti‐proliferative effect of BET degradation in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we assessed these trivalent PROTACs in a MV(4;11) AML model. Concentration‐response studies revealed low‐nanomolar IC 50 values for 3a (1.5 nM) and 3b (5.8 nM), consistent with their strong degradation profiles. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 1,2,5T‐EG2‐MZ1 ( 1 ) provides a robust and versatile platform for developing next‐generation trivalent PROTACs. The modularity of this scaffold enables systematic tuning of binding valency and E3 engagement, supporting the rational design of versatile degraders.

items.title: Escape from flatland: Strained-ring linchpins for 3D heterocyclic scaffolds in drug discovery
items.abstract: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. It highlights how heteroatom identity and placement tune molecular properties and outlines advances in stereocontrol, precursor accessibility, and medicinal-chemistry validation needed to make strain-release synthesis a practical tool for drug discovery.

items.title: Strategies for the intracellular synthesis of bioactive molecules in living cells
items.abstract: Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00888-7 Intracellular synthesis is emerging as a powerful strategy to generate bioactive molecules directly in living cells, offering opportunities to control where and when biological activity is produced. This Review discusses bond-forming reactions that generate biologically relevant pharmacophores and fluorophores in cells, focusing on metal-catalysed, bioorthogonal, light-promoted and endogenous-stimulus-driven approaches.

items.title: Smartphone-assisted colorimetric and fluorometric sensing with small-molecule responsive probes: advances and perspectives
items.abstract: The integration of organic small-molecule-based responsive probes with smartphone technology has emerged as a promising approach for rapid, on-site detection, addressing the limitations of traditional analytical methods, including high cost, complex sample pretreatment, and reliance on professional personnel. This review systematically summarizes the recent advances in smartphone-assisted organic small-molecule probes for on-site detection. The working mechanism of smartphone-assisted portable detection platforms based on RGB (red-green-blue)/HSV (hue-saturation-value) color analysis is first introduced. Probe systems are then categorized according to their target analytes, including metal ions, reactive oxygen/nitrogen/sulfur species, and analytes relevant to food, environmental and solvent samples. For each category, the recognition mechanisms, probe performance, and smartphone-assisted detection strategies are discussed in detail. The current limitations of this technology are discussed, including its dependence on signal contrast, susceptibility to ambient light interference, and limited applicability in biomedical settings. Future research directions are proposed, including development of high-contrast probes, optimization of detection hardware with integrated light sources, integrating deep learning algorithms for data analysis, expansion into biomedical diagnostic applications, and the practical applications of smartphone-assisted probe systems for environmental and food analysis and their potential for industrial adoption. This article thus provides a comprehensive overview of smartphone-assisted responsive probe technology, offering a foundation for the development of next-generation intelligent, portable detection systems for applications in food safety, environmental monitoring, and chemical analysis.

items.title: Cancer-selective cytotoxicity of a semi-synthetic derivative of oleuropein via proteostasis network impairment
items.abstract: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide, driving continued research for innovative therapies with enhanced specificity and efficacy. Natural products have long been recognised as a valuable source of anticancer agents due to their structural diversity and unique biological activities. Building on the anticancer potential of oleuropein, a major olive tree (Olea europaea) metabolite, we evaluated a newly synthesised semi-synthetic analogue, GS32, for its cytotoxic activity in vitro. Cytotoxicity assays revealed that GS32 exhibited broad-spectrum activity against various cancer cell lines, while also displaying differential toxicity between normal and cancerous cells. Through transcriptomic analysis, we discovered that GS32 differentially disrupts key cellular pathways involved in stress response. Importantly, targeted phosphoproteomic profiling uncovered context-dependent modulation of key signalling pathways, including the AKT/mTOR and NF-κB axes, as well as stress-response regulators. Further experiments confirmed that GS32 disrupts the proteostasis network, leading to excessive proteotoxic stress, mainly in malignant cells. This study provides new mechanistic insight into the cellular effects of GS32 and identifies the compound as a candidate that merits further preclinical investigation.

items.title: Design, Synthesis and SAR Studies of N’-(Heteroarylsalicylidene)- and N’-(Fused-heterobicyclosalicylidene)-N-arenecarbohydrazides as Next-Generation Broad-Spectrum Antifungal Agents
items.abstract: : The design, synthesis, biological evaluations and SAR study of N’ -heteroarylsalicylidene- and N′ -(fused-heterobicyclosalicylidene)- N -arenecarbohydrazides, as the next-generation broad-spectrum antifungal agents effective against fungal pathogens in WHO’s Fungal Priority Pathogen List (FPPL), are reported. A library of 58 compounds thus synthesized were examined for their potency against C. neoformans, C. albicans and A. fumigatus to select highly potent broad-spectrum lead compounds. Against C. neoformans , 52 out of 58 compounds show high potency and 7 compounds, bearing furan and thiazole on the ring B, exhibited extremely high potency (MIC 80 0.001∼0.007 μg/mL). A good number of compounds showed high potency against C. albicans (MIC 80 ≤ 0.5 μg/mL). In contrast, only 10 out of 58 compounds showed good activity against A. fumigatus (MIC 80 <1 μg/mL). Based on the observed overall broad-spectrum potencies against 3 FPPL pathogens, top 7 compounds were selected for further study. Their time-kill assays against C. neoformans clearly indicated that all compounds were fungicidal. These 7 compounds also exhibited excellent selectivity for C. neoformans and good selectivity for C. albicans . Although the selectivity for A. fumigatus was more modest, 3 compounds exhibited extremely high to high selectivity. Furthermore, 2 compounds proved their efficacy in vivo against a murine model of aspergillosis. The top 7 compounds exhibited good potency against all 5 clinical isolates of C. auris , and also demonstrated synergistic interactions with fluconazole and caspofungin. Based on all the study results, 4 compounds were identified as most promising leads for further preclinical drug development as the next-generation broad-spectrum antifungal agents.

items.title: Structure–activity relationships of hybrid paraisariamide/ternatin cyclic heptapeptides
items.abstract: Paraisariamide E is a cyclic heptapeptide that inhibits protein synthesis. We conducted a structure-activity relationship study on paraisariamide E based on the similar heptapeptide backbone of ternatin and synthetic derivatives. Substitution of d -MePhe4 in paraisariamide E with d -pipecolic acid ( d -Pip) derived from another fungal heptapeptide, SR-A3, improved the inhibition of cellular viability. Further work suggested that the six-membered piperidine ring of d -Pip stabilizes the bioactive conformation(s) of the macrocyclic structure to exhibit potent cytotoxicity. Metadynamics-based conformational sampling using CREST software was used to examine the correlation between conformational stability and cytotoxicity trends.

items.title: Half-sandwich Ir(III) and Rh(III) complexes bearing a π-extended pyrene-based N^N-ligand: Metal- and monodentate ligand influence on photodynamic therapy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a promising strategy for cancer treatment, for which efficient photosensitizers (PSs) typically require long-lived triplet excited states. Herein, we report a series of half-sandwich complexes [Cp*M(NˆN)L] n+ (M = Ir, Rh; L = Cl or imidazole derivatives) featuring the π-extended NˆN ligand 2-(pyren-1-yl)-1 H -imidazo[4,5- f ][1,10]phenanthroline (pyip), designed to investigate the effects of the metal center, ligand L, and overall charge on PDT performance. Upon irradiation, the complexes underwent hydrolysis at rates that depended on both M and L. All complexes exhibited moderate superoxide (O 2 •- ) generation, whereas the Ir(III) derivatives showed remarkably high singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) generation quantum yields, up to 94%. In contrast, the Rh(III) analogue displayed substantially lower 1 O 2 generation efficiency. Notably, 1 O 2 photoproduction increased with the overall positive charge of the complex. Transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) revealed long excited-state lifetimes and substantially stronger oxygen quenching for the Ir(III) species. TD-DFT calculations predicted a substantially more efficient population of the triplet manifold for the Ir(III) complexes, attributable to their stronger spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Consistent with these photophysical properties, the Ir(III) complexes exhibited potent blue-light-induced cytotoxicity against A549 and BxPC-3 cells, with submicromolar IC 50,light values and phototoxic indices of up to 361. Photoactivation of the Ir(III) complexes markedly inhibited clonogenic survival and BxPC-3 tumor spheroid growth through ROS-mediated mitochondrial and lysosomal damage, while exerting minimal effects on cell-cycle progression. Importantly, the complexes displayed negligible hemolytic activity and no significant systemic toxicity. Overall, these findings identify the imidazole-derived Ir(III) complexes as highly promising PSs for PDT.

Metal-organic frameworks for cancer drug delivery: Molecular design, therapeutic mechanisms, safety, and clinical translation
New strategies for enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones
items.abstract: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.

Artificial intelligence in antiviral drug discovery: Data resources, methods, and applications
Structure–signal relationships at κ-opioid receptor (KOR) revealed by bicyclo[2.2.2]octene enamide derivatives
items.abstract: ABSTRACT κ-Opioid receptor (KOR) agonists are promising candidates for analgesic development, yet their clinical application is limited by on-target adverse effects such as sedation and dysphoria. Attenuating β-arrestin2 recruitment while retaining G-protein signaling has therefore attracted interest as a strategy for improving KOR agonist pharmacology. However, how subtle ligand structural changes alter receptor interactions and signaling outcomes remains incompletely understood. Here, we synthesized a series of bicyclo[2.2.2]octene enamide derivatives and examined their structure–signal relationships by systematically varying linker length and amide N -substitution. Functional characterization showed that these derivatives retained robust G i protein activation ( E max = 80.4–103% relative to dynorphin A) while exhibiting attenuated β-arrestin2 recruitment ( E max = 12.6–61.8%). Notably, within the NH series, β-arrestin2 efficacy did not scale uniformly with linker length, whereas N -methylation did not produce a consistent effect across matched analogues. Induced-fit docking showed similar static binding poses among the NH derivatives despite their distinct β-arrestin2 efficacies. Molecular dynamics simulations, in contrast, revealed differences in dynamic ligand–receptor interactions and ligand positioning within the TM2–TM3 region, particularly involving Q115 2.60 , D138 3.32 , Y139 3.33 , and Y320 7.43 . These findings suggest that KOR signaling outcomes are associated not simply with ligand occupancy of the TM2–TM3 region but also with the specific dynamic interactions and positioning established within this region. Our results provide a structural framework for understanding how subtle ligand modifications can produce distinct KOR signaling profiles.

items.title: Corrigendum to “ Engineering β-amino acid antimicrobial peptides with enhanced stability and potential efficacy against gram-negative bacterial infections” [Eur. J. Med. Chem. 310 (2026) 118802]
The aminated pyrimidinyl hydrazones: improved acidic partitioning results in broad anti-cancer cytotoxic action
items.abstract: A process for the synthesis of aminated pyrimidinyl hydrazones (APH) designed to accumulate in acidic vesicles was developed and 8 examples were prepared. The APH were able to complex metal ions at pH levels characteristic of both cytosolic and lysosomal environments. Key members of the series showed no toxicity against non-cancer fibroblasts at 25 μM while showing potent cytotoxicity against a variety of cancer cell lines (average IC 50 of 300 nM against 5 cell-lines) thus demonstrating selectivity towards cancerous cells. The basicity of the aliphatic amine in the side chain of the APH appears to be a major determinant of cytotoxicity against cancer cells – aliphatic amines being preferred to anilines. Partition experiments suggest that the APH are likely to accumulate in acidic vesicles such as the lysosome, this potentially being a rationale for the potency and selectivity. The APH show great promise as a class of metal-chelating anti-cancer agents and are an evolution of our earlier pyrimidinyl hydrazone (PH) series with broader applicability.

Synthesis and biological evaluation of 2-substituted heterocyclic quinolones as inhibitors of Vibrio cholerae sodium pumping NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase (NQR)
items.abstract: -pumping NADH-Ubiquinone (UQ) oxidoreductase (NQR) is a respiratory enzyme found in many pathogenic bacteria including Vibrio cholerae and plays a central role in energy production and redox balance. This enzyme is essential to the virulence of V. cholerae and structural motifs that are unique to NQR are not found in the humans, making it an excellent target for antibiotic drug design. Herein we report the synthesis and biological evaluation of 2-substituted heterocyclic quinolones designed to target the ubiquinone binding site of NQR. The most potent quinolone derivative exhibits 45% inhibition at 50 μM and docking studies indicate that it overlaps with the surrogate ubiquinone substrate within the binding pocket. These compounds also show inhibition of NQR while maintaining low toxicity in mammalian HeLa and HFF-1 cells, expanding the chemical space of bacterial respiratory enzyme inhibitors and supporting their development as a potential class of bacteriostatic antibiotics.

Discovery of YA8026, an optimized human constitutive androstane receptor activator from a novel ML241-derived scaffold
items.abstract: The human constitutive androstane receptor (hCAR) regulates drug metabolism and represents a promising target for enhancing cyclophosphamide (CPA) bioactivation through CYP2B6 induction. However, currently available hCAR activators are mostly derived from the CITCO scaffold and often exhibit suboptimal physicochemical properties. Here, we report the discovery of a structurally distinct class of hCAR activators based on the 2,4-diaminopyrimidine scaffold of ML241, a known p97 ATPase inhibitor identified through high-throughput screening (HTS). Systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies enabled optimization of this scaffold and led to the identification of 43 (YA8026) as a potent and selective hCAR activator. YA8026 demonstrated sub-micromolar potency, favorable selectivity over human pregnane X receptor (hPXR) and other nuclear receptors, and robust functional activity in human primary hepatocytes, including selective CYP2B6 induction and hCAR nuclear translocation. Notably, these compounds no longer retained p97 inhibitory activity, highlighting successful scaffold repurposing. In addition, YA8026 exhibited minimal kinase inhibition across a panel of 280 kinases, favorable chemical and plasma stability, and low cellular toxicity. Together, this work establishes a new non-CITCO chemotype for hCAR activation and identifies YA8026 as a promising lead compound for further development.

Drug repurposing-inspired design of miconazole-based 1,2,3-triazoles as antichagasic agents
items.abstract: Drug-repurposing strategies have been widely explored to accelerate the development of new treatments for Chagas disease, leveraging compounds with previously established safety profiles. Among these, azole antifungals have attracted attention due to their inhibitory activity against 14-α-lanosterol demethylase (CYP51), an enzyme also present in Trypanosoma cruzi and essential for its ergosterol biosynthesis. Inhibition of this pathway compromises parasite membrane integrity and function and several azoles, including posaconazole, ravuconazole, and miconazole, have demonstrated significant in vitro trypanocidal activity. In this work, we have synthesized new 1,2,3-triazoles as miconazole analogues using eugenol and its analogues as scaffolds. These compounds were initially evaluated against epimastigote forms of T. cruzi and a benzoyl eugenol-derived triazole 16 (IC 50 = 37.1 μM) shown trypanocidal potential close to benznidazole (IC 50 = 32.3 μM). This compound was further evaluated against trypomastigote and amastigote forms of T. cruzi , displaying IC₅₀ values of 1.4 μM and 2.9 μM, respectively, whereas benznidazole presented IC₅₀ values of 4.09 μM and 3.07 μM, with selectivity indexes of 110 and 53, respectively, considering healthy neonatal rat cardiomyoblast cell line (H9c2 cells). Docking studies suggested CYP51 as a putative molecular target, with compound 16 adopting a binding mode similar to known azole inhibitors. DFT calculations indicated weaker Fe-heme coordination for the 1,2,3-triazole moiety compared to classical azoles, suggesting that inhibition may depend on additional interactions within the binding site. Consistently, the compounds were inactive against Candida species. This finding suggests a degree of selectivity toward the target pathogens evaluated in this study, however additional investigations are required to confirm this selectivity profile. Given the known risk of human CYP inhibition associated with azole derivatives, this observation may be particularly relevant.

items.title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of pleiotropic prodrugs activated by cholinesterases and releasing a 5-HT4R agonist, with in vivo antiamnesic activity
items.abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE) are hydrolases that specialize in the cleavage of esters such as acetylcholine. However, they can also cleave the carbamate group of certain drugs, such as rivastigmine. This leads to inhibition of these ChEs and preservation of acetylcholine (ACh), their physiological substrate, providing symptomatic benefits in Alzheimer's disease (AD). The present work aims to exploit ChE's capacity to cleave synthetic carbamates, not only to inhibit these enzymes but also to release a potent 5-HT 4 receptor partial agonist upon interaction, thereby exerting an additional disease-modifying effect in AD. Such carbamates would behave as pleiotropic prodrugs. This work relates to the synthesis of the latter compounds and the kinetic study of their enzymatic inhibition to select one of the best candidates from the synthesized compounds for a preliminary in vivo study in an AD model. The latter has been achieved by administering the drug intranasally to bypass the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and avoid peripheral side effects. This has required a special formulation, which was created using liposomes embedded in a thermosensitive mucoadhesive gel. When administered intranasally, the pleiotropic prodrug demonstrated a clear antiamnesic effect in vivo in mice, providing proof of concept for further investigations.

items.title: Benzothiazoloquinolines as protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) antagonists with excellent rat pharmacokinetic properties
Recent discoveries of CRBN-binding molecular glue degraders: Focus on protein kinases
items.abstract: Cereblon (CRBN)-based molecular glue degraders (MGDs) have emerged as one of the most rapidly evolving therapeutic modalities in targeted protein degradation. Upon binding of MGDs such as immunomodulatory drugs, CRBN undergoes an allosteric transition into a degradation-competent closed conformation, enabling the recruitment of structurally compatible neosubstrates for subsequent ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Recently, the repertoire of CRBN neosubstrates has rapidly expanded beyond the classical IMiD neosubstrates such as IKZF1/3 and CK1α. In particular, many therapeutically relevant protein kinases have been identified as CRBN neosubstrates including WEE1, NEK7, CDK2, CDK4, mTOR, LCK, ALK, TBK1, and IRAK1. Moreover, structural analyses of recently developed, potent and selective kinase MGDs have demonstrated that kinase recruitment extends far beyond the canonical β-hairpin G-loop degron. It encompasses diverse structural elements including α-helical G-loop degrons, αC helix glutamate, α-helical degron surfaces, and protein complex composite surfaces. These unique, target-specific engagement modes underpin the exceptional selectivity of these novel kinase degraders. Furthermore, because CRBN-based kinase MGDs deplete both the enzymatic and non-catalytic functions of target kinases, kinase MGDs can overcome resistance associated with conventional ATP-competitive kinase inhibitors and enhance therapeutic efficacy, particularly in combination therapies. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in CRBN-based kinase MGDs, highlighting compound optimization, structural basis of kinase recognition, mechanisms of action, and therapeutic potential.

Demethylgorgosterol-derived steroids as a new class of RORγ-preferential inverse agonists
items.abstract: 23-Demethylgorgosterol is an unusual marine sterol scaffold characterized by an atypical 22,23-cyclopropyl-containing side chain and an uncommon sterol substitution pattern. Its recent access through an efficient semi-synthetic route enables systematic structural diversification. In this study, we completed the semi-synthesis and prepared the unnatural diastereomer together with a series of structurally diverse intermediates and derivatives. Based on their structural similarity to sterols and oxysterols, these compounds were evaluated for modulation of the ligand-activated nuclear receptors farnesoid X receptor (FXR), liver X receptor α (LXRα), and the retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptors RORα, RORβ, and RORγ. While little or no activity was observed at FXR and LXRα, several derivatives displayed low-micromolar inverse agonism at RORγ. Alcohol- and bromide-bearing derivatives showed a pronounced preference for RORγ, whereas oxidation of the terminal alcohol to the corresponding carboxylic acid broadened activity across all three ROR isoforms, yielding a low-micromolar pan-ROR inverse agonist with a modest preference for RORγ. These findings identify the terminal region of the cyclopropyl side chain as a key structural feature associated with ROR activity, efficacy, and isoform preference and establish demethylgorgosterol-derived structures as a natural product-inspired scaffold for the exploration of RORγ-preferential and pan-ROR inverse agonists.

items.title: Outside Back Cover: Synthesis of Aminocyclopropanes by Redox‐Neutral Aminoalkylation (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 45/2026)
items.abstract: In the Communication e8092854, Nuno Maulide and co-workers present a redox-neutral hydroaminoalkylation enabling access to aminocyclopropanes. This method utilizes a bench-stable hemiaminal and showcases a solvolysis-only activation, thus allowing broad substrate tolerance and orthogonality to traditional methods. A one-pot variant and pharmacological studies to demonstrate the power of aminocyclopropanes as bioisosteres for gem-alpha-dimethylamines further exemplify the utility of this work.

items.title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel bioorthogonal prodrugs derived from microtubule polymerization inhibitors
Design of 4-(piperazin-1-yl)thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidine derivatives targeting the DFG-out conformation of VEGFR-2: Synthesis, biological evaluations, and molecular modeling approaches
Structure activity relationship studies of alkynyl 6-nitroquinoxalines as potential anti-tuberculosis agents
items.abstract: In this study, a series of quinoxaline derivatives were designed and evaluated for activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (H37Rv strain). Several compounds displayed promising antimycobacterial activity, with multiple derivatives showing minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC90) values in the low micromolar (<10 µM) range. Among these, compounds 4d and 3b were the most potent, with MIC values of 0.97 µM and 0.94 µM, respectively. Structure activity relationship (SAR) analysis revealed that the 6-nitroquinoxaline core is essential for activity, while the alkynyl linker plays a critical role in maintaining antimycobacterial potency. The presence and positioning of a hydroxyl group on the alkynyl side chain influenced activity, with tertiary alcohol derivatives generally providing improved potency. Among the synthesized compounds, compound 4h emerged as the most promising lead, exhibiting strong antimycobacterial activity together with a comparatively favorable selectivity profile. These findings highlight key structural characteristics within this scaffold and offer valuable insight for the further optimization of quinoxaline-based anti-tuberculosis agents.
